Announcements
‼~ ( Maximum $5⃣0⃣0⃣allowance!) Recruiting youths (aged 15–24) for online self-help mental health treatment study ~‼ ‼~（最高可獲得$5⃣0⃣0⃣津貼！）誠邀15至24歲青年參加網上自助心理健康療程研究 ~‼ - Department of Psychiatry
From: Winifred Wong
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
winifredtywong@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
香港中文大學精神科學系正進行一項研究，旨在評估手機應用程式網上自助心理健康療程對改善青年睡眠及情緒健康的成效。現招募年齡介乎15歲至24歲青年研究。詳情如下:
我們誠邀符合以下條件的人士參與本次研究：
1. 15歲至24歲青年
2. 有失眠及情緒症狀
3. 過去三個月沒有接受失眠及情緒心理治療或藥物治療
您需要做什麼？
參與為期6週的手機App自助療程
每週觀看20分鐘左右的網上療程
完成四次網上問卷及七天睡眠日記，包括治療前、治療後、三個月跟進及六個月跟進
全部評估及治療皆在電話或網上進行，無需面見！
如有興趣，請即登記並填寫簡單的網上篩查問卷：
https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_domAhEzzCmdV2sK
研究小組將會聯絡適合參與本研究的人士並進一步解釋研究詳情。閣下登記時留下的資料僅供研究用途，絕對保密。如閣下對是項研究有任何查詢，請電郵
winifredtywong@cuhk.edu.hk
或 WhatsApp: (+852- 47544464 黃小姐)查詢。
The Department of Psychiatry at The Chinese University of Hong Kong is conducting a research study to evaluate the effectiveness of an online self-help mobile app program for improving sleep and emotional well-being among youths. We would like to invite participants aged between 15 and 24 to join the study. Details are as follows:
Inclusion criteria:
1. Youths aged between 15-24 years
2. Experience symptoms of insomnia and emotional distress
3. Have not received psychological or medication treatment for these issues in the past 3 months
What will you do?
Join a 6-week self-help treatment via mobile app
Attend 20 minutes of online therapy weekly
Complete four online surveys and seven-day sleep diary: before treatment, after treatment, at 3-month follow-up, and at 6-month follow-up during the study
All assessments and treatments are conducted via phone or online — no in-person visits required!
If you are interested, please register and complete a short screening questionnaire here:
https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_domAhEzzCmdV2sK
The research team will contact eligible participants and further explain the details of the study. Information collected will be only used for research purpose and will be kept strictly confidential. If you have any enquiries, please contact us via email
winifredtywong@cuhk.edu.hk
or WhatsApp: (+852- 47544464 Miss Wong).
View Count

https://cumassmail.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk
For enquiries, please write to:

Announcements
( Receive up to HK$400Allowance!) Recruiting young adults (aged 18–24)for online sleep and mental health intervention with individualized support （最高可獲得$400津貼！）誠邀18至24歲青年參加網上睡眠及心理健康課程，仲有個人化的指導 - Department of Psychiatry
From: Winifred Wong
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
sleepresearch@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
香港中文大學精神科學系正進行一項研究，旨在評估手機應用程式的認知行為治療結合晝夜節律改善大學生的睡眠及情緒。現招募年齡介乎18歲至24歲在學青年研究。詳情如下:
我們誠邀符合以下條件的人士參與本次研究：
1. 18歲至24歲大專生
2. 有失眠症狀及遲睡傾向(凌晨12點後才睡覺)
3.  過去三個月沒有接受失眠及情緒心理治療或藥物治療
您需要做什麼？
∎ 填寫網上評估問卷
∎佩戴睡眠手錶及填寫睡眠日記
∎完成 7 日簡短錄音錄影紀錄當下狀態（每日兩次，每次約１—２分鐘）
∎手機應用程式上的網上治療課程​ ，共6個單元，​每一星期睇一個單元 （15-30分鐘）
∎在完成治療​後的一星期及６個月後，會邀請你再填寫網上評估問卷及和配戴睡眠手錶
如有興趣，請即登記並填寫簡單的網上篩查問卷：
https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_09uYGHApXoC8CDY
研究小組將會聯絡適合參與本研究的人士並進一步解釋研究詳情。閣下登記時留下的資料僅供研究用途，絕對保密。如閣下對是項研究有任何查詢，請電郵
sleepresearch@cuhk.edu.hk
或 WhatsApp: (+852 47544464 吳小姐) 查詢。
The Department of Psychiatry at The Chinese University of Hong Kong is conducting a research study to evaluate the effectiveness of a mobile app-based cognitive behavioral therapy program combined with a circadian rhythm intervention in improving sleep and mental health among college/university students. We would like to invite participants aged between 18 and 24 to join the study. Details are as follows:
Inclusion criteria:
1.  College or university students aged between 18-24 years
2. Reporting symptoms of insomnia and a delayed sleep pattern, typically falling asleep after midnight.
3. Do not receive psychological, behavioural, or pharmacological treatment for insomnia or emotional problems in the past three months.
What will you do?
∎ Complete online questionnaires
∎ Wear the actigraphy watch and keep a sleep diary
∎ Record brief audio and video entries about your current state for 7 consecutive days (twice daily, 1–2 minutes each)
∎ Complete a  6-week intervention program through a mobile app-based  (one module per week,   15–30 minutes per module).
∎ Complete follow-up assessments and wear the actigraphy watch one week and six months after the intervention.
If you are interested, please register and complete a short screening questionnaire here:
https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_09uYGHApXoC8CDY
The research team will contact eligible participants and further explain the details of the study. Information collected will be only used for research purpose and will be kept strictly confidential. If you have any enquiries, please contact us via email
sleepresearch@cuhk.edu.hk
or WhatsApp: (+852 47544464 Miss Ng).

title: (Earn $700!!!) Recruiting adults aged 18–65 who have recovered from depression to participate in a study on depression recurrence (participants on medication are welcome if condition is medically stable) (獲得 $700!!!) 誠邀年齡介乎18歲至65歲的抑鬱症康復者參與預測抑鬱症復發相關的研究(歡迎仍在服藥但病情穩定者參加)
bodyText:

Mass Mail System
Digest of CUHK Mass Mails for Undergraduate Students
»
2026/10/23
»
Announcements
(Earn $700!!!) Recruiting adults aged 18–65 who have recovered from depression to participate in a study on depression recurrence (participants on medication are welcome if condition is medically stable) (獲得 $700!!!) 誠邀年齡介乎18歲至65歲的抑鬱症康復者參與預測抑鬱症復發相關的研究(歡迎仍在服藥但病情穩定者參加) - Department of Psychiatry
From: Phoebe Chan
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
mastersleep@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
香港中文大學精神科學系正進行一項研究，探討運用語音分析能否預測抑鬱症復發。現招募年齡介乎18歲至65歲的抑鬱症康復者參與研究。詳情如下：
我們誠邀符合以下條件的人士參與本次研究：
18歲至65歲的抑鬱症康復者
廣東話為母語
使用智慧型手機並可持續連接互聯網
接受本研究所使用的即時通訊應用程式的服務條款和隱私權政策
您需要做什麼？
接受臨床評估作為篩查
填寫問卷
連續
7
天
於指定的手機應用程式以語音方式記錄情緒狀態
一年後接受跟進臨床評估
完成整個實驗及跟進評估，可以獲得最多HK$700作為研究津貼
如有興趣參與研究，請按以下連結填寫篩選問卷。
https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_e9b0QXbpcuCUxrE
若您適合參與研究，研究人員會聯絡您解釋研究詳情。
閣下留下的資料僅供研究用途，絕對保密。如閣下對是項研究有任何查詢，請電郵
mastersleep@cuhk.edu.hk
或 WhatsApp:(+852- 53202853)。
If you are interested, please complete the following screening questionnaire.
https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_e9b0QXbpcuCUxrE
If you are suitable for participating in the study, the researchers will contact you to explain the study details.
Information collected will be only used for research purposes and will be kept strictly confidential. If you have any enquiries, please contact us via email
mastersleep@cuhk.edu.hk
or WhatsApp: (+852-53202853).
View Count
For request submissions, please submit them at
https://cumassmail.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk
For enquiries, please write to:
http://servicedesk.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk
Copyright © 2013. All Rights Reserved. The Chinese University of Hong Kong.
/weekly/

Announcements
(Earn $200!!) Recruiting teenagers (aged 18 to 24) to participate in depressive disorder study (welcome healthy people) (獲得 $200!!)誠邀18-24歲青少年參加與抑鬱症狀相關的研究(歡迎健康人士) - Department of Psychiatry
From: Phoebe Chan
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
mastersleep@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
香港中文大學精神科學系正進行一項研究，主要探討運用語音分析檢測青少年的憂鬱症狀。現招募年齡介乎18歲至24歲的青少年參與研究，歡迎所有健康人士、抑鬱和焦慮人士參加。詳情如下:
我們誠邀符合以下條件的人士參與本次研究：
18歲至24歲青少年,
除了抑鬱和焦慮外，沒有確診其他精神障礙
能說流利的廣東話
使用智慧型手機（附錄音機）並可持續存取互聯網
接受本研究所使用的即時通訊應用程式的服務條款和隱私權政策
您需要做什麼？
通過篩查訪談後，在手機
連續 7 天
使用指定的訊息應用程式
使用手機上的錄音功能進行數位語音錄音，包括（a）指定的段落閱讀和（b）引導音訊日記。
每天
早上
和
晚上
，在應用程式分別回答4個指導性問題
進行跟進訪談

[23 Oct Anthropology Friday Seminar] Darren Fung, "A Landscape of Enchantment: Visually Impaired People’s Immersion in Bus Fandom in Hong Kong"  - Anthropology
From: M.W.Leung
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
anthropology@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
Dear all,
You are cordially invited to join a talk on 23 October, in which PhD candidate Darren Tsz-Hin Fung will discuss the bus fandom among a network of visually impaired boys and men and explore how the enchantment serves as an antidote to experience of marginalization and fosters their sense of belonging to the city of Hong Kong.
Title: A Landscape of Enchantment: Visually Impaired People’s Immersion in Bus Fandom in Hong Kong
Speaker: Darren Tsz-Hin Fung (Department of Anthropology, CUHK)
Date: Friday 23 October, 2026
Time: 1:00-2:30pm
Mode: In-person
Venue: Room 114, Humanities Building, New Asia College, The Chinese University of Hong Kong
A light lunch will be served at 12:45 pm. First come, first served.
Look forward to seeing you at the Friday Seminar!
Regards,
Department of Anthropology, CUHK
Abstract:
In Hong Kong - a city heavily dependent on public transportation, there is a fan culture revolving around buses. While many non-bus fans are perplexed by and even deride bus fans' enthusiasm for a banal transportation technology, bus fans derive much intellectual and sensory pleasure from taking part in the activities of bus fandom. Drawing on ethnographic fieldwork, this talk explores how a network of visually impaired boys and men immerse themselves in this subculture. I will discuss how they steer each other into learning bus knowledge, evaluate and relish the sensations of bus rides, and participate in the subcultural activity of "bus cruise." I will argue that the enchantment offered by buses serves as an antidote to visually impaired bus fans' experience of marginalization in other social domains and fosters their sense of belonging to the city.
Bio:
Darren Tsz-Hin Fung is a PhD candidate in the Department of Anthropology at The Chinese University of Hong Kong. His research project examines visually impaired people's entanglement with technologies in Hong Kong. His research interests include embodiment, disability, medical anthropology, and Hong Kong studies.

From: 人間佛教研究中心 Centre for the Study of Humanistic Buddhism
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to

【精彩上線｜紀念星雲大師百歲誕辰系列講座】
為紀念星雲大師百歲誕辰，香港中文大學人間佛教研究中心與佛學研究中心聯合舉辦 「人間佛教的文本、行跡與時代開展」 系列講座。我們特別邀請了宗教學、文學、哲學、出版、媒體與博物館學等領域的頂尖專家學者，帶來 9 場重磅專題演講！內容橫跨跨跨文化對話、文學考察、媒體實踐到新博物館學，從多元視角深化對星雲大師思想的理解。本次系列講座全面開放線上參與，歡迎大眾踴躍共霑法益。
題目：
星雲大師歌詞創作的「人間」應用特質
時間：11月19日 | 週四 14:30 - 16:30
講者：林仁昱教授 | 中興大學中文系特聘教授兼藝術中心主任
主持：陳劍鍠教授 | 香港中文大學人間佛教研究中心主任
形式：ZOOM網絡會議
ZOOM ID: 964 5779 7423，密碼: 999999
報名：https://cloud.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk/webform/view.php?id=13741303
演講簡介：
星雲大師在倡議與實踐「人間佛教」的道路上，不僅以歌曲來推廣理念，許多歌曲也成為導引新時代儀節與活動的重要部分。從1950年代作〈西方〉以取代念佛共修的傳統迴向四句偈，作〈佛化婚禮祝歌〉來適應建立「佛化家庭」的重要典儀；1970年代作〈三寶頌〉濃縮歷代各種〈三皈依〉偈讚歌詞要義，更方便傳唱應用；到2000年以後，創作眾多「人間音緣」歌詞，廣徵作曲，使相同歌詞可有不同風格的譜曲，靈活運用於各種弘法與社會活動，充分表現「人間」應用的特質。本次講座將順著時代脈絡，剖析歌詞內涵與實際應用情形，論述其具體意義及影響力。
On his path of advocating and practicing "Humanistic Buddhism," Venerable Master Hsing Yun not only promoted Buddhist concepts through songs, but many of his musical works also became essential components guiding rituals and activities in the modern era.
Historically, this practical approach unfolded across several key stages: In the 1950s, he composed Western Land (〈西方〉) to replace the traditional four-line verse for the dedication of merit during collective chanting cultivation, and penned the Blessing Song for Buddhist Weddings (〈佛化婚禮祝歌〉) to accommodate the pivotal rituals of establishing "Buddhist Families." In the 1970s, he authored the Ode to the Triple Gem (〈三寶頌〉), which condensed the essential meanings of various historical verses praising the Three Refuges into a format more accessible for singing and collective use. From 2000 onward, he created numerous lyrics for Sounds of the Human World (「人間音緣」) and openly solicited musical compositions, allowing the same lyrics to be adapted into diverse musical styles and flexibly utilized in various Dharma propagation and social events. This approach fully exemplifies the characteristics of "humanistic" and practical application.
Following a chronological framework, this lecture will analyze the inner connotations and practical applications of these lyrics, discussing their concrete significance and far-reaching influence.
嘉賓簡介：
林仁昱，中興大學中文系特聘教授兼藝術中心主任，以佛教文學與文化、敦煌文獻與文學、歌謠俗曲與風俗為研究領域，重要著作有：《敦煌佛教歌曲之研究》、《廿世紀初中國俗曲唱述人物》、《敦煌佛教讚歌寫本「原生態」與應用研究》，近期刊登於期刊的單篇著作有：〈星雲大師1950－70年代佛教歌詞創作探究〉、〈星雲大師「人間音緣」歌詞的文學表現及其效應〉、〈《觀音十二圓覺》的菩薩化身與度化對象探究〉、〈觀音與地藏組合供奉的信仰意義與衍發現象〉、〈現代東亞佛誕節文藝與文化考察—以臺灣、日本、馬來西亞為探究核心〉等。

報名：https://cloud.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk/webform/view.php?id=13741299
演講簡介：
本次講座立足於思想史的視野與方法，對太虛在1920年代的世界佛教運動及其文明論述進行詳密的討論與分析。分別從三個方面來開展論述。首先，把太虛的東西文明論放置在1920年代中國思想界有關東西文明與文化論爭這一脈絡中來加以審查，以深入理解太虛相關論述的思想史處境。其次，討論太虛歐美布教中的文明論論述，特別闡釋他是如何「格義」佛教與西方的科學、哲學而另立新說。最後，對太虛佛教世界化的文明論述進行評論，闡析其論述背後複雜的思想面向，特別是他的文明論述中所隱含的東方主義及其民族主義觀念。
Grounded in the perspectives and methodologies of intellectual history, this lecture provides a detailed discussion and analysis of Master Taixu’s World Buddhist Movement and his discourse on civilization during the 1920s.
The presentation unfolds across three primary dimensions:First, it situates Master Taixu’s views on Eastern and Western civilizations within the context of the 1920s Chinese intellectual debates surrounding Eastern versus Western civilization and culture, thereby deepening our understanding of the intellectual milieu of his discourse.
Second, it examines Master Taixu’s civilizational discourse during his missionary travels in Europe and America, specifically elucidating how he utilized Geyi (conceptual matching) to interface Buddhism with Western science and philosophy to forge his innovative theories.
Finally, the lecture reflects critically on Master Taixu’s civilizational discourse regarding the globalization of Buddhism, analyzing the complex intellectual dimensions underlying his arguments—particularly the implicit notions of Orientalism and nationalism embedded within his discourse on civilization.
嘉賓簡介：
龔雋教授，現任中山大學哲學系教授、中華外國哲學史學會東方哲學專業委員會副主任、中國社科院評價研究院宗教專業委員會委員，並擔任《新史學》、《漢語佛學評論》、《人文宗教研究》等多種學術刊物編委。主要從事中國佛教思想的教學與研究，代表性著作包括《作為「知識」的近代佛學史論——在東亞視域內的知識史論述》（商務印書館，2019，合著）、《中國禪學研究入門》（復旦大學出版社，2009，合著）及《禪史鉤沉：以問題為中心的思想史論述》（北京三聯書店，2006）。另於海內外學術刊物發表論文四十餘篇。

From: Kelly Tam
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
medical_alum@med.cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
Don't miss this unique opportunity to gain firsthand insights into humanitarian medical work! Join us for an upcoming Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF) screening of the documentary
Affliction
(《伊波拉戰疫》), followed by a sharing session.   Through the perspectives of local communities, aid workers, and patients, the film captures the unprecedented and devastating Ebola outbreak in West Africa, revealing the human stories behind one of the world’s most challenging public health crises.
Speakers
：
Dr Shannon CHAN
陳詩瓏醫生
(CUHK MBChB 2007)
Profile: As a dedicated surgeon and veteran MSF volunteer who has served in conflict zones such as South Sudan and Yemen, Dr Chan brings profound, first-hand insights into the emotional and physical challenges of wartime healthcare. Honoured with the Hong Kong Red Cross Humanity Award and named one of the Ten Outstanding Young Persons, she shares powerful reflections on finding purpose, coping with extreme adversity, and ensuring that every vulnerable life is valued with dignity.
Mr CHIU Cheuk-pong, Pong
趙卓邦先生
Profile: An experienced emergency room nurse and MSF veteran who has responded to some of the world's most critical public health emergencies—including the Ebola outbreak in Liberia and conflict-driven trauma care in Yemen. Mr Chiu offers compelling perspectives on rapid triage under extreme resource constraints, adapting to frontline crises, and sustaining humanitarian care in high-risk environments.
Event Details:
4 November 2026 (Wednesday)

6:30 pm – 7:00 pm (Registration)
7:00 pm – 8:30 pm (Programme)

Shaw Auditorium, 1/F, Postgraduate Education Centre, Jockey Club School of Public Health and Primary Care, Prince of Wales Hospital, Shatin
Note:
Prior registration is required. Seats are available on a first-come, first-served basis.
Each registrant may attend with up to 3 guests.
We look forward to welcoming you to this inspiring session!
Enquiries: 2959 4223 / events@hongkong.msf.org

Telephone Survey Research Laboratory of Hong Kong Institute of Asia-Pacific Studies will recruit undergraduate student helpers for conducting telephone surveys. The telephone surveys are normally carried out from 6:15 p.m.to 10:15 p.m. (4 hours). The working dates are irregular. The hourly rate for telephone interviewers will be HK64/hr. Those who can conduct telephone interviews by fluent Cantonese is prerequisite. If you are interested in this job, please apply via the online application system by the following link:
https://cloud.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk/webform/view.php?id=13724138
Those who have submitted the online application will be put into the pool of waiting list. We will hold a briefing session for fresh interviewers irregularly and will select the applicants from the waiting list. Those who are selected will be informed by email and are required to attend a briefing session before formal fieldwork.

[CACHS Public Lectures] (1) Beyond Memory: Museums, Heritage and Care in Asia; (2) Archives, Families and the Search for Information: Prison Museums, Memory Politics and Social Repair in Vietnam [CACHS 公開講座] (1) 超越記憶：亞洲的博物館、文化遺產與關懷; (2) 檔案、家庭與資料搜尋：越南監獄博物館、記憶政治與社會修復 - Anthropology
From: M.W.Leung
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
anthropology@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
Dear colleagues and students,
The Center for Archaeology and Cultural Heritage Studies (CACHS) invites you to two public lectures by Graeme Were, Honorary Professor of Anthropology at the University of Bristol and Distinguished Visiting Professor at Minjiang University. The talks explore the role of museums in traditions of care across Asia, and how archives shape family memory and social repair in Vietnam.
1. Beyond Memory: Museums, Heritage and Care in Asia
Speaker: Graeme Were, Honorary Professor of Anthropology, University of Bristol, and Distinguished Visiting Professor, Minjiang University
Date and time: Thursday, 5 November 2026, 4:30–6:15 pm
Venue: CUHK CYT 202 (鄭裕彤樓 202室)
Moderator: Lam Wengcheong, Associate Professor, Dept. Anthropology/Dept. History
Registration:
https://cloud.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk/webform/view.php?id=13744144
2. Archives, Families and the Search for Information: Prison Museums, Memory Politics and Social Repair in Vietnam
Speaker: Graeme Were
Date and time: Tuesday, 10 November 2026, 4:30 pm-6:15pm
Venue: CUHK ELB LT1 (利黃瑤璧樓 LT1室)
Moderator: Cheung Chin Hung Sidney, Professor, Dept. Anthropology
Registration:
https://cloud.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk/webform/view.php?id=13744146
Both talks will be delivered in English and are open to the public. Please register in advance for each talk you wish to attend.
We look forward to seeing you.
Best Regards,
Department of Anthropology

Announcements
Plan Your Next Gathering at Si Yuan Amenities Centre 活動籌備中？思源館助您輕鬆打造理想聚會 - Dean of Students' Office, United College
From: Jackie Chow/ Marco Chan
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
marcohwchan@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
正在籌備活動，想尋找一個環境舒適、氣氛輕鬆的場地嗎？
思源館（SYAC）現正接受場地預訂，歡迎學生組織、中大學系／部門／單位及校友團體租用，舉辦各類型活動，包括聚會、工作坊、分享會、生日派對，以及其他社交或文化活動。
除了提供舒適的活動空間外，思源館亦可按活動需要安排餐飲服務，讓參加者在輕鬆愉快的環境中交流互動，為活動增添更多特色與便利。
有關場地租用收費、餐飲安排及餐單選擇，以及預訂程序等詳情，歡迎瀏覽思源館網站：
https://www.uc.cuhk.edu.hk/si-yuan-amenities-centre-2/
如有任何查詢，歡迎致電 2603 7486 與我們聯絡。
Are you looking for a comfortable and welcoming venue for your upcoming event?
Si Yuan Amenities Centre is open for venue bookings!
Si Yuan Amenities Centre (SYAC) is now open for venue bookings. Student organisations, CUHK departments/units and alumni groups are welcome to make use of the venue for a wide range of activities, including gatherings, workshops, sharing sessions, birthday parties and other social or cultural events.
To make your event even more enjoyable, catering services can also be arranged upon request. With its relaxed atmosphere and flexible facilities, SYAC offers an ideal setting for bringing people together.
For venue rental charges, catering arrangements and menu options, as well as booking details, please visit:
https://www.uc.cuhk.edu.hk/si-yuan-amenities-centre-2/
Should you have any enquiries, please contact us at 2603 7486.

Join us at “Study in Europe Fair” at YIA Today, 23 October!  歐洲升學展今天10 月23 日在YIA 舉行，歡迎參加！ - Office of Academic Links
From: Heidi O
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to

- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -

Join us at “Study in Europe Fair” at YIA Today, 23 October!

The third edition of the
Study in Europe Fair
is today! The event is proudly organised by the European Union Office to Hong Kong and Macao in cooperation with Consulates-General of EU Member States and The Chinese University of Hong Kong. It is a must-attend event for all Hong Kong students interested in pursuing an academic exchange or a degree programme in Europe.
Three highlights of the event:
12 EU countries showcasing a wide range of study and exchange opportunities for undergraduates and postgraduates students from Hong Kong, including scholarships
Discover the EU's flagship Erasmus Mundus Joint Masters programmes and scholarship opportunities
Chat with local alumni and hear about their unique study experiences in Europe!
Registration Link and Event Rundown:
https://www.lyyti.fi/reg/Study_in_Europe_Fair_2026
Event Details:
Date: 23 October
Time: 10:30 am to 6:00 pm (Opening Ceremony begins at 11:00 am)
Venue: G/F, Yasumoto International Academic Park (YIA), The Chinese University of Hong Kong (MTR University Station Exit D)
Event Poster:
Link
We look forward to seeing you there!

第三屆
歐盟升學展
今天 10 月 23 日（星期五）舉行！活動由歐盟駐港澳辦事處、歐盟成員國駐港澳總領事館及香港中文大學合辦。各位有意到歐洲交流或修讀學位課程的同學前往不要錯過是次活動！
活動有三大特色：
12 個歐盟國家將展示多元升學及交流機會，包括獎學金計劃，適合香港的本科及研究生
認識歐盟旗艦碩士計劃 Erasmus Mundus 聯合碩士課程及獎學金機會
與本地學長學姐對話，了解各位喺歐洲留學嘅經驗！

零廢生活新態度

美食當前，識食更要「惜」食
每一口食物、每一滴水，都是地球寶貴的資源 與其說大道理，不如把「零廢」變成日常的生活態度
只需四個日常小習慣，輕鬆為地球減負
拒絕即棄：主動向一次性塑膠說不
隨身補水：攜帶水樽，減少製造膠樽垃圾
拒絕剩食：按量點餐，挑戰零廚餘
環保外賣：自備餐具與食物盒，走塑又安心
Eat Smart, Waste Less

A New Zero-Waste Lifestyle

Good food deserves good habits!
Every bite and every drop counts when it comes to our planet’s resources . Going zero-waste isn't just a buzzword; it's a lifestyle we can easily adopt
Level up your eco-game with these 4 simple daily habits :
Ditch the plastic: Say no to single-use plastics
Hydrate smart: Bring your own bottle and cut down on plastic waste
Clear your plate: Order only what you can finish and say goodbye to food waste
Takeaway upgrade: BYO containers and cutlery for a greener meal to go

We are students from the General Education fyp group of United College, The Chinese University of Hong Kong. We are currently recruiting participants for a questionnaire study on "Situationship" intimate relationships. This research aims to understand Hong Kong university students' and postgraduate students' awareness and views on "Situationship" intimate relationships, and to collect relevant data for academic analysis.
This questionnaire is completely anonymous and takes only 5–8 minutes. Complete the final question and share your views or personal experiences about situationships, and you'll have a chance to receive HKD 20!  If you're willing, please leave your WhatsApp number. The reward will depend on how detailed and useful your response is to our research.
Your responses are extremely important to us. Please scan either of the QR codes below to complete the questionnaire:
我們是香港中文大學聯合書院畢業專題項目的學生，現正招募「情境關係」(Situationship) 親密關係研究問卷的參與者。本研究旨在了解香港大學生及研究生對「情境關係」(Situationship) 親密關係的認識與看法，並收集相關數據作學術分析之用。
本問卷完全匿名，只需 5 至 8 分鐘即可完成，所有填寫問卷最後問題、分享自己對情境關係觀點看法及個人經歷的參與者，均有機會獲得 20 港元作為答謝！如果您願意，請填寫您的 WhatsApp 號碼。我們會根據填寫詳細程度和對研究的有效程度發放獎金。

【
Interprofessional Self Determination theory-based educational interventions on diabetes mellitus
ma
nagement
】
.
It aims to examine the effects and mechanisms of a theory-based educational program on diabetes mellitus management and provide evidence for potential policy changes in the framework for care of diabetes mellitus in primary care settings.

From: Wellness and Counselling Centre, Office of Student Affairs
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
mpss@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
Multicultural Psychological Support Service (MPSS) – English Mental Health First Aid Course for Non-local
students
Dear Students,
To strengthen non-local students' resilience and equip students to cope with life’s challenges, sign up for the 12-hour Mental Health First Aid Standard Course taught by qualified counsellors who are certified MHFA trainers by The Mental Health Association of Hong Kong.
Upon completion of the course, participants will be able to:
Identify the signs and symptoms of common mental health and substance use challenges;
Provide someone with initial support until they are connected with appropriate professional help;
Identify risk factors and warning signs for mental health and addiction concerns; and
Learn strategies to help someone in both crisis and non-crisis situations, and know where to turn for help.
Details:
Language
English
Date
7 & 14 December 2026 (Monday)
Time
09:30 – 16:30
Venue
Room 502, 5/F, Wong Foo Yuan Building (FYB)
Quota
20
Targets
Full-time non-local students at CUHK (including exchange students). *Local students with rich non-local cultural backgrounds (e.g., those who studied at international schools or ethnic minority students born in Hong Kong) are also welcome.
Instructor
Ms. Kimberly Ho (Counsellor from St. John’s Cathedral Counselling Service)
Fee
Free of charge (Deposit of $100, refundable upon attendance)
Application Deadline
16 November 2026 (Monday)
Application Link
https://cloud.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk/webform/view.php?id=13734413

Limited spots – register early!

Places will be allocated on a
first-paid, first-served basis
. After submitting your online registration, please pay the HKD100 deposit as soon as possible during office hours at Room 312, 3/F, Pommerenke Student Centre (Wellness and Counselling Centre).
Enquiries:
Tel: 3943 9951 / 3943 7208 or Email:
mpss@cuhk.edu.hk
/
wacc@cuhk.edu.hk
多元文化心理支援服務
(MPSS) -
英語精神健康急救標準課程（非本地學生適用）





各位同學：
多元文化心理支援服務為增強非本地學生抗壓能力及裝備自己應對生活的挑戰，開辦精神健康急救標準課程，由香港心理衛生會認證的輔導員教授。
完成課程後，你將能夠：
識別常見的心理健康和物質濫用問題的徵兆和症狀；
在受精神困擾的人士獲得專業支援前，提供初步協助；
辨識心理健康和成癮問題的風險因素和警告信號； 及
學習在危機和非危機情況下幫助受精神困擾的人士，以及尋求適切的協助。
詳情如下：
語言
英語
日期
2026年12月7日及14日 (星期一)
時間
09:30 – 16:30
地點
王福元樓5樓502室
名額
20
對象
中大全日制非本地學生（包括交換學生 ）
*本地學生如有豐富的非本地文化背景（如曾就讀國際學校，或在香港出生的少數族裔人士）亦歡迎參加
導師
Ms. Kimberly Ho (聖約翰座堂輔導服務中心輔導員)
費用
全免（$100按金，出席後全數退回）
截止日期
2026 年11月16 日 (星期一)
報名連結
https://cloud.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk/webform/view.php?id=13734413

名額有限，請儘早報名！

*由於工作坊名額將按照付按金的先後次序、以先到先得的原則分配，提交網上報名後，請盡快將$100 按金交到龐萬倫學生中心3樓心理健康及輔導中心 312室，額滿即止。
查詢
致電：3943 9951/3943 7208 或 電郵：
mpss@cuhk.edu.hk
/
wacc@cuhk.edu.hk
View Count
For request submissions, please submit them at
https://cumassmail.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk
For enquiries, please write to:
http://servicedesk.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk

Announcements
Participants Wanted: 12-Week Exercise Training and Heat Tolerance Study &amp;amp;#128227;【運動體適能及耐熱能力研究，12週運動干預】運動體適能改善計劃誠邀18–40歲合資格人士參與 - Department of Sports Science and Physical Education, The Chinese University of Hong Kong; Program Director: Prof. Eric Tsz-chun
From: CHEN Yonghui
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
chenyonghui0601@link.cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
香港中文大學體育運動科學系現正招募健康成年人參與
運動體適能及耐熱能力研究
！
研究目的
：
規律運動有助提升心肺適能及整體健康，但不同運動強度是否能進一步改善人體在高溫環境下的生理調節及耐熱能力，仍有待進一步研究。為探討不同運動訓練方式對
體適能、運動能力及體溫調節能力
的影響，香港中文大學體育運動科學系現正開展一項為期12週的運動體適能改善計劃，並由專業體能教練及研究人員提供運動指導及跟進。
參加條件
：
年齡：
18–40
歲
華人，男女均可
身體質量指數（BMI）：
18.5–25.0 kg/m²
平時較少運動／無規律運動習慣
身體狀況良好，適合進行運動訓練及體能測試
其他健康及安全相關條件將於正式參加研究前進行進一步篩查。
研究內容
：
參加者將接受一系列體適能及生理評估，包括：
身體成分測試
心肺功能測試
肌力測試
日常身體活動及飲食評估
體溫調節能力測試：於受控溫熱環境下進行約30分鐘步行測試
體溫調節測試前後採集血液樣本
符合參加資格人士將會被
隨機分配
至以下其中一組：
高強度間歇運動組
中等強度運動組
低強度步行組
對照組
運動干預為期
12
週
。研究將於干預前及12週後進行評估，並於約
4
個月後進行跟進測試
。
完成研究後可獲
：
運動手錶
價值
HK$200
禮
券
個人研究評估報告，包括肌肉與脂肪含量、運動能力及體溫調節能力等結果
參加方法
：
掃描海報上的二維碼進行網上登記
研究團隊將根據登記資料進行初步篩選
初步符合資格人士將獲聯絡並預約測試時間
前往香港中文大學體育運動科學系進行相關檢查及體適能測試
符合正式參加條件後，將會被隨機分組並開始12週研究計劃
參與地點
：
香港中文大學體育運動科學系
沙田，香港
如您有任何疑問，可透過以下方式聯絡研究團隊
：
陳先生
WhatsApp：5534 4775
電郵：
chenyonghui0601@link.cuhk.edu.hk
[
數據安全聲明
]
所有收集的資料僅供研究用途，並會嚴格保密及以去識別化方式進行研究分析
。
[
歡迎邀請身邊感興趣的親友參加
]
The Department of Sports Science and Physical Education at The Chinese University of Hong Kong is recruiting healthy adults to participate in a research study on physical fitness and heat tolerance.
Study Purpose:
Regular exercise can improve cardiorespiratory fitness and overall health. However, the extent to which different exercise intensities may also improve physiological regulation and tolerance during heat exposure remains unclear.
The Department of Sports Science and Physical Education at The Chinese University of Hong Kong is conducting a
12-week Physical Fitness Improvement Programme
to investigate the effects of different exercise training programmes on
physical fitness, exercise capacity, and thermoregulatory responses
. Exercise guidance and follow-up support will be provided by trained fitness and research staff.
Recruitment Criteria:
Aged between
18 and 40 years
Ethnic Chinese, males and females are both welcome
Body Mass Index (BMI) between
18.5 and 25.0 kg/m²
Currently physically inactive or without a regular exercise habit
Generally healthy and able to participate in exercise training and physical fitness testing
Additional health and safety eligibility criteria will be assessed before formal enrolment.
Study Procedures:
Participants will undergo a series of physical fitness and physiological assessments, including:
Body composition assessment
Cardiorespiratory fitness testing
Muscular strength testing
Physical activity and dietary assessment
Thermoregulatory assessment involving approximately 30 minutes of walking in a controlled warm environment
Blood sampling before and after the thermoregulatory assessment
Eligible participants will be
randomly assigned
to one of the following groups:
High-intensity interval exercise
Moderate-intensity exercise
Low-intensity walking
Control group
The intervention will last for
12 weeks
. Assessments will be conducted before and after the 12-week intervention, followed by an additional assessment approximately
4 months later
.
Upon completion of the study, participants will receive:
A sports watch
An
HK$200 voucher
An individual research assessment report, including information on muscle and fat composition, exercise capacity, and thermoregulatory responses
How to Participate:
Scan the QR code on the poster or register via the following link
The research team will conduct an initial screening based on the registration information
Potentially eligible individuals will be contacted to arrange an assessment
Attend the Department of Sports Science and Physical Education at CUHK for the relevant screening and physical fitness assessments
Eligible participants will be randomly assigned to a study group and begin the 12-week programme
Study Location:
Department of Sports Science and Physical Education
The Chinese University of Hong Kong
Sha Tin, Hong Kong
Contact Us
If you are interested or have any enquiries, please contact:
Mr. Chen
WhatsApp: 5534 4775
Email:
chenyonghui0601@link.cuhk.edu.hk
[Data Safety] All information collected will be used for research purposes only, kept strictly confidential, and analysed using de-identified data.
[You are welcome to invite interested friends or family members to participate.]
View Count
For request submissions, please submit them at
https://cumassmail.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk
For enquiries, please write to:
http://servicedesk.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk

bodyText:

Announcements
[Max. HKD$1200] Recruiting Native Cantonese-speaking Grandparents with hearing loss and Grandchildren for an Interaction Experiment [最高可獲HKD$1200][長者認知及聽力測試報告 + 兒童IQ智商測試報告] 招募聽力損失長者及其孫子女參與互動實驗 - Brain and Mind Institute
From: LEUNG Mei Yee
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
meiyeeleung424@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
我們是
香港中文大學大腦與認知研究所（BMI）
的研究團隊。我們團隊誠摯邀請有聽力損失的長者及其孫子女來參與一項互動研究。
參與者需符合以下條件：
長者：
65歲或以上，存在聽力損失，
無其他已知認知障礙症狀， 且
有意願配戴助聽器
孩童：
6-9歲
，無其他已知發展問題，母語為廣東話
實驗內容：本實驗共分為兩節（每節約1.5至2小時）：
- 第一節：長者將獨自參與一項
認知及聽力檢測
（當日孫子女無需到場）
- 第二節：長者將與孫子女一同進行
簡單遊戲
，期間我們將使用安全且非侵入性的
「近紅外光譜儀」（fNIRS）
進行腦部掃描
- 請注意：參與者必須先完成第一節的實驗，且結果符合研究要求，方會獲邀參與第二節的實驗
完成整個實驗後，您可獲得：
- 長者：一份
認知能力測試報告
+ 一份
純音聽力測試報告
- 孩童：一份
非語言智商測試報告
+ 一份
價值HKD$80的禮物
報酬：
現金HKD$400-1200
，以及免費停車券（如適用）
實驗地點：香港中文大學大腦與認知研究所（位於校園內）
如您對本研究感興趣，請點擊以下連結填寫報名表格：
https://ci.cuhk.edu.hk/surveys/?s=LJEXMFLMR79XA7TX
如祖孫兩位初步符合條件，我們將會儘快與您聯絡！
如有疑問，請發送電郵至 meiyeeleung424@cuhk.edu.hk，
亦可致電或Whatsapp 95867123 查詢。
我們期待你的參與！
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
We are researchers from the
Brain and Mind Institute (BMI) at the Chinese University of Hong Kong
. Our team sincerely invites grandparents with hearing loss and their grandchildren for a social interaction study.
Participants need to be:
- Grandparent:
65+ years old with hearing loss
, with no other diagnosed cognitive impairment, interested in fitting hearing aids
- Grandchild:
6-9 years old
with no other developmental problems; speaking Cantonese as the first language
What is involved? The experiment consists of two sessions (approx. 1.5-2 hours each):
- Session 1: The grandparent will participate alone in a
cognitive and hearing test
. (The grandchild does not need to attend)
- Session 2: The grandparent and grandchild will participate together in some
simple games
while using
fNIRS
(
functional near-infrared spectroscopy
, safe and non-invasive!!!) brain scanning device
- NOTE: Participants must first complete Session 1 and meet the study's requirements to be invited to Session 2
What you'll get (upon completion of the entire study):
- For the grandparent:
A cognitive test report
and
a pure-tone audiometry
(hearing test) report
- For the child:
An non-verbal IQ test report
and
a gift (~HKD$80)
Reward:
HKD$400-1200 allowance
and free parking ticket.
Location: Brain and Mind Institute, The Chinese University of Hong Kong (In campus).
If you are interested in our study, please fill in the form below via the following link:
https://ci.cuhk.edu.hk/surveys/?s=LJEXMFLMR79XA7TX
We will contact you afterwards if the dyad are suitable.
For inquiries, please contact: meiyeeleung424@cuhk.edu.hk,
call or Whatsapp 95867123.
We look forward to your participation!

title: Research Seminar on “Community Engagement as a Public Policy Imperative in Caregiving Research” (Nov 4)
bodyText:

Research Seminar on “Community Engagement as a Public Policy Imperative in Caregiving Research” (Nov 4)  - Department of Social Work
From: Horatio Gong
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
horatiogong@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
The Department of Social Work is delighted to share that the Research Programme for Aging and Disabilities has invited
Prof. Nathan Boucher
, Associate Professor of Public Policy, Nursing, and Medicine at Duke University, to offer a research seminar on “Community Engagement as a Public Policy Imperative in Caregiving Research”. This seminar will be held in hybrid mode (in-person & Zoom).
We warmly invite you to attend the seminar. For details, please find in the attached poster and below:
Time: 4 November 2026 (Wednesday); 2:30 p.m.-4:00 p.m.
Speaker: Prof. Nathan Boucher, Associate Professor of Public Policy, Nursing, and Medicine at Duke University
Venue: Room 520, Chen Kou Bun Building, CUHK (
Google Maps
) & Zoom
Registration: Please register via
this link
or scan the QR code in the poster
About the Seminar: Community engagement is essential to relevant and equitable aging and caregiving research. Dr. Nathan Boucher argues that lived experience should be treated as a form of data and incorporated throughout the research lifecycle. Older adults, family caregivers, clinicians, community organizations, and system leaders can help identify meaningful outcomes, expose structural inequities, and reveal contextual factors that administrative and clinical datasets often miss. Partnership-driven approaches—including interviews, focus groups, advisory councils, listening sessions, and user-centered design—can improve construct validity, feasibility, implementation, and policy translation. Community engagement also reduces research waste by aligning questions and interventions with the priorities of those most affected. Examples from aging, Veterans’ health, homelessness, and the direct care workforce illustrate how engagement can refine research questions, identify unintended consequences, and generate more responsive practices and policies. The presentation concludes that investing in engagement infrastructure is not optional; it is fundamental to producing sustainable, legitimate, and meaningful health systems research.
About the Speaker: Nathan Boucher is an expert in assessing patient and caregiver experiences during serious illness. As a Research Scientist with US Veterans Administration Health Systems Research and Associate Professor at Duke University, he specializes in both qualitative and intervention research at the intersection of social care and healthcare for older populations in need. Dr. Boucher leads projects to support family caregivers and older adults—including those assisting older adults re-entering the community from prison—and develops innovative interventions for families living with dementia and other serious illness. Dr. Boucher’s multidisciplinary perspective bridges clinical practice, health/social policy, and community engagement to drive meaningful advances in health and social supports for older adults.
Should you have any enquiries, please feel free to contact Mr. Horatio Gong at 39431709 or
horatiogong@cuhk.edu.hk
.
Thank you very much.

(Un)Seen | Our Moments with Loneliness 今日一起為孤獨留步 (20 – 30 Oct 2026)  - WACC, OSA
From: Wellness and Counselling Centre, Office of Student Affairs
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
waccactivities@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
(Please scroll down for the Traditional Chinese version.)
(Un)Seen | Our Moments with Loneliness
Presented by the Wellness and Counselling Centre, Office of Student Affairs
Loneliness often goes unnoticed, quietly woven into our daily lives. Through stories, art, and immersive experiences, we warmly invite you to reflect on these unseen emotions and transform them into connections.
Take a moment to slow down, see others, and be seen.
⭐
Exhibition
Through student artworks, personal reflections, psychoeducational content, multimedia, and interactive installations, the exhibition explores the many dimensions of loneliness in university life. By sharing students’ voices and experiences, it seeks to foster greater connection, compassion, and understanding within the University community.
Date:
20 – 30/10/2026
Opening Hours:
Monday to Friday | 10:00 a.m. – 6:00 p.m.
Saturday | 10:00 a.m. – 4:00 p.m.
Closed on Sunday
Venue:
G/F & i-LOUNGE, 3/F, Yasumoto International Academic Park
All CUHK members are welcome.
⭐
Workshop and Talk Series
Explore the complexities of loneliness and discover practical coping strategies through over 15 talks, workshops and interactive drop-in activities under the themes "Shape of Loneliness" and "Dance with Loneliness". Join us in reflecting on different experiences of loneliness while learning ways to foster connection and well-being. Quota is limited, and pre-registration is needed.
Click
here
for workshop details and registration.
⭐
Instagram Photo Challenge
What does loneliness look like through your lens? Join our Instagram Photo Challenge and capture a moment, place, or scene on campus that reflects the theme of loneliness—you might just discover new meanings and something unexpected!
Participating students will have the chance to win exciting prizes, including Kodak Charmera Blind Box Camera, Fujifilm Instax Mini instant cameras, and more!
Follow
sunshineatcuhk_osa_wacc
on Instagram for challenge details and participation details.
Stay connected with us:
Instagram:
sunshineatcuhk_osa_wacc
Website:
https://wacc.osa.cuhk.edu.hk/unseen-our-moments-with-loneliness/
Enquiry: waccactivities@cuhk.edu.hk / 3943 7208
*************************************************
「(Un)Seen | 今日一起為孤獨留步」
學生事務處心理健康及輔導中心呈獻
孤獨常常不被察覺，但卻又悄悄地隱藏在我們的日常之中。透過故事、藝術作品、沉浸式體驗及工作坊等，我們誠邀你一同探索這些未被看見的情緒，並將它們轉化為彼此的連結。
不妨放慢腳步，給自己一些時間及空間——看見他人，也讓自己被看見
。
⭐
展覽
透過學生藝術創作、個人反思、心理健康教育資訊、多媒體展示及互動裝置，展覽帶領參觀著探討大學生活中孤獨的多重面向。藉由分享同學們的聲音與經歷，促進中大社群成員之間的連結、同理心與彼此理解。
日期:
2026年10月20至30日
開放時間 :
星期一至五 | 上午10時至下午6時
星期六 | 上午10時至下午4時
星期日休館
地點 :
康本國際學術園 地下及3樓 i-LOUNGE
歡迎所有中大成員參觀。
⭐
工作坊及講座系列
以「孤獨的形狀」及「與孤獨共舞」為主題，超過 15 場的講座、工作坊及互動活動帶領參加者認識孤獨、探索孤獨的複雜面向，學習實用的應對策略，並從中反思不同的孤獨經驗，建立更有意義的人際連結與身心健康。名額有限，須預先報名。
按
此處
查看活動詳情及報名。
⭐
Instagram大挑戰
在你的鏡頭下，孤獨是什麼模樣？
參加我們的Instagram挑戰吧! 在中大校園裡捕捉屬於你的「孤獨的形狀」、角落或畫面。透過你的獨特視角，也許會發現意想不到的驚喜。
參與同學有機會贏取豐富獎品，包括Kodak Charmera相機盲盒、Fujifilm Instax Mini即影即有相機等。
追蹤Instagram專頁 @
sunshineatcuhk_osa_wacc

- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
香港中文大學體育運動科學系運動營養與體力活動實驗室
誠邀您參加一項運動幹預研究!本研究將有助於瞭解您的運動代謝表現並提高您的代謝健康。
研究題目
：比較不同有氧運動訓練對超重或肥胖絕經後女性代謝及循環血液指標影響的隨機對照試驗
親愛的女士：
您好！
隨着年齡增長與絕經後的荷爾蒙變化，您是否覺得體重逐漸增加、脂肪容易囤積，或者開始擔心體脂、血脂等健康指標？香港中文大學體育運動科學系目前正開展一項研究以了解不同有氧運動訓練對絕經後超重或肥胖女性代謝健康的影響。我們誠邀符合條件的華人女性參與，一起通過科學運動重拾健康！
參與本研究，您將免費獲得：
1. 全面身體成分評估：精準檢測體脂率、肌肉量、內臟脂肪等。
2. 專業血液指標檢測：了解您的血脂、血糖等核心代謝指標。
3. 專家級運動能力測試：精準測量您專屬的運動代謝表現，以評估您的體能與代謝反應。
4. 為期 12 週的免費運動指導：由專業研究人員全程跟進，保障運動安全與效果。

我們在尋找這樣的您：
華人女性，且已自然絕經 12 個月或以上（距離最後一次月經少於 6 年）。
體型偏胖（BMI ≥ 23 kg/m² 或 體脂率 > 30%，以實驗室測試為準）。
平時運動較少（每星期少於 150 分鐘中等強度體能活動、少於 75 分鐘劇烈強度體能活動，或二者同等組合）。
過去 3 個月體重相對穩定，且無嚴重運動禁忌（如嚴重心臟病、中風等）。
⏳
您需要做什麼？（
3
次評估
+ 12
周幹預訓練）
本研究為期 12 週，合格者將隨機分配至對照組、有氧運動組A、有氧運動組B，期間需前往香港中文大學實驗室進行 3 次評估，具體包括：問卷調查、空腹靜脈抽血檢測、指尖採血、身體成分測量、運動代謝測試。為減少測試過程中的不適感，運動代謝測試將與其他健康測試分開進行，整個研究過程中，您總共需要到達實驗室
6
次。

3

Invitation to Participate in CUHK Health Study: Free 12-Week Exercise Guidance and
Comprehensive Health Check!
(Complete the trial and receive a HK$150 shopping voucher)
Department of Sports Science and Physical Education
The Chinese University of Hong Kong
Sports Nutrition and Physical Activity Laboratory
Sender: He Wenke
For any questions, please contact:
wenke.he@link.cuhk.edu.hk
The Department of Sports Science and Physical Education, The Chinese University of Hong Kong,
Sports Nutrition and Physical Activity Laboratory,
sincerely invites you to participate in an exercise intervention study! This study will help us understand your exercise metabolic performance and improve your metabolic health.
Study Title
: A Randomized Controlled Trial Comparing the Effects of Different Aerobic Exercise Training on Metabolic and Circulating Blood Indicators in Postmenopausal Women with overweight or obesity
Dear Madam:
With aging and postmenopausal hormonal changes, do you feel that your weight is gradually increasing, fat is easily accumulated, or you begin to worry about health indicators such as body fat and blood lipids? The Department of Sports Science and Physical Education at The Chinese University of Hong Kong is currently conducting a study to understand the effects of different aerobic exercise training on metabolic health in postmenopausal women with overweight or obesity. We sincerely invite eligible Chinese women to participate and regain health together through scientific exercise!
By participating in this study, you will receive for free:
1. Comprehensive body composition assessment: accurate measurement of body fat percentage, muscle mass, visceral fat, etc.
2. Professional blood indicator testing: understand your core metabolic indicators such as blood lipids and blood glucose.
3. Expert-level exercise capacity test: accurately measure your exercise metabolic performance to evaluate your physical fitness and metabolic response.
4. 12 weeks of free exercise guidance: full follow‑up by professional researchers to ensure exercise safety and effectiveness.
We are looking for:
1. Chinese women who have been naturally postmenopausal for 12 months or more (less than 6 years since the last menstrual period).
2. Are overweight or obese (BMI ≥ 23 kg/m² or body fat percentage > 30%; will be confirmed by laboratory testing).
3. Are usually physically inactive (less than 150 minutes of moderate‑intensity physical activity, less than 75 minutes of vigorous‑intensity physical activity per week, or an equivalent combination).
4. Have had relatively stable body weight in the past 3 months, and have no serious contraindications to exercise (e.g., severe heart disease, stroke, etc.).
⏳ What do you need to do? (3 assessments + 12‑week intervention training)
This study lasts 12 weeks. Eligible participants will be randomly assigned to a
control group
,
aerobic
exercise group A,
or
aerobic exercise group B
. During the period, you will need to visit the laboratory at The Chinese University of Hong Kong for 3 assessments, including: questionnaire surveys, fasting venous blood draw, finger‑prick blood sampling, body composition measurement, and exercise metabolic testing. To reduce discomfort during testing, the exercise metabolic test will be conducted separately from other health tests. Throughout the study, you will need to come to the laboratory
6 times.
12‑week intervention training: 3 times per week, 40‑70 minutes per session, for 12 weeks.
Upon completion of the study, you will receive a HK$150 shopping voucher and a health report.
Trial location: G02 Office, Ground Floor, Kwok Sports Building, The Chinese University of Hong Kong
Register now / Enquire:
Places are limited, first‑come, first‑served! You can click the link below to register:
https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSfZKjSc55Ov13iAjw_GAGkFIbINsXc9rH1ePEYg6CWrU5w5Ew/viewform?usp=header
If you have any questions, please contact the research team:
Study coordinator: Ms. He (WhatsApp: +852 5984 8824)
Supervising professor: Prof. Stephen Heung-sang WONG (Department of Sports Science and Physical Education, The Chinese University of Hong Kong)
Wishing you good health!
Research Team
Department of Sports Science and Physical Education
The Chinese University of Hong Kong
Respectfully

Announcements
[Free of charge] UP TO HKD$1000 ALLOWANCE! Assess the safety, efficacy and tolerability of a CUHK proprietary Chinese medicine formula – A 9-month trial targeting patients with diabetes <6-year disease duration and on two or less oral drugs 津貼高達一千港元!以確認香港中文大學研發的專利中藥配方的安全性、療效及耐受性。招募糖尿病人(六年內確診，飲食控制或服用2種或以下口服糖尿藥)參與為期九個月的研究 - Department of Medicine and Therapeutics
From: Maggie Lee
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
maggielee@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
[
新中藥方劑治療
2
型糖尿病的臨床安全性、有效性和多組評價：對
β
細胞功能和胰島素抵抗的影響】
香港中文大學內科及藥物治療學系與香港中文大學香港中西醫結合醫學研究所現正聯合進行一項為期九個月，以內服中藥(沖劑)治療 2 型糖尿病人
 研究對象：18至80歲華人
沒有重大疾病 (例如:心臟病或中風等重大併發症)
沒有服用中藥
身體質量指數 (BMI) ≥18 kg/m²  (公斤 ÷ 米 ÷ 米)
患糖尿病6 年或以下
目前飲食控制或用2種或以下口服糖尿藥 [例如metformin（品牌藥名：Glucophage）或/及 gliclazide（品牌藥名：Diamicron）]
如不確定自己是否患有糖尿病，但具備以下其中一項風險因素，我們會安排你服用葡萄糖飲料（75 克口服葡萄糖耐量試驗）作篩查
糖尿病家族史 (尤其父母或兄弟姐妹在40歲前診斷 )
代謝綜合症 (3高：高血糖，高血壓，高膽固醇)
超重或肥胖
脂肪肝
多囊卵巢綜合症
妊娠糖尿病病史
研究內容：中西醫評估、心電圖、肝纖維化掃描、抽血檢查、填寫問卷、服用研究中藥或安慰劑等
地點：新界沙田威爾斯醫院，舊座，3 樓，3M 病房 - 糖尿及內分泌研究中心
參與研究費用全免，成功參與者可獲得高達港幣 $1,000 的津貼，名額有限，先到先得！
閣下如對本研究有興趣請透過以下連結報名參加：
https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_1EK8XyC5ac5ykiG
如果初步合適參與研究，負責同事將稍後聯絡你，謝謝
如對研究內容有任何疑問，歡迎致電  3505 3897 / 6937 3365 或 WhatsApp 6937 3365與負責研究人員聯絡、查詢詳情。
[Clinical safety, efficacy and multiomic evaluation of a novel Chinese Medicine formula in Type 2 diabetes: Effects on beta-cell function and insulin resistance
.]
Department of Medicine and Therapeutics and Hong Kong Institute of Integrative Medicine, CUHK are jointly conducting a 9-month clinical study on the use of oral Chinese medicine (granule form) for treating type 2 diabetes.
Eligibility Criteria: Ethnic Chinese individuals aged 18 to 80 years
No major illnesses (e.g., heart disease or stroke)
Not taking Chinese medicine
Body Mass Index (BMI) ≥ 18 kg/m² (kg ÷ metre ÷ metre)
Diagnosed with type 2 diabetes within the past 6 years
Diet control alone or taking no more than 2 oral diabetes medications [e.g., metformin (Glucophage®) and/or gliclazide (Diamicron®)]
Not sure if you have diabetes? If you have any of the following risk factors, we can arrange a 75 g Oral Glucose Tolerance Test (OGTT) for diabetes screening
Family history of diabetes (especially if parents or siblings were diagnosed before age of 40)
Metabolic syndrome (three highs: high blood sugar, high blood pressure, high blood cholesterol)
Overweight or obesity
Fatty liver
Polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS)
History of gestational diabetes

Study Procedures: Chinese and Western medical assessments, Electrocardiogram (ECG), Liver fibrosis scan, Blood tests, Questionnaire completion, Taking either the study Chinese medicine or a placebo
Location: Ward 3M, 3/F, Old Block, Diabetes and Endocrinology Research Centre, Prince of Wales Hospital, Sha Tin, New Territories
Free of charge to participate.
Successful participants may receive an allowance of up to HKD $1,000.
Limited quota – first come, first served!
Register via the following link:
https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_1EK8XyC5ac5ykiG
If you are eligible based on initial assessment, our research team will contact you shortly. Thank you!
For inquiries, please contact:
3505 3897 / 6937 3365
WhatsApp: 6937 3365
View Count

https://cumassmail.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk
For enquiries, please write to:
http://servicedesk.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk

/weekly/

Announcements
Wanted: CU Hunters  - Prof. LIU Xiaonan, Department of Psychology
From: SHI Aike
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
Ak-Shi@link.cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
Hi all,
We are recruiting participants for a study exploring freshmen’s experiences of the CU Hunt activity during this year’s Orientation Camps (O’Camps).
You may be eligible to participate if you are a freshman who:
Participated in the CU Hunt activity during this year’s O’Camps; and
Is affiliated with the following colleges/departments:
United College (UC)
,
New Asia College (NA)
,
Wu Yee Sun College (WYS)
; Department of:
Psychology
,
Chinese Language and Literature
,
Science
, or
Linguistics
.
The study involves a structured interview about your CU Hunt experience. The interview can be conducted either via Zoom or face-to-face, according to your preference.
The session will take approximately 30–60 minutes, and you will receive HK$60 in compensation immediately upon completion.
If you are interested, please fill out the form https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSc0w_AJlnwAtNdfHCq1yq9EgSoXTztnTAf3rSg9c3YaUue6Jg/viewform?usp=dialog to register.
Thank you!

title: HKPFS & Ph.D. in Public Health, CUHK 2027-28 - Application deadline on 1 Dec 2026 歡迎申請2027-28 入學
bodyText:
Mass Mail System
Mass Mail System
Digest of CUHK Mass Mails for Undergraduate Students
»
2026/10/16
»
Announcements
HKPFS & Ph.D. in Public Health, CUHK 2027-28 - Application deadline on 1 Dec 2026  歡迎申請2027-28 入學 - JC School of Public Health and Primary Care
From: MPhil and PhD Programmes in Public Health Enquiry
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
phtraining@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
CUHK PhD in Public Health
香港中文大學
公共衛生哲學博士課程
The Hong Kong PhD Fellowship Scheme (HKPFS) is a government initiative to support outstanding students from around the world (including local HK) to study in Hong Kong. For Intake 2027-28, the academic year starts on 1 August 2027.
We invite excellent students to apply for CUHK PhD programme in Public Health and welcome students to apply for HKPFS. These provide opportunities to study full-time with financial support in Hong Kong.
Please note that both application deadlines are on December 1, 2026.
Our research themes include:
•          Non-communicable disease and aging, and Family Medicine & Primary Healthcare
•          Environmental health and infectious diseases
•          Global health policy, health system & healthcare delivery
•          Mental well-being, social & health behaviours
•          Bioinformatics, machine learning and big data
CUHK HKPFS offers:
- HKPFS stipend at HK$344,400 (approx. US$44,200) per year; Up to HK$1.38 Million (approx. US$176,620)
- Conference and Research-related Travel Allowance is HK$14,400 (approx. US$1,850) per year; Up to HK$87,600 (approx. US$11,230)
- And CUHK Vice-Chancellor HKPFS Scholarship - an award of total HK$80,000 (approx. US$10,260)
- Tuition Fee Waiver - Up to HK$198,0000 (approx. US$25,390)
- Lodging Award - Up to HK$100,000 (approx. US$12,820)
- 1st Year Accommodation Fee Waiver and Guaranteed On-campus Accommodation
Step 1: To submit an initial application to RGC. Application deadline: 1 Dec 2026 at 12:00 noon (GMT+8, Hong Kong Time); and
Step 2: To submit full application to CUHK. Application deadline: 1 Dec 2026 at 11:59pm (GMT+8, Hong Kong Time).
Details of MPhil-PhD programme in Public Health can be found on webpage
https://www.gs.cuhk.edu.hk/admissions/programme/medicine#mphil-phd-in-public-health
or
https://sphpc.cuhk.edu.hk/rpg-programme/
For more info about our School’s Research Themes and list of on-going grants, please refer to webpage
https://sphpc.cuhk.edu.hk/research-themes/
You can find the scholarship information at
https://www.gs.cuhk.edu.hk/admissions/scholarships-fees/scholarships
You may also refer to the "FAQs" Section at
https://www.gs.cuhk.edu.hk/admissions/faqs
for more information.
F
or how to prepare application documents
, please refer to the Graduate School webpage
https://www.gs.cuhk.edu.hk/admissions/admissions/documents-required
and
to press the button “+” to see more on each item.
Would you have friends, classmates or colleagues who might have an interest in pursuing CUHK PhD in Public Health? Would you mind forwarding the message to them please?
FB:
https://www.facebook.com/share/v/1Eua3i6KSq/
IG:
https://www.instagram.com/reel/DeL_LabDVbN/?utm_source=ig_web_copy_link&xtok=MzRlODBiNWFlZA==&srtk=MzRlODBiNWFlZA==
Thank you for your support.
Best regards,
Graduate Division of Public Health
JC School of Public Health and Primary Care
Faculty of Medicine
The Chinese University of Hong Kong
Email:
phtraining@cuhk.edu.hk

www.sphpc.cuhk.edu.hk

We are recruiting participants for a memory experiment involving reading and interactive learning.
During the experiment, you will:
Read expository texts in
English
.
Participate in an interactive learning activity with another participant in
English
.
Complete a final memory test after a
one-day delay
.
The total participation time is approximately
100 minutes.
You will receive an allowance of
HK$100 after completing the final test
.
If you are interested, please complete the registration form below and provide your name, gender, email address, mobile phone number, and major.
Registration form:
https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_3lnpaaCMhKvMjuC

title: 中醫內科診症 – 免診金優惠 | Complimentary Chinese Medicine General Consultation
bodyText:
Mass Mail System
Mass Mail System
Digest of CUHK Mass Mails for Undergraduate Students
»
2026/10/16
»
Announcements
中醫內科診症 – 免診金優惠 | Complimentary Chinese Medicine General Consultation  - School of Chinese Medicine
From: CUHK Chinese Medicine Clinics
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
cuscmclinics@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
香港中文大學中醫學院中西醫結合醫務中心
中大中醫健康月
中醫義診服務
中大中醫診所舉行「中大中醫健康月」活動，以中醫養生理念為基礎，提倡預防保健及慢性病調理，為社區人士提供專業的中醫健康支援。活動內容包括中醫義診服務、巡迴展覽、健康講座及其他推廣活動等。
現誠意邀請香港中文大學同事參加我們的中醫義診服務，享免診金優惠。
無論您是關注日常健康，或正與慢性病同行，都歡迎參與，一同探索中醫智慧，邁向更健康的生活。
中醫義診服務詳情﹕
指定診所﹕
香港中文大學中醫學院中西醫結合醫務中心
地址﹕沙田威爾斯親王醫院舊座4樓4L
活動日期﹕
20/10/2026 – 6/11/2026
合資格對象﹕
新症病人 或 六個月內未曾到中大中醫診所求診之香港中文大學同事
收費﹕
中大同事於優惠期內可享﹕
內科診金﹕全免
診症連針灸﹕$290
藥費﹕$80起/ 每劑
(額外藥費另計﹕內科診症人士必須於中大中醫診所配發藥物，否則須付原額診金)
查詢及預約﹕
2873 3100 / cuscmclinics@cuhk.edu.hk
優惠條款及細則﹕
上述服務必須由香港中文大學中醫學院中西醫結合醫務中心之指定中醫師進行，所有治療服務內容將根據臨床決定。
優惠只適用於首次/ 半年內未有到診所求診之人士。
以上優惠不可與其他優惠同時使用。
上述服務名額有限，先到先得。
香港中文大學中醫診所 (中大中醫診所)* 保留最終決定權。
*香港中文大學中醫診所 (中大中醫診所) 包括﹕
香港中文大學中醫專科診所暨臨床教研中心 (中大校園)
香港中文大學中醫學院中西醫結合醫務中心 (沙田)
香港中文大學 - 上海總會中西醫結合醫務中心 (灣仔)
香港中文大學中醫學院中醫專科診所 (尖沙咀)
Integrative Medical Centre, School of Chinese Medicine, CUHK
CUSCM Wellness Month
Complimentary Chinese Medicine General Consultation
CUSCM clinic is launching the “CUSCM Wellness Month” initiative. Grounded in traditional Chinese medicine wellness principles, the campaign promotes preventive healthcare and chronic disease management, offering professional Chinese medicine health support to the community. Activities include complimentary Chinese medicine consultations, roving exhibitions, health seminars, and other promotional events.
We sincerely invite CUHK staff to participate in our complimentary Chinese medicine general consultation service and enjoy the promotional offers.
Details of Complimentary Chinese Medicine General Consultation:
Designated Clinic﹕
Integrative Medical Centre, School of Chinese Medicine, CUHK
Address﹕4L, 4/F, Old Block, Prince of Wales Hospital
Promotional Period﹕
20/10/2026 – 6/11/2026
Eligible Participant﹕
New Patients or whose have not visited CUSCM clinics within 6 months
Charge﹕
CUHK staff could enjoy the following offers during promotional period﹕
Chinese Medicine General Consultation﹕Free of Charge
Chinese Medicine General Consultation and Acupuncture Treatment﹕$290
Chinese Medication﹕$80 up/ per dose
(Extra or precious Chinese medicines cost are excluded; medication must be dispensed at our clinics, otherwise the participant will need to pay for the original consultation fee)
Inquiry and Appointment﹕
2873 3100 / cuscmclinics@cuhk.edu.hk
Terms and Conditions﹕
The above services will be provided by designated Chinese medicine practitioner of Integrative Medical Centre, School of Chinese Medicine, CUHK.
This promotion offer is applicable to new patients or whose have not visited the clinics within 6 months.
This promotional offer cannot be used in conjunction with other promotional offer and discount offer.
The above services are available in limited quota and will be offered on a first-come, first-served basis.
CUHK Chinese Medicine Clinics (CUSCM Clinics)* reserve the right of final decision.
*CUHK Chinese Medicine Clinics (CUSCM Clinics) includes﹕
The Chinese University of Hong Kong Chinese Medicine Specialty Clinic cum Clinical Teaching and Research Centre (CU Campus)
Integrative Medical Centre, School of Chinese Medicine, CUHK (Shatin)
CUHK – SHFA Integrative Medical Centre (Wan Chai)
Chinese Medicine Specialty Clinic, School of Chinese Medicine, CUHK (Tsim Sha Tsui)

Two courses. A shared project. Zero traditional barriers.
CUHK students from ARCH2222 Digital Media and MAEG3060 Introduction to Robotics teamed up to bring computational designs into the physical world using robotic arms.
Creative decisions influenced the fabrication. Technical realities reshaped the design. Communication wasn't just a learning outcome—it was what made the work possible.
Join us for a closer look at how this cross-disciplinary collaboration between architecture and engineering came to life and what these students pulled off together.

Call for nominations for SCGE Exemplary Teaching Award in General Education 2026  - Office of University General Education
From: Office of University General Education
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
ouge@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
Dear Members of the CUHK Community,
We are pleased to announce that nominations for the Exemplary Teaching Award in General Education 2026 are now open.  This Award is presented annually to recognize teachers for their outstanding contributions to teaching and learning in General Education (GE). Departments, Faculties, Programmes of Study, Colleges, GE teachers, and undergraduate students are welcome to submit nominations.
Nominees should hold a full-time appointment.  All nominations, upon endorsement by heads of the respective units, will be reviewed by SCGE and its Standing Committee, with primary consideration given to evidence of sustained excellence in the nominee’s contributions to GE.  Relevant supporting documentation, including records of the nominee’s contributions to GE during the past two academic years (i.e. 2024-25 and 2025-26 for the current call) should be submitted to facilitate the evaluation.  Contributions to teaching and learning will be evaluated based on the following objectives of the CUHK GE Programme and expectations of GE courses:
Objectives of CUHK GE Programme:
Provide a broad intellectual perspective and to instill an understanding of the values of different academic disciplines;
Develop sensitivity to the common concerns of human existence especially from the perspective of the Chinese culture;
Help students develop their own judgment and sense of values;
Cultivate awareness of the connections among different fields of knowledge; to develop the potentiality for integrating different fields of knowledge as needed; and
Equip students with life-long learning capacities especially through understanding of the connections between academic pursuits and life experience.
Expectations of GE courses:
GE courses should be at the same intellectual level as major courses, and should carry the same workload as major courses with the same number of units.
Upon receipt of a duly completed nomination, the Office of University General Education (OUGE), as the secretariat of SCGE, will contact the nominee concerned directly and invite the nominee to provide his/her teaching philosophy, course and assessment materials, Course and Teaching Evaluation (CTE) reports, and any other relevant supporting documents and materials in the past two academic years, i.e. 2024-25 and 2025-26 for the current call.
More information about the Award can be found on the website of the Office of University General Education:
https://www.cuhk.edu.hk/oge/eta
.  Nominations should be made through the
online nomination form
by 16 November 2026.
For any inquiries, feel free to contact us at
ouge@cuhk.edu.hk
or call us at 3943 7075.
Thank you for helping us recognize the exceptional educators who contribute to our community.
Best regards,
Office of University General Education

Dear Students,
Co-op@CUHK Field Trip to Beijing (19 - 24 Dec 2026)
Have you ever wondered what it is like to experience China's dynamic business environment and technological innovation first-hand? This winter, Co-op@CUHK invites you to join an exciting six-day field trip to Beijing and explore one of the world's most vibrant economic and cultural centres!
Organised by the
Office of Co-operative Education Programme (OCEP)
, the Co-op@CUHK Field Trip to Beijing will take place from 19 to 24 December 2026. Through visits to leading enterprises, renowned universities, and iconic cultural landmarks, participants will gain a deeper understanding of China's economic development, technological advancement, and rich cultural heritage. The field trip is designed to broaden students' perspectives, enhance their global awareness, and provide valuable insights into emerging industries and career opportunities.
This credit-bearing field trip is associated with COOP1001 Field Trip to China, and participating students will be enrolled in the course in Term 2, 2026-27. Upon successful completion of the field trip and fulfilment of course requirements, students will earn 1 unit.
Please refer to the attached poster for field trip details, itinerary highlights, and package information.
Registrants will be notified of the application result in late November 2026.
All
successful applicants will be required to attend a mandatory pre-trip briefing session, tentatively scheduled for early December 2026.
Please note that the package fee does not include visa application fees. Students who require a visa are responsible for arranging their own visa applications. Payment details will be provided in the confirmation email.
If you are interested in joining this unique learning journey, please register [
here

title: If You Want to Make a Change on Campus, This Is for You. 給想為校園帶來改變的你
bodyText:
Mass Mail System
Mass Mail System
Digest of CUHK Mass Mails for Undergraduate Students
»
2026/10/16
»
Announcements
If You Want to Make a Change on Campus, This Is for You. 給想為校園帶來改變的你 - Department of Psychology
From: Czarina Tong
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
puikiutong@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
你好！
如果你希望為支援校園精神健康出一份力，或者對現時校園精神健康制度感到困惑或無力，我們誠邀你參與這次精神健康倡議者培訓。你將與其他志同道合的夥伴，一起重新思考校園內習以為常的觀念和模式，探索大專校園內不同持份者如何共建更友善、安全、重視精神健康的校園環境。
培訓內容
在課程中，我們一起從基礎概念開始學習和同行：
甚麼是精神健康倡議
青年主導的社會影響力與如何實現可持續的倡議
策劃和實踐倡議行動的實用技巧
在實習中，我們會一起：
創作推動校園精神健康的公眾教育素材
﻿﻿將所學的概念與技巧結合親身經歷及專長，應用到共同創作中
在合作過程中練習並實踐健康且有效的溝通與合作方式
活動詳情：
課堂： 12/12/2026, 19/12/2026, 9/1/2027 (星期六 10:00-12:30, 14:00-16:30)
實習：16/1, 23/1, 30/1, 13/2/2027 (星期六 14:00-16:30)
地址：香港中文大學
費用：免費
如果你是：
18-29歲的青年
正在或曾經在大專院校就讀
能夠閱讀繁體中文及以廣東話溝通
已登記心導遊+平台會員 （可免費登記）
*如之前曾完成說書人精神健康倡議培訓，將獲優先錄取
培訓簡介會和Q&A：
https://www.jcthplus.org/event/mental-health-impact-generation-training-info-session
培訓報名：
https://www.jcthplus.org/event/third-mental-health-impact-generation-training-2026-dec
聲音不應只停留在「聽見」，期待你的加入，一齊推動校園精神健康。
祝好，
賽馬會心導遊+計劃
If you are feeling confused or powerless about the mental health systems in university, and eager to support initiatives in campuses, join the
Mental Health Impact Generation Training
.
By participating in our training, you’ll work alongside like-minded peers to challenge the norms, reimagine mental health practices in campus environments, and explore ways various stakeholders can support student well-being.
What to Expect:
Over the course of 10 sessions, we’ll start with foundational concepts and progressing to hands-on practicum:
Lecture-Based Sessions
What is advocacy
Youth-led social impact and sustainable advocacy
Practical skills for planning and executing advocacy actions
Advocacy communication & collaboration
Practicum
Co-create public educational materials on campus mental health advocacy
Try out concepts in practice while bringing your own experience and strengths into the process
Practice healthy communication and collaboration in a supported group process
Event Details
Lecture Dates (Saturdays): 12/12/2026, 19/12/2026, and 9/1/2027 (10:00-12:30; 14:00-16:30)
Practicum Dates (Saturdays): 16/1, 23/1, 30/1, and 13/2/2027 (14:00-16:30)
Venue: The Chinese University of Hong Kong
Language: Cantonese
Fee: Free
Training Info Session and Q&A
https://www.jcthplus.org/event/mental-health-impact-generation-training-info-session
Apply to training
https://www.jcthplus.org/event/third-mental-health-impact-generation-training-2026-dec
We look forward to your participation in advancing mental health advocacy together.
Best regards,

title: HK$250 Stipend: Two-Person fNIRS Experiment for Chinese Mainland Male Students-Come with your travel companion! 250港币酬劳: 双人近红外实验机会，面向中国大陆男学生 – 与你的旅行朋友一起来体验吧！
bodyText:
Mass Mail System
Mass Mail System
Digest of CUHK Mass Mails for Undergraduate Students
»
2026/10/16
»
Announcements
HK$250 Stipend: Two-Person fNIRS Experiment for Chinese Mainland Male Students-Come with your travel companion! 250港币酬劳: 双人近红外实验机会，面向中国大陆男学生 – 与你的旅行朋友一起来体验吧！ - Department of Linguistics and Modern Languages
From: Xiaohui RAO
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
1155197282@link.cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
你对自己的大脑了解吗？你知道你跟小伙伴在交流对话过程中的共脑表现吗？不要错过这样一次难得的双人实验机会噢！！
本实验室使用临床级安全的近红外脑图系统，收集人大脑局部的耗氧变化，不会对人体产生伤害。有任何安全顾虑都可以和研究人员联系了解：
Miss RAO,
1155197282@link.cuhk.edu.hk
实验日期：5 Oct 2026 - 30 Oct 2026
实验时长：每次60-65分钟，共两次，可分别在同一天的上下午完成（包括实验准备20分钟，任务30-35分钟，填问卷5分钟）。
实验内容：1）佩戴近红外设备，参加互动实验，；2）填写一些问卷。
实验地点：中文大学梁銶琚楼G层（语言学系）G34实验室。
实验结束后，会通过转数快/现金/百佳优惠券来支付250港元被试费用。
参与者需要符合以下要求：
1. 母语为汉语普通话；
2. 视力（矫正后）正常，听力正常；
3. 无脑损伤、癫痫等神经类疾病，无头皮外伤或感染；
4. 右利手（写字，用筷子等习惯使用右手）；
5. 实验当天不化妆，实验当天或前一晚在家自行洗头；
6. 可以接受在实验过程上戴上类似脑电设备的头套（实验结束后无需洗头）
7. 有共同旅游经历的两位同性别朋友，共同线下参与实验
8. 旅游经历发生在近两个月内，且旅行时间跨度2天1晚及以上
报名链接：
https://www.wjx.top/vm/huu9JXm.aspx#
香港中文大学语言学及现代语言系
如有问题，请联系饶女士（1155197282@link.cuhk.edu.hk）
This research is endorsed by
Prof. CAI Zhenguang
zhenguangcai@cuhk.edu.hk
Department of Linguistics and Modern Languages
The Chinese University of Hong Kong
English Version:
Do you know your own brain? Are you curious about the inter-brain synchrony between you and your partner during communication and conversation? Don't miss out on this rare opportunity to participate in a two-person experiment!
Our laboratory utilizes a clinical-grade, safe functional Near-Infrared Spectroscopy (fNIRS) system to collect localized oxygenation changes in the human brain. This process is completely safe and does not cause any harm to the human body.
Experiment Date
: 5 Oct 2026 - 30 Oct 2026
Duration:
60-65 minutes per session, two sessions in total. Sessions can be completed consecutively in the morning and afternoon of the same day (including 20 mins preparation, 30-35 mins tasks, and 5 mins questionnaire).
Content:
1) Wear an fNIRS device and participate in an interactive experiment; 2) Complete questionnaires.
Location:
Room G34, G/F, Leung Kau Kui Building (Department of Linguistics), The Chinese University of Hong Kong (CUHK).
Compensation:
Upon completion, a stipend of HK$250 will be paid via FPS, cash, or ParknShop vouchers.
Participants need to meet the following requirements:
1. Native Mandarin speaker;
2. Normal vision (after correction) and normal hearing;
3. No brain injury, epilepsy, or other neurological diseases; no scalp trauma or infection;
4. Right-handed (e.g., writing, using chopsticks);
5. No make-up on the day of the experiment; wash hair at home on the day of or the night before the experiment;
6. Comfortable wearing an EEG-like cap during the experiment (no need to wash hair afterwards);
7. Two same-gender friends/colleagues with a shared travel experience, participating in the experiment together in person;
8. The travel experience occurred within the last two months, and the trip lasted for at least 2 days and 1 night.
Enrolment link:
https://www.wjx.top/vm/huu9JXm.aspx#
Department of Linguistics and Modern Languages, The Chinese University of Hong Kong
If you have any questions, please contact Miss Rao (1155197282@link.cuhk.edu.hk)
This research is endorsed by
Prof. CAI Zhenguang
zhenguangcai@cuhk.edu.hk
Department of Linguistics and Modern Languages
The Chinese University of Hong Kong

From: Global Business Programmes
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
denniswong@cuhk.edu.hk

Dear first-year students,
Ready to transform your university experience and stand out in today’s competitive business landscape?
The
International Business and Chinese Enterprise (IBCE)
and
Asian Business Studies (ABS)
transfer-in programmes are designed to cultivate regional expertise across diverse business contexts, while developing career readiness, professional networks, and focused skill sets.
To experience firsthand how IBCE and ABS can help you achieve your goals, we invite you to join session 2 of our exclusive taster event - the
AI Supercycle Finance Lab
!
In this session, we will explore how optical technology can help solve the growing networking bottleneck in AI, and how technological bottlenecks shape industry growth, business decisions, and value creation. You will be able to look beyond the headlines, understand how technology works, and develop the judgement to ask better business and investment questions.
AI Supercycle Finance Lab (Session 2)
Date: 28 October 2026 (Wed)
Time: 18:45 – 20:30
Venue: CYT 209B
Topic:
Beyond GPUs: Why Optics Matters to AI
Guest:
Mr. Caleb Chan (Asia Research Merchandising at Goldman Sachs; IBCE Alumnus)
Seats are limited. Register
here
by 25 October
and join IBCE and ABS students for a rewarding learning experience. Successful applicants will receive a confirmation email before the event.
Should you have any questions, please feel free to contact Mr. Dennis Wong, Programme Manager, Global Business Programmes at
denniswong@cuhk.edu.hk
.

誠邀香港失胎母親參加支持性護理需求研究－「香港經歷失胎女士的支援需求量表」
(完成問卷可獲送贈港幣$100元正超市禮券)
研究目的：
了解香港失胎女士在面對失胎經歷時的護理需求
協助日後有關失胎護理的服務、資訊及干預措施的發展
參加者納入標準：
年齡≥18歲的香港失胎女士
過去一年曾經經歷失胎的女士
能夠以中文回答問卷
研究程序：
基線問卷：參加者將會被要求完成一份約25分鐘分鐘問卷，問題與失胎的護理需要相關。
跟進問卷：在基線調查的兩週後，我們將再次隨機邀請 80 位參與者，完成一份跟進問卷。
⁠
完成問卷後，我們會送贈港幣
$100元正超市現金購物禮券
本研究均屬自願參與。研究資料會被保密，除研究人員外，任何人均不能獲取參與者所填寫的問卷資訊。本研究已通過香港中文大學調查及行為研究操守委員會(SBRE-23-0190)及香港中文大學–新界東醫院聯網臨床研究倫理聯席委員會 (Joint CUHK-NTEC CREC Ref. No. 2023.619) 批准。

電話：44643831
WhatsApp：44643831
The Jockey Club School of Public Health and Primary care is now recruiting women having experienced pregnancy loss for a supportive care needs study.
The study aims to explored the needs among women having experienced pregnancy loss, and to assist in the development of future healthcare services, information, and interventions related to pregnancy loss
Participant Eligibility Criteria:
1.Women who are over 18, having experienced pregnancy loss
2.Experienced pregnancy loss in the past 1 year
3.Able to read Chinese to answer questionnaires
Online survey details:
1.Baseline questionnaire: Participants will be asked to complete a 25-minute online survey, which includes questions about their supportive care needs following the loss.
2.Follow-up questionnaire: 80 participants will be randomly selected to complete a 20-minute follow-up questionnaire two weeks after the baseline survey.
Upon completion of the survey, a HK$100 supermarket voucher will be given to the participant.
How to participate:
Please complete the questionnaire via the following link:
https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_elphs5An5tseXNY
For enquiries, please contact Dr. Ling:
Phone: 44643831
WhatsApp: 44643831

We are now inviting Hong Kong young adults to participate in a bereavement survey, titled “Trajectories of grief outcomes and the associated psychosocial predictors among recently bereaved young adults in Hong Kong: A retrospective longitudinal mixed-methods approach”. Participants will receive up to HK$300 coupons upon completion.
Participant Inclusion Criteria:
Local young adults aged 18 to 29 residing in Hong Kong.
Have experienced the death of a close friend/relative or an important person within the past 18 months.
Able to read Chinese and communicate in Cantonese.
1) Baseline Questionnaire
- After signing the consent form, participants will complete a 20-minute baseline questionnaire.
- The questionnaire will include questions about grieving process in response to the death of a loved one or significant person, and attitudes toward death
- Participants will receive HK$100 coupons for completing the baseline questionnaire.
2) First Follow-up Questionnaire
- Six months later, participants who have completed the baseline questionnaire will be invited to complete a follow-up questionnaire.
- Participants who complete the first follow-up questionnaire will be rewarded with HK$100 coupons.
3) Second Follow-up Questionnaire
- Six months after the first follow-up questionnaire, participants who have completed the first follow-up questionnaire will be invited to complete a second follow-up questionnaire.
- Participants who complete the second follow-up questionnaire after will be rewarded with HK$100 coupons.
Participation in this study is voluntary. The study data will be kept confidential and no one other than the researchers will have access to the questionnaire information or audio recordings completed by the participants. This study has been approved by The Joint CUHK-NTEC CREC (CREC-2025.748) and the Survey and Behavioral Research Ethics Committee of the Chinese University of Hong Kong (SBRE‐24‐0378).
Please use the following link to fill out the consent form and questionnaire. Upon completion, you will be rewarded with HK$100 coupons.
https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_4SbSwIIE6shc67I
You are welcome to recommend this recruitment information to qualified young adults in Hong Kong.
For enquiries, please contact Dr. Ling
E-mail: haofengling@cuhk.edu.hk
