(Un)Seen | Our Moments with Loneliness
Presented by the Wellness and Counselling Centre, Office of Student Affairs
Loneliness often goes unnoticed, quietly woven into our daily lives. Through stories, art, and immersive experiences, we warmly invite you to reflect on these unseen emotions and transform them into connections.
Take a moment to slow down, see others, and be seen.
⭐
Exhibition
Through student artworks, personal reflections, psychoeducational content, multimedia, and interactive installations, the exhibition explores the many dimensions of loneliness in university life. By sharing students’ voices and experiences, it seeks to foster greater connection, compassion, and understanding within the University community.
Date:
20 – 30/10/2026
Opening Hours:
Monday to Friday | 10:00 a.m. – 6:00 p.m.
Saturday | 10:00 a.m. – 4:00 p.m.
Closed on Sunday
Venue:
G/F & i-LOUNGE, 3/F, Yasumoto International Academic Park
All CUHK members are welcome.
⭐
Workshop and Talk Series
Explore the complexities of loneliness and discover practical coping strategies through over 15 talks, workshops and interactive drop-in activities under the themes "Shape of Loneliness" and "Dance with Loneliness". Join us in reflecting on different experiences of loneliness while learning ways to foster connection and well-being. Quota is limited, and pre-registration is needed.
Click
here
for workshop details and registration.
⭐
Instagram Photo Challenge
What does loneliness look like through your lens? Join our Instagram Photo Challenge and capture a moment, place, or scene on campus that reflects the theme of loneliness—you might just discover new meanings and something unexpected!
Participating students will have the chance to win exciting prizes, including Kodak Charmera Blind Box Camera, Fujifilm Instax Mini instant cameras, and more!

sunshineatcuhk_osa_wacc
on Instagram for challenge details and participation details.

不妨放慢腳步，給自己一些時間及空間——看見他人，也讓自己被看見
。
⭐
展覽

We are recruiting volunteer native speakers of Hindi, Punjabi, Urdu, and/or Tamil to assist with recording a list of vocabulary items and short phrases. This project aims to
support children from ethnically diverse backgrounds
in learning Cantonese, English, and their home languages.
You must be:
1. Aged 18 or above;
2. A native speaker of Hindi, Punjabi, Tamil, and/or Urdu;
3. Able to read Hindi, Punjabi, Tamil, and/or Urdu;
4. Able to perform the recording task on the CUHK campus.
Non-CUHK volunteers are also welcome.
Details:
• Location: Academic Building No. 2, CUHK
• Duration: Approximately 1.5–2 hours
• Task: You will be asked to audio record a set of vocabulary items and short phrases in the language(s) you speak.

上次錯過左我地公眾展覽嘅朋友，我地返黎啦! 想了解陸地植被生態系統同碳循環嘅關係？咁就要黎參觀我哋嘅公眾展覽–「陸地植被生態系統在碳循環的關鍵角色」，我地會同大家拆解森林、灌木叢、草地點樣封存同儲存二氧化碳，仲會講解大嶼山植被嘅分佈狀況添～
Missed our last public exhibition? We are back! Want to discover the connection between terrestrial vegetated ecosystems and the carbon cycle? Come and join our public exhibition on the "Key Roles of Terrestrial Vegetated Ecosystems in Carbon Cycling". We will explain how forests, shrublands, and grasslands sequester and store CO2, and also provide an overview of the vegetation distribution in Lantau Island~

From: New Asia College

「新亞儒學講座系列」由夢周文教基金會贊助舉辦。第十二屆講座將於十月舉辦，講者為方嵐生教授。方教授為現任夏威夷大學馬諾阿分校哲學系教授。講座詳情如下：
第一講
題目：孟子論人之所欲
主持：香港中文大學哲學系教授Prof. David Chai
日期：2026年10月21日（星期三）
時間：下午6時30分至下午8時
地點：香港中文大學邵逸夫堂
（本講座於書院雙週會內舉行）
第二講
題目：早期儒家倫理的共同基礎
主持：香港中文大學哲學系姚治華教授
日期：2026年10月22日（星期四）
時間：下午4時30分至下午6時15分
地點：香港中文大學行政樓地下祖堯堂
（本講座由香港中文大學新亞書院與哲學系合辦）
第三講
題目：死後生命在早期儒學中的相關性
主持：香港中文大學哲學系鄭澤綿教授
日期：2026年10月24日（星期六）
時間：下午3時至下午5時
地點：九龍尖沙咀香港文化中心行政大樓四樓會議室AC1
講座以英語講述，歡迎現場或網上參與。
(Zoom網上連結將於活動前以電郵通知已報名者)
網上報名：
https://cloud.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk/webform/view.php?id=13740305
如有查詢，請聯絡書院輔導處王先生（電話：3943-1690 電郵：
jackwong@cuhk.edu.hk
）或梁小姐（電話：3943-9589 電郵：
angelaleung@cuhk.edu.hk
）。
“New Asia Lectures on Confucianism” is generously sponsored by the Moonchu Foundation. The 12th New Asia Lectures on Confucianism will be held in October 2026, and it is our honor to have invited Professor Franklin Perkins to be our speaker. Professor Perkins is the Professor of Philosophy at the University of Hawai’i at Mānoa. Details of the lectures are as follows:
1st Lecture
Topic: Mengzi on What People Really Want
Moderator: Prof. David Chai, Department of Philosophy, CUHK
Date: 21 October 2026 (Wednesday)
Time: 6:30pm – 8:00pm
Venue: Sir Run Run Shaw Hall, CUHK
(This lecture will be held at the College Bi-weekly Assembly)
2nd Lecture
Topic: The Common Foundation for Early Confucian Ethics
Moderator: Prof. Zhihua Yao, Department of Philosophy, CUHK
Date: 22 October 2026 (Thursday)
Time: 4:30pm – 6:15pm
Venue: Cho Yiu Conference Hall, G/F, University Administration Building, CUHK
(This lecture is jointly organized by New Asia College and Department of Philosophy, CUHK)
3rd Lecture
Topic: The Relevance of Life After Death in Early Confucianism
Moderator: Prof. Zemian Zheng, Department of Philosophy, CUHK
Date: 24 October 2026 (Saturday)
Time: 3:00pm – 5:00pm
Venue: Function Room AC1, 4/F, Administration Building, Hong Kong Cultural Centre, Tsim Sha Tsui, Kowloon
All lectures will be conducted in English.
Participation in person or via Zoom online is also welcome.
(A Zoom link will be sent to registrants by email before the event)
Online Registration:
https://cloud.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk/webform/view.php?id=13740305
For enquiries, please contact Mr. Jack Wong, Dean of Students’ Office (Tel: 3943-1690; Email:
jackwong@cuhk.edu.hk
) or Miss Angela Leung, Dean of Students’ Office (Tel: 3943-9589; Email:
angelaleung@cuhk.edu.hk
).
View Count
For request submissions, please submit them at
https://cumassmail.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk
For enquiries, please write to:
http://servicedesk.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk

Ready to put your data analytics skills into action? This is your chance to showcase your expertise and collaborate with peers across disciplines!
The CUHK Library, in collaboration with the Data Science and Policy Studies Programme, is pleased to invite applications for the Data Analytics Practice Opportunity 2026/27. This initiative provides CUHK students with valuable hands-on experience working with real-world datasets and digitised records, empowering them to craft compelling stories through data visualisation and analytics tools. Participants will also have the opportunity to showcase their projects and findings during Data Excellence Week 2027.

Teams of 2-3 members

Announcements
Take Charge of Your Health: Central Obesity Programme for Adults Aged 40–64 [HK$200 Coupon]   40–64歲健康新開始：參與中央肥胖改善計劃，完成可獲HK$200現金券！ - Department of Sports Science and Physical Education
From: MA Chun hin
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
ericaaama@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
邀請參加本項研究
初步證據顯示, 間歇性飲食（INTD）和高強度間歇運動（HIIE）在改善心血管代謝健康和減重方面存在協同作用。本研究旨在探討INTD和HIIE對體力活動不足的中央肥胖成人的心血管健康影響。
受試者招募
本研究的目標人群為香港體力活動不足的中年成年人（年齡40至64歲），並且具有中央肥胖。中央肥胖將定義為男性腰圍達90厘米（cm）或以上，女性腰圍達80厘米或以上。如果您對任何列出的條件有疑問，請諮詢研究人員。
問卷網址
https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_5q1f0ammiljEDOu
如您有任何疑問，可通過以下渠道聯絡這項研究的相關人員：
馬先生
WhatsApp: 39436085
Email: ericaaama@cuhk.edu.hk
Invitation to Participate in Research Study
Preliminary evidence has suggested a synergistic interaction effect of intermittent dieting (INTD) and high intensity interval exercise (HIIE) on cardio-metabolic health and weight loss. This study aims to examine the effects of INTD and HIIE and intermittent dieting for cardiometabolic and cardiovascular fitness in physically inactive adults with central obesity.
Participant Recruitment
The target population of the proposed study will be physically inactive middle-aged adults (aged 40–64 years) with central obesity in Hong Kong. Central obesity will be defined as having a waist circumference 90 centimeters (cm) or above for men and 80 cm or above for women. If you are unsure about any of the listed conditions, then you should consult with the researchers.
Survey address
https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_5q1f0ammiljEDOu
Contact Us
If you are interested and have any inquiries, please feel free to contact us:
Mr. MA
WhatsApp: 39436085
Email: ericaaama@cuhk.edu.hk

bodyText:

2026/10/09

Announcements
HK$500 reward! Recruiting Cantonese speakers for a language learning study  招募廣東話母語者參與語言學習研究，成功完成測試可獲500hkd酬謝 - Department of Linguistics and Modern Languages
From: CHEN Xinwen
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
xinwen.chen@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
實驗時間：
需來两次：一節爲腦電實驗，約3小時；一節爲行為實驗，約2.5小時。
實驗內容：
①腦電實驗：
佩戴腦電帽
（對人體安全無害）完成語言學習任務
腦電實驗中，您將會接受
經顱光生物調節（tPBM）
：此儀器用一束微弱的光刺激額頭，同樣對人體完全無害，不會有任何感覺，已獲得大學和醫院的使用批准，這種儀器已被證實可以有效提高記憶力。
②行為實驗：完成一系列語言和認知測試；
③填寫問卷。
實驗地點：
①腦電/光調節實驗在香港中文大學王福元樓406A進行；②行為實驗在香港中文大學梁銶琚樓G/F進行
兩次實驗結束後，會支付500港元被試費用。
參與者需要符合以下要求：
1. 年齡18-30歲，非心理學/語言學專業。
2. 母語為廣東話；
3. 聽力、視力或矯正視力正常；
4. 無腦損傷、癲癇等神經類疾病，無頭皮外傷或感染；
5. 右利手；
6. 實驗時間身體健康，無感冒發燒咳嗽等狀況；
7. 實驗前要保證充足的睡眠，精力充沛認真負責完成實驗；
8. 實驗前24小時未服用大量茶、咖啡等飲料；實驗前不要有劇烈的體育活動；
9. 實驗前兩週不能染髮；
10. 實驗當天需要洗頭，不能化妝，額頭不要塗防曬霜、隔離霜等。
如有任何問題，請聯繫：xinwen.chen@cuhk.edu.hk
報名連結：
http://137.189.158.12/limesurvey/index.php?r=survey/index&sid=813414&lang=zh-Hant-HK
Experiment Duration:
You will need to visit twice: one session for the EEG experiment (approximately 3 hours) and one session for the behavioral experiment (approximately 2.5 hours).
Experiment Details:
1. EEG experiment: Completing language learning tasks with an
EEG
cap
Participants in the EEG study will receive
transcranial photobiomodulation (tPBM)
: This device uses a weak beam of light to stimulate the forehead. It is completely harmless to the human body and causes no sensation. This type of device has been proven to effectively improve memory and has been approved for use by universities and hospitals.
2. Behavioral experiment: Completing a series of language and cognitive tests;
3. Completion of questionnaires.
Experiment Locations: 406A, Wong Foo Yuan Building OR G/F, Leung Kau Kui Building, CUHK
After completing
both sessions
, participants will receive a reimbursement of
HK$500
.
Eligibility Requirements:
Aged 18–30; not majoring in psychology or linguistics.
Cantonese native speaker.
Normal hearing and vision, or corrected-to-normal vision.
No history of brain injury, epilepsy, or other neurological conditions; no scalp injuries or infections.
Right-handed (i.e., habitually writes or uses chopsticks with the right hand).
In good health on the day of the experiment (no cold, fever, cough, etc.).
Well-rested before the experiment, and able to complete the task attentively and responsibly.
No consumption of large amounts of tea, coffee, or similar drinks within 24 hours prior; no intense physical activity before the experiment.
No hair dyeing within two weeks before the experiment.
Please wash your hair and do not wear makeup or apply sunscreen/primer/foundation on the forehead on the day of the experiment.
For inquiries, please contact: xinwen.chen@cuhk.edu.hk
Registration link:
http://137.189.158.12/limesurvey/index.php?r=survey/index&sid=813414&lang=zh-Hant-HK

From: The Programme Secretariat
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
b133856@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
MSc in Clinical Gerontology and End-of-Life Care
equips students with advanced knowledge and practical skills in gerontology, palliative care, and end-of-life care. It is designed for professionals in social welfare, healthcare, and related sectors who wish to strengthen their practice and expand their career opportunities.The programme is designed to support
healthcare professionals
and
social workers
.
The 2027/28 academic year will commence in September 2027. Students may choose to pursue the programme on
1-year full-time
or
2-year part-time
basis.
臨牀老人學與寧養關顧理學碩士
課程涵蓋老年學、認知障礙症照顧、紓緩治療及安寧照顧等範疇，旨在提升社福、醫護及相關專業人士的知識與實務能力，以回應人口老化帶來的服務需要。課程適合
醫療衛生專業人員及社工
。 2027/28學年將於2027年9月開始, 學生可選擇入讀1年全日制或2年兼讀制課程。

Plan Your Next Gathering at Si Yuan Amenites Centre 活動籌備中？思源館助您輕鬆打造理想聚會 - Dean of Students' Office, United College
From: Jackie Chow/ Marco Chan

正在籌備活動，想尋找一個環境舒適、氣氛輕鬆的場地嗎？
思源館（SYAC）現正接受場地預訂，歡迎學生組織、中大學系／部門／單位及校友團體租用，舉辦各類型活動，包括聚會、工作坊、分享會、生日派對，以及其他社交或文化活動。
除了提供舒適的活動空間外，思源館亦可按活動需要安排餐飲服務，讓參加者在輕鬆愉快的環境中交流互動，為活動增添更多特色與便利。
有關場地租用收費、餐飲安排及餐單選擇，以及預訂程序等詳情，歡迎瀏覽思源館網站：
https://www.uc.cuhk.edu.hk/si-yuan-amenities-centre-2/
如有任何查詢，歡迎致電 2603 7486 與我們聯絡。

title: EEG Experiment: 1.5h for 120 HKD (Native Mandarin Speakers) 【普通话母语者招募中】你的大脑是怎么读中文的？来实验室告诉我们
bodyText:
Mass Mail System
Mass Mail System
Digest of CUHK Mass Mails for Undergraduate Students
»
2026/10/09
»
Announcements
EEG Experiment: 1.5h for 120 HKD (Native Mandarin Speakers) 【普通话母语者招募中】你的大脑是怎么读中文的？来实验室告诉我们 - Department of Linguistics and Modern Languages
From: Yiting WANG
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
yitingwang@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
你好！
我们诚挚地邀请你参加一项关于语言认知的脑电（EEG）实验。任务很简单：
来实验室看一些视频
。我们会记录你的脑电波，看看母语阅读时大脑有多忙碌！
本实验室使用临床级安全的脑电图系统，收集人自身产生的微弱生物电并绘制成波形图，不会对人体产生伤害。有任何安全顾虑都可以和研究人员联系了解：Miss WANG, yitingwang@cuhk.edu.hk
实验时长
：约1.5小时
实验内容：
1）佩戴脑电设备，参加互动实验，观看一些视频并用键盘按键做出反应；2）填写一些问卷。
实验地点：
中文大学梁銶琚楼G层（语言学系）G34实验室。
实验结束后，会通过转数快支付
120港元
被试费用。
参与者需要符合以下要求
：
1.
18-30
岁
，来自中国大陆，母语为汉语普通话；
2. 视力（矫正后）正常，无干涩等眼部不适；
3. 听力正常；
4. 无脑损伤、癫痫等神经类疾病，无头皮外伤或感染；
5. 无身体残疾；
6. 近2个月内无染发，实验当天不化妆，实验当天在家自行洗头；
7. 可以接受在头发头皮上涂抹特制的导电膏体（实验室配备专门的洗头房，供您实验结束之后洗净吹干）；
8. 非心理学、语言学专业；
9. 右利手（写字、用筷子等习惯使用右手）；
10. 没有参加过此实验的相关实验（如果不确定可以联系主试确认：Miss WANG, yitingwang@cuhk.edu.hk)
报名链接
：https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_9FZeVuIlwkN6tKK
香港中文大学语言学及现代语言系
This research is endorsed by
Prof. CAI Zhenguang
zhenguangcai@cuhk.edu.hk
Department of Linguistics and Modern Languages
The Chinese University of Hong Kong
Hi there!
Ever wondered how does your brain read Chinese?
We’re recruiting
native Mandarin speakers
for an EEG experiment. The task is simple:
come to the lab and watch some videos
. We’ll record your brainwaves to see how busy your brain gets when processing your native language.
Duration of the experiment
: The experiment duration is approximately 1.5 hours
Experiment content:
1) wearing EEG devices, reading some Chinese sentences and responding with keyboard keys; 2) filling out some questionnaires.
Experiment location
: Room G34, G/F, K.K. Leung Building, The Chinese University of Hong Kong.
The subject fee of
HK$120
will be paid via FPS (other approaches are supported) at the end of the experiment.
Participants need to meet the
following requirements
:
1. native Mandarin Chinese speaker, 18-30 years old;
2. have normal vision (after correction) and no eye discomfort such as dryness;
3. have normal hearing;
4. no brain injury, epilepsy or other neurological diseases, no scalp trauma or infection;
5. no physical disability;
6. no hair coloring in the last 2 months, no make-up on the day of the experiment, and washing hair at home by themselves on the day of the experiment;
7. can accept the application of special conductive paste on the hair scalp (the laboratory is equipped with a special hair washing room; participants can wash hair at the end of the experiment);
8. non-psychology / linguistics majors;
9. right-handed (writing, using chopsticks, etc.);
10. have not participated in the preparatory experiment for this experiment. If you are not sure, you can contact the experimenter to confirm: Miss WANG, yitingwang@cuhk.edu.hk
Enrolment link:
https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_9FZeVuIlwkN6tKK
Department of Linguistics and Modern Languages, The Chinese University of Hong Kong

Prof. CAI Zhenguang
zhenguangcai@cuhk.edu.hk

Turn environmental data into solutions for a more sustainable future. CUHK’s M.Sc. in Earth and Environmental Analytics for Sustainability Programme combines earth system science with data analytics, AI, and environmental modelling to address the most pressing sustainability issues our world faces today. Through both lecture-based and project-based learning, students develop skills in areas such as climate risk analysis, remote sensing, and ESG analysis—preparing for careers in environmental consulting, research, conservation, and corporate sustainability.
Applications for the 2027–28 academic year are open and reviewed on a rolling basis, so early applications are encouraged.

title: .~~【Interprofessional Self Determination theory-based educational interventions on diabetes mellitus management】.. 誠邀糖尿病(DM)及前期糖尿病(Pre DM)病患者參與【基於自決理論的跨專業干預，以改善香港基層醫療機構的糖尿病管理】研究計劃 (最多可獲$400超市禮券) ~
bodyText:
Mass Mail System
Mass Mail System
Digest of CUHK Mass Mails for Undergraduate Students
»
2026/10/09
»
Announcements
.~~【Interprofessional Self Determination theory-based educational interventions on diabetes mellitus management】.. 誠邀糖尿病(DM)及前期糖尿病(Pre DM)病患者參與【基於自決理論的跨專業干預，以改善香港基層醫療機構的糖尿病管理】研究計劃 (最多可獲$400超市禮券) ~  - The Nethersole School of Nursing
From: Irene Cheung
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
b193099@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
香港中文大學學能提升研究中心現正招募二型糖尿病(DM) / 前期糖尿(Pre DM)患者參與
【基於自決理論的跨專業干預，以改善香港基層醫療機構的糖尿病管理】
研究計劃，目的旨在開發和驗證適合香港情況的跨專業教育干預措施，為政府的衛生保健策略提供資訊，以加强慢性病管理。
如閣下有興趣參與是項研究，請點擊以下連結
https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_cNNsLtBwB2nxkR8
或掃描海報中的QR code填寫網上報名表，研究人員將會初步評估及聯絡合適的參加者。
如有查詢，請於星期一至五(公眾假期除外)辦公時間內致電3943 5015查詢。
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Centre for Learning Enhancement And Research – CLEAR, The Chinese University of Hong Kong is recruiting individuals with Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus (DM) or Prediabetes (Pre DM) to participate in a study
【
Interprofessional Self Determination theory-based educational interventions on diabetes mellitus
ma
nagement
】
.
It aims to examine the effects and mechanisms of a theory-based educational program on diabetes mellitus management and provide evidence for potential policy changes in the framework for care of diabetes mellitus in primary care settings.
If you are interested, please fill in the online form via
https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_cNNsLtBwB2nxkR8
or scan the QR code in the above poster. We will contact eligible participants and further explain the details of the study.
For inquiries, please contact us during office hour (Mon-Fri):  3943 5015.
View Count
For request submissions, please submit them at
https://cumassmail.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk
For enquiries, please write to:
http://servicedesk.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk
Copyright © 2013. All Rights Reserved. The Chinese University of Hong Kong.
/weekly/

The Nethersole School of Nursing, Faculty of Medicine, The Chinese University of Hong Kong is recruiting children diagnosed with autism spectrum disorder (ASD) and relatives of them to participate in a study
【Investigate Structural Variations (SVs) in Autism Spectrum (ASD) and Related Endophenotypes】
. It aims to investigate the association of mutations in genes, as well as other potential structural variants, with autism spectrum disorder (ASD) in individuals from Hong Kong.
If you are interested, please fill in the online form via
https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_79egbgKOW0c0cFU

title: Communication Seminar Series Community-Engaged AI in Civic and Social Organizations: Meaningful and Democratic Communication Co-Creation for Health Equity and Social Good

Communication Seminar Series Community-Engaged AI in Civic and Social Organizations: Meaningful and Democratic Communication Co-Creation for Health Equity and Social Good  - School of Journalism and Communication
From: School of Journalism and Communication
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
com@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
Communication Seminar Series - Community-Engaged AI in Civic and Social Organizations: Meaningful and Democratic Communication Co-Creation for Health Equity and Social Good
Date: 23 October 2026 (Friday)
Time: 10:30 am-12:00 nn
Venue: C-Centre (NAH313, Humanities Building, CUHK)
Speaker:
Prof. Andy Tan
Associate Professor
Annenberg School for Communication
University of Pennsylvania, USA
Bio:
Andy Tan is Associate Professor of Communication at the Annenberg School for Communication of the University of Pennsylvania. Dr. Tan’s research program is aimed at advancing communication science to achieve health equity for all. His work examines the impact of marketing, media, and public health messages on health behaviors and outcomes among diverse populations including young adults, socioeconomically disadvantaged, and lesbian, gay, bisexual, and transgender (LGBT) populations. He conducts community-engaged research involving organizations that serve LGBT communities to design and develop culturally appropriate communication interventions that are informed by persuasion and message effects theories, social determinants of health frameworks, and implementation science. The goal of this work is to translate this knowledge into scalable and culturally sensitive communication interventions to alleviate tobacco- and cancer-related health disparities. Dr. Tan is the recipient of awards for his communication and health equity research including the 2025 Presidential Early Career Award for Scientists and Engineers (PECASE), the American Public Health Association Health Equity Award in 2021, and was inducted as a Fellow by the Society for Research in Nicotine and Tobacco in 2026.
Abstract:
Civic and social organizations are embedded within local communities and provide essential health and social services to individuals, families, and communities. Staff of civic and social organizations have a deep understanding of the issues and community assets, are trusted messengers, and have shared lived experiences with the communities they serve. However, they often have limited resources for health communication and to create professional quality education and outreach campaigns. Over 2 summers (2025-2026), the Annenberg School partnered with COLOURS, a Philadelphia-based organization serving BIPOC and LGTBQ+ residents for 35 years, to design, test, and deploy
OurSpace
, an AI-supported workspace. In the summer of 2026, the study piloted
OurSpace
for COLOURS staff to plan for and promote an outreach event for medical and social needs case managers serving people living with HIV. In this talk, the speaker introduces the Community-Engaged AI lifecycle, describe the underlying rationale of
OurSpace
’s design, trace the evolution of its affordances, and deploying
OurSpace
in ways that ensure AI amplifies rather than substitutes local knowledge and experience of civic social organizations. Using examples of products created by COLOURS staff, observation notes, surveys, and qualitative inputs, the speaker discusses the strengths, limitations, and next steps for responsible and meaningful use of
OurSpace
to achieve health equity and social good in communication research and practice.
Language: English

bodyText:

Announcements
.【 $250 Coupon 】Recruiting Children (aged 11 or under) for the Gut Microbiome and Children's Emotional Health Development Study 誠意邀請11歲或以下兒童參加腸道微生物及兒童心智發展的研究-Department of Psychiatry  - Department of Psychiatry
From: Dr. WONG Wing Ho, Oscar
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
oscarwhwong@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
家長您好，我們是香港中文大學醫學院精神科學系的研究團隊。本研究由香港中文大學醫學院精神科學系、內科及藥物治療學系統籌。
本研究團隊誠邀5歲以下兒童參與一項有關腸道微生態與兒童大腦發展及風險研究。此研究希望透過收集小朋友之大便及口腔樣本，幫助了解腸道微生態與大腦發展的關係。
研究對象:
1) 確診/懷疑小朋友有自閉症傾向或其他發展問題
2) 4歲或以下的小朋友 (交齊問卷和樣本的日子未滿5歲即可)
3) 父母皆為華裔或亞裔人士
4) 小朋友18歲以下的兄弟姊妹
以下為是次研究需要完成的事項：
1) 簽署參加同意書
2) 網上問卷調查：網上問卷主要詢問小朋友的行為及腸道情況，填寫時間約45分鐘
3) 收集大便和口腔樣本：我們會給家長一個樣本收集包，請家長使用收集包內的物在家中資協助收集樣本
4) 飲食習慣的問卷：記錄小朋友的飲食習慣
完成研究後，參加者可以獲得$200的超市現金券、 G-NiiB益生菌試用裝和腸道健康報告作為答謝 另外，家長有機會被邀請進行面談並隨訪2年,如有需要我們會提供轉介信。是次研究是自願參與性質參與，這個研究期間所取得的資料都會被嚴格保密。
如家長有意願參與此項研究，請填寫以下網上篩選問卷(https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_81kdBVoLu4f6l3o)。收到問卷回覆後，我們會再與合適參加是次研究的小朋友之家長連絡。
如果家長對研究細節有任何疑問，歡迎透過WhatsApp 6099-3064或致電 2607-6057與我們聯絡。
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Dear Parents,
We are a team of researchers from the Department of Psychiatry at the Chinese University of Hong Kong. We are conducting a research project jointly organised by the Department of Psychiatry, the Department of Medicine and Therapeutics of the Chinese University of Hong Kong.
Our team sincerely invites your children to participate in research on gut microbiome and children's brain development. Through collecting stool and buccal samples, we aim to investigate the relationship between gut microbiome and brain development.
A gut health report will be provided, A G-Niib probiotics trial pack and a $200 supermarket voucher will be awarded to participants.
Target participants:
1) The child is diagnosed/suspected to have autism or other developmental problems
2) The child is 4 years old or under (all questionnaires and samples are submitted before 5 years old)
3) Both parents are Chinese or Asian
4) Children’s brothers and sisters under 18 years old are also welcome to join
Procedures and details of this Study:
1) Research Consent
2) Online Questionnaire : A 45-minute questionnaire on children’s behaviors and their physical health condition
3) Stool and Buccal Sample Collection: Samples collection kit will be provided for sample collection at home
4) Dietary Questionnaire: Recording children's eating habits
You will receive a $200 supermarket voucher after completing all the research procedures. Participation is voluntary, and your responses will be kept confidential. The information you provide will be used solely for research purposes.
If you are interested in participating in our research study, please fill out the following online questionnaire (https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_81kdBVoLu4f6l3o). We will contact you afterwards if your children are suitable to join this study.
For inquiries, please contact 2607-6057 or WhatsApp 6099-3064.

親愛的女士：
您好！
隨着年齡增長與絕經後的荷爾蒙變化，您是否覺得體重逐漸增加、脂肪容易囤積，或者開始擔心體脂、血脂等健康指標？香港中文大學體育運動科學系目前正開展一項研究以了解不同有氧運動訓練對絕經後超重或肥胖女性代謝健康的影響。我們誠邀符合條件的華人女性參與，一起通過科學運動重拾健康！
參與本研究，您將免費獲得：
1. 全面身體成分評估：精準檢測體脂率、肌肉量、內臟脂肪等。
2. 專業血液指標檢測：了解您的血脂、血糖等核心代謝指標。
3. 專家級運動能力測試：精準測量您專屬的運動代謝表現，以評估您的體能與代謝反應。
4. 為期 12 週的免費運動指導：由專業研究人員全程跟進，保障運動安全與效果。

我們在尋找這樣的您：
華人女性，且已自然絕經 12 個月或以上（距離最後一次月經少於 6 年）。
體型偏胖（BMI ≥ 23 kg/m² 或 體脂率 > 30%，以實驗室測試為準）。
平時運動較少（每星期少於 150 分鐘中等強度體能活動、少於 75 分鐘劇烈強度體能活動，或二者同等組合）。
過去 3 個月體重相對穩定，且無嚴重運動禁忌（如嚴重心臟病、中風等）。
⏳
您需要做什麼？（
3
次評估
+ 12
周幹預訓練）
本研究為期 12 週，合格者將隨機分配至對照組、有氧運動組A、有氧運動組B，期間需前往香港中文大學實驗室進行 3 次評估，具體包括：問卷調查、空腹靜脈抽血檢測、指尖採血、身體成分測量、運動代謝測試。為減少測試過程中的不適感，運動代謝測試將與其他健康測試分開進行，整個研究過程中，您總共需要到達實驗室

Department of Sports Science and Physical Education
The Chinese University of Hong Kong

Sender: He Wenke

wenke.he@link.cuhk.edu.hk
The Department of Sports Science and Physical Education, The Chinese University of Hong Kong,
Sports Nutrition and Physical Activity Laboratory,
sincerely invites you to participate in an exercise intervention study! This study will help us understand your exercise metabolic performance and improve your metabolic health.
Study Title
: A Randomized Controlled Trial Comparing the Effects of Different Aerobic Exercise Training on Metabolic and Circulating Blood Indicators in Postmenopausal Women with overweight or obesity
Dear Madam:
With aging and postmenopausal hormonal changes, do you feel that your weight is gradually increasing, fat is easily accumulated, or you begin to worry about health indicators such as body fat and blood lipids? The Department of Sports Science and Physical Education at The Chinese University of Hong Kong is currently conducting a study to understand the effects of different aerobic exercise training on metabolic health in postmenopausal women with overweight or obesity. We sincerely invite eligible Chinese women to participate and regain health together through scientific exercise!
By participating in this study, you will receive for free:
1. Comprehensive body composition assessment: accurate measurement of body fat percentage, muscle mass, visceral fat, etc.
2. Professional blood indicator testing: understand your core metabolic indicators such as blood lipids and blood glucose.
3. Expert-level exercise capacity test: accurately measure your exercise metabolic performance to evaluate your physical fitness and metabolic response.
4. 12 weeks of free exercise guidance: full follow‑up by professional researchers to ensure exercise safety and effectiveness.
We are looking for:
1. Chinese women who have been naturally postmenopausal for 12 months or more (less than 6 years since the last menstrual period).
2. Are overweight or obese (BMI ≥ 23 kg/m² or body fat percentage > 30%; will be confirmed by laboratory testing).
3. Are usually physically inactive (less than 150 minutes of moderate‑intensity physical activity, less than 75 minutes of vigorous‑intensity physical activity per week, or an equivalent combination).
4. Have had relatively stable body weight in the past 3 months, and have no serious contraindications to exercise (e.g., severe heart disease, stroke, etc.).
⏳ What do you need to do? (3 assessments + 12‑week intervention training)
This study lasts 12 weeks. Eligible participants will be randomly assigned to a
control group
,
aerobic
exercise group A,
or
aerobic exercise group B
. During the period, you will need to visit the laboratory at The Chinese University of Hong Kong for 3 assessments, including: questionnaire surveys, fasting venous blood draw, finger‑prick blood sampling, body composition measurement, and exercise metabolic testing. To reduce discomfort during testing, the exercise metabolic test will be conducted separately from other health tests. Throughout the study, you will need to come to the laboratory
6 times.
12‑week intervention training: 3 times per week, 40‑70 minutes per session, for 12 weeks.
Upon completion of the study, you will receive a HK$150 shopping voucher and a health report.
Trial location: G02 Office, Ground Floor, Kwok Sports Building, The Chinese University of Hong Kong
Register now / Enquire:
Places are limited, first‑come, first‑served! You can click the link below to register:
https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSfZKjSc55Ov13iAjw_GAGkFIbINsXc9rH1ePEYg6CWrU5w5Ew/viewform?usp=header
If you have any questions, please contact the research team:
Study coordinator: Ms. He (WhatsApp: +852 5984 8824)
Supervising professor: Prof. Stephen Heung-sang WONG (Department of Sports Science and Physical Education, The Chinese University of Hong Kong)
Wishing you good health!
Research Team

title: [Max. HKD$1200] Recruiting Native Cantonese-speaking Grandparents with hearing loss and Grandchildren for an Interaction Experiment [最高可獲HKD$1200][長者認知及聽力測試報告; + 兒童IQ智商測試報告] 招募聽力損失長者及其孫子女參與互動實驗
bodyText:

Mass Mail System
Digest of CUHK Mass Mails for Undergraduate Students
»
2026/10/09
»
Announcements
[Max. HKD$1200] Recruiting Native Cantonese-speaking Grandparents with hearing loss and Grandchildren for an Interaction Experiment [最高可獲HKD$1200][長者認知及聽力測試報告; + 兒童IQ智商測試報告] 招募聽力損失長者及其孫子女參與互動實驗 - Brain and Mind Institute
From: LEUNG Mei Yee
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
meiyeeleung424@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
我們是
香港中文大學大腦與認知研究所（BMI）
的研究團隊。我們團隊誠摯邀請有聽力損失的長者及其孫子女來參與一項互動研究。
參與者需符合以下條件：
長者：
65歲或以上，存在聽力損失，
無其他已知認知障礙症狀， 且
有意願配戴助聽器
孩童：
6-9歲
，無其他已知發展問題，母語為廣東話
實驗內容：本實驗共分為兩節（每節約1.5至2小時）：
- 第一節：長者將獨自參與一項
認知及聽力檢測
（當日孫子女無需到場）
- 第二節：長者將與孫子女一同進行
簡單遊戲
，期間我們將使用安全且非侵入性的
「近紅外光譜儀」（fNIRS）
進行腦部掃描
- 請注意：參與者必須先完成第一節的實驗，且結果符合研究要求，方會獲邀參與第二節的實驗
完成整個實驗後，您可獲得：
- 長者：一份
認知能力測試報告
+ 一份
純音聽力測試報告
- 孩童：一份
非語言智商測試報告
+ 一份
價值HKD$80的禮物
報酬：
現金HKD$400-1200
，以及免費停車券（如適用）
實驗地點：香港中文大學大腦與認知研究所（位於校園內）
如您對本研究感興趣，請點擊以下連結填寫報名表格：
https://ci.cuhk.edu.hk/surveys/?s=LJEXMFLMR79XA7TX
如祖孫兩位初步符合條件，我們將會儘快與您聯絡！
如有疑問，請發送電郵至 meiyeeleung424@cuhk.edu.hk，
亦可致電或Whatsapp 95867123 查詢。
我們期待你的參與！
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
We are researchers from the
Brain and Mind Institute (BMI) at the Chinese University of Hong Kong
. Our team sincerely invites grandparents with hearing loss and their grandchildren for a social interaction study.
Participants need to be:
- Grandparent:
65+ years old with hearing loss
, with no other diagnosed cognitive impairment, interested in fitting hearing aids
- Grandchild:
6-9 years old
with no other developmental problems; speaking Cantonese as the first language
What is involved? The experiment consists of two sessions (approx. 1.5-2 hours each):
- Session 1: The grandparent will participate alone in a
cognitive and hearing test
. (The grandchild does not need to attend)
- Session 2: The grandparent and grandchild will participate together in some
simple games
while using
fNIRS
(
functional near-infrared spectroscopy
, safe and non-invasive!!!) brain scanning device
- NOTE: Participants must first complete Session 1 and meet the study's requirements to be invited to Session 2
What you'll get (upon completion of the entire study):
- For the grandparent:
A cognitive test report
and
a pure-tone audiometry
(hearing test) report
- For the child:
An non-verbal IQ test report
and
a gift (~HKD$80)
Reward:
HKD$400-1200 allowance
and free parking ticket.
Location: Brain and Mind Institute, The Chinese University of Hong Kong (In campus).
If you are interested in our study, please fill in the form below via the following link:
https://ci.cuhk.edu.hk/surveys/?s=LJEXMFLMR79XA7TX
We will contact you afterwards if the dyad are suitable.
For inquiries, please contact: meiyeeleung424@cuhk.edu.hk,
call or Whatsapp 95867123.
We look forward to your participation!
View Count

https://cumassmail.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk
For enquiries, please write to:
http://servicedesk.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk

/weekly/

From: Social Responsibility and Sustainable Development Office

srsdo@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
中秋節將至，我們歡度佳節的同時，各種的送禮及慶祝活動往往會產生大量垃圾。為減少節日期間的垃圾，中大今年繼續參與綠領行動「月餅盒回收大行動」，收集到的月餅盒將送往環保署核准的回收商進行本地循環再造。
***中大收集日期：2026年9月28日（一 ）至10月9日（五）***
***月餅盒回收箱位置：康本國際學術園地下大堂***
回收指引：紙製及金屬製的月餅盒均可回收（請移除所有包裝物料並妥善處理）
如有查詢，請聯絡社會責任及可持續發展處（3943 3972/
srsdo@cuhk.edu.hk
）。
As the Mid-Autumn Festival approaches, we will enjoy the delicious mooncakes and collect some mooncake boxes.  Instead of discarding these boxes, we can recycle them and give them a new purpose.  This year, CUHK continues to participate in the Greeners Action’s Mooncake Boxes Recycling Program.  The collected boxes will be processed by the EPD-approved recyclers for local recycling initiatives.
***CUHK Collection Period: 28 September (Monday) – 9 October 2026 (Friday) ***
***Collection Box Location:
G/F lobby, Yasumoto International Academic Park
***
Recycling guidelines: paper and metal boxes are acceptable (please remove any packaging materials and recycle them appropriately)
For enquiries, please contact the Social Responsibility and Sustainable Development Office (3943 3972/
srsdo@cuhk.edu.hk
).

For enquiries, please write to:

Announcements
[Free of charge] UP TO HKD$1000 ALLOWANCE! Assess the safety, efficacy and tolerability of a CUHK proprietary Chinese medicine formula – A 9-month trial targeting patients with diabetes <6-year disease duration and on two or less oral drugs 津貼高達一千港元!以確認香港中文大學研發的專利中藥配方的安全性、療效及耐受性。招募糖尿病人(六年內確診，飲食控制或服用2種或以下口服糖尿藥)參與為期九個月的研究 - Department of Medicine and Therapeutics
From: Maggie Lee
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
maggielee@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
[
新中藥方劑治療
2
型糖尿病的臨床安全性、有效性和多組評價：對
β
細胞功能和胰島素抵抗的影響】
香港中文大學內科及藥物治療學系與香港中文大學香港中西醫結合醫學研究所現正聯合進行一項為期九個月，以內服中藥(沖劑)治療 2 型糖尿病人
 研究對象：18至80歲華人
沒有重大疾病 (例如:心臟病或中風等重大併發症)
沒有服用中藥
身體質量指數 (BMI) ≥18 kg/m²  (公斤 ÷ 米 ÷ 米)
患糖尿病6 年或以下
目前飲食控制或用2種或以下口服糖尿藥 [例如metformin（品牌藥名：Glucophage）或/及 gliclazide（品牌藥名：Diamicron）]
如不確定自己是否患有糖尿病，但具備以下其中一項風險因素，我們會安排你服用葡萄糖飲料（75 克口服葡萄糖耐量試驗）作篩查
糖尿病家族史 (尤其父母或兄弟姐妹在40歲前診斷 )
代謝綜合症 (3高：高血糖，高血壓，高膽固醇)
超重或肥胖
脂肪肝
多囊卵巢綜合症
妊娠糖尿病病史
研究內容：中西醫評估、心電圖、肝纖維化掃描、抽血檢查、填寫問卷、服用研究中藥或安慰劑等
地點：新界沙田威爾斯醫院，舊座，3 樓，3M 病房 - 糖尿及內分泌研究中心
參與研究費用全免，成功參與者可獲得高達港幣 $1,000 的津貼，名額有限，先到先得！
閣下如對本研究有興趣請透過以下連結報名參加：
https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_1EK8XyC5ac5ykiG
如果初步合適參與研究，負責同事將稍後聯絡你，謝謝
如對研究內容有任何疑問，歡迎致電  3505 3897 / 6937 3365 或 WhatsApp 6937 3365與負責研究人員聯絡、查詢詳情。
[Clinical safety, efficacy and multiomic evaluation of a novel Chinese Medicine formula in Type 2 diabetes: Effects on beta-cell function and insulin resistance
.]
Department of Medicine and Therapeutics and Hong Kong Institute of Integrative Medicine, CUHK are jointly conducting a 9-month clinical study on the use of oral Chinese medicine (granule form) for treating type 2 diabetes.
Eligibility Criteria: Ethnic Chinese individuals aged 18 to 80 years
No major illnesses (e.g., heart disease or stroke)
Not taking Chinese medicine
Body Mass Index (BMI) ≥ 18 kg/m² (kg ÷ metre ÷ metre)
Diagnosed with type 2 diabetes within the past 6 years
Diet control alone or taking no more than 2 oral diabetes medications [e.g., metformin (Glucophage®) and/or gliclazide (Diamicron®)]
Not sure if you have diabetes? If you have any of the following risk factors, we can arrange a 75 g Oral Glucose Tolerance Test (OGTT) for diabetes screening
Family history of diabetes (especially if parents or siblings were diagnosed before age of 40)
Metabolic syndrome (three highs: high blood sugar, high blood pressure, high blood cholesterol)
Overweight or obesity
Fatty liver
Polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS)
History of gestational diabetes

Study Procedures: Chinese and Western medical assessments, Electrocardiogram (ECG), Liver fibrosis scan, Blood tests, Questionnaire completion, Taking either the study Chinese medicine or a placebo
Location: Ward 3M, 3/F, Old Block, Diabetes and Endocrinology Research Centre, Prince of Wales Hospital, Sha Tin, New Territories
Free of charge to participate.
Successful participants may receive an allowance of up to HKD $1,000.
Limited quota – first come, first served!
Register via the following link:
https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_1EK8XyC5ac5ykiG
If you are eligible based on initial assessment, our research team will contact you shortly. Thank you!
For inquiries, please contact:
3505 3897 / 6937 3365
WhatsApp: 6937 3365

For enquiries, please write to:

Invitation: “My Heart is Sinking” Photovoice Exhibition | 10–18 October 2026 「My Heart is Sinking」香港巴基斯坦女性攝影發聲展覽｜2026年10月10–18日 - JC School of Public Health and Primary Care
From: Dong Dong
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
dongdong@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
My Heart is Sinking: A Photovoice Exhibition
10–18 October 2026 | 9:00 am–9:00 pm
Quarryside, 20 Hoi Shin Lane, Quarry Bay, Hong Kong
Opening Ceremony: 10 October 2026, 10:30 am–1:30 pm
Members of the CUHK community are warmly invited to visit
My Heart is Sinking
, a photovoice exhibition originating from a two-year community-based research project with Pakistani women in Hong Kong.
Developed through an ongoing academic–community partnership between the C.A.R.E. research team at The Chinese University of Hong Kong, led by Professor Dong DONG, and Pakistani women in Hong Kong, the exhibition invites audiences to explore their lived experiences of migration, emotional struggles, perseverance, and fortitude.
Across five participatory workshops, 73 Pakistani women learned photography and photovoice methods and used photographs and personal narratives to reflect on their migration journeys. Their works explore themes including enduring patience, family caring responsibilities, loss associated with migration, loneliness, and experiences of marginalisation, while also highlighting collective strength, mutual support, and the building of new lives in Hong Kong.
Registration:
https://www.eventbrite.com/e/my-heart-is-sinking-a-photovoice-exhibition-tickets-2002107836434?aff=oddtdtcreator
Admission is free. We warmly welcome colleagues, students, community members, and friends to visit the exhibition and join us at the opening ceremony.
The research on which this exhibition is based was fully supported by a grant from the Research Grants Council of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region, China [Project No. CUHK 14610923].
We gratefully acknowledge the Pakistani women photographers and storytellers who generously shared their images and voices; photographer and artist Faye Yingfei Liang for providing the training; and the Jockey Club S.A.T.H. Project for Healthy Families for its invaluable support throughout the project.

From: Chaplain's Office

各位中大同學、老師及同事, 你好!
誠邀你於 10月5日 出席午間心靈綠洲新系列 「午間心靈絮語」。今次主題是 “Speak to Yourself” 。
新系列由高國雄牧師、盧厚敏博士及音樂主任莫永康每月第一個星期一負責。
我們希望藉着音樂、詩詞與短信息，在忙碌的中午留一段可以停低的時間：
唔使預備好多，亦唔使即時有答案，只係容讓一段旋律、幾句詩詞、一句說話，慢慢行到心靈深處，喚出內心的平靜，也給自己一個回應的空間。
“Speak to Yourself”，係對自己說一句。有時最不容易聽見的，不是別人的聲音，而是自己心底那一句。
無論你是想靜一靜、聽一首歌，或者只是路過坐低，都歡迎同學、老師及員工過來。到時見 !
Dear students, teachers and staff,
You are warmly invited to the new Midday Oasis series, Midday Soul Whispers, on 5 October. This session’s theme is “Speak to Yourself.”
The series is led by Rev.Ko, Dr. Lo Hau-man and Music Officer Edmond Mok.
Through music, poetry and a short reflection, we hope to hold a little space in the middle of a busy day: nothing to prepare, and no answer required. A melody, a few lines of verse, a word or two — enough to reach a little further in, to find some quiet, and perhaps a response of your own.
“Speak to Yourself” is an invitation to say something to yourself. Sometimes the hardest voice to hear is not someone else’s, but the one already waiting inside.
Come if you would like a moment of stillness, a song, or simply a place to sit. Students, teachers and staff are all welcome. See you there !

Mainland Students: Join the Mental Health Mini-Module Study 邀请在港内地学生参与线上心理健康小学堂体验评估研究 - Psychology
From: Han ZHAO
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
hanzhao@link.cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
Invitation to Participate in the JC TourHeart+ Mental Health Mini-Module Study
We are inviting
Mainland Chinese students currently studying in Hong Kong
to take part in a research study evaluating a digital mental health mini-module co-created with Mainland students.
The mini-module covers topics relevant to studying and living in Hong Kong, including
cultural adjustment, interpersonal relationships, academic/research stress, future development, and seeking support
.
You may be eligible if you:
are
18 years old or above
;
are currently an
undergraduate, master's, or doctoral student at a university in Hong Kong
;
are from
Mainland China
; and
can read and understand
Mandarin / Simplified Chinese
.
Participation involves an online baseline questionnaire, a short Zoom orientation, approximately one week of flexible self-guided use of the mini-module, and an online follow-up questionnaire.
Questionnaire Link：
https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_a2Zktui4Uk8GT4y
Please see the Chinese information below and the poster for further details.
诚邀在港内地学生参与
「心导游+」线上心理健康小学堂体验评估研究
在香港读书的你，是否也经历过：
适应新的生活环境、人际关系、学业或科研压力、对未来的思考，或不知道哪里可以寻求支持？
香港中文大学心理学系研究团队与在港内地学生共同创作了一个
「心导游+」线上心理健康小学堂
，希望从同学真实的在港学习与生活经验出发，提供更贴近需要的心理健康资源。
我们现诚邀你亲自体验小学堂，并告诉我们：
它是否好用？内容是否贴近你的经历？哪些地方真正有帮助？还有什么可以做得更好？
你可以参加，如果你：
年满
18 岁
来自
中国内地
目前为香港院校的
本科生、硕士生或博士生
能够阅读及理解
普通话／简体中文
参与过程很简单：
1.
完成网上基线问卷
2.
参加一次简短的
Zoom 线上简介
，了解如何使用「心导游+」
3.
一星期
按自己的时间和需要自由体验小学堂
4.
完成网上随访问卷，分享你的使用感受
你
不需要一次完成所有小学堂内容
，可以按照自己的时间和兴趣自由浏览。
参与酬谢
完成研究后，可获由
「心导游+」提供的纪念品一份（放松减压球）
。
有兴趣参加？
请扫描海报中的二维码报名：
或点击报名链接：
https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_a2Zktui4Uk8GT4y

Recruitment Flyer
Project Title
A cross-cultural perspective on the association between anxiety and independent life skills
What is the study about?
In this study, we are interested in exploring whether and the extent to which independent life skills are associated with problematic behaviours (e.g., alcohol consumption) and mental health challenges (e.g., anxiety)
Who can take part?
You can take part if you are aged 18-25 and an undergraduate student at CUHK and can complete an online English survey independently.
What do we have to do?
You will complete an online English survey include questions about demographic information, educational performance, independent life skills, and mental health. The survey should take approximately 20 minutes.
What will participants receive?
As a token of appreciation for your time, participants will have the opportunity to enter a
PRIZE DRAW
to win a $100 HKD gift card.
One prize will be available for approximately every 10 participants
. If you wish to enter the draw, you will be asked to provide an email address at the end of the survey
Interested?

Unlock Your Potential: Join the CUHK eLearning Student Ambassadors 2026/2027! Registration is NOW open for all CUHK students (UG & PG)  - Information Technology Services Centre (ITSC)
From: Rudi C. (ITSC)
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
rudichow@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
Are you someone who has a strong interest in communication, digital media, publication, information technology, AI trends, and online learning?
Would you like to develop your own multimedia and online portfolio while assisting other fellow students to have a better online learning experience?
If the answer is YES, we would like to invite you to apply and join us to become a
CUHK eLearning Student Ambassador (eLSA)
.
We are seeking applicants (Year 1 - 4 UG students, and all PG students) who are:
Driven to perform a
creative
and
dynamic
role to help fellow students in utilising various eLearning resources (including AI trends and its application in education).
Committed
and
motivated
to learn and improve IT, AI tools, online media, and digital skills to support their studies and future careers.
eLSA programme offers you:
An opportunity to develop digital, media production, IT, communication, organisation and teamwork skills.
Regular trainings that cover the fundamental IT and digital production skills you would need to support the work.
An opportunity to create and showcase your digital and online portfolio. (including CUHK SDP - Student Development Portfolio programme)
A space to contribute innovative ideas and exercise creative thinking to improve the CUHK eLearning environment.
eLSA ambassadors will receive subsidies under the
University’s Campus Work Scheme
.
Please complete the webform at:
https://cloud.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk/webform/view.php?id=13741495
Application deadline
(extended)
: October 3, 2026 - 11.59 PM.
To learn more about eLearning@CUHK, please visit
https://www.cuhk.edu.hk/eLearning
.
For more information, please contact ITSC-EDT via email at:
rudichow@cuhk.edu.hk

From: Li Ching Tung
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to

- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
「跨學科靜觀教學法：以生成式AI與科技促進全人教育中的深度學習與幸福感」項目（2026–2028）現正招募學生助手，協助課堂拍攝工作
工作內容：
- 於課堂期間在室內進行拍攝（包括影片及照片）
- 按指示協助現場基本拍攝工作
申請者須具備：
(i) 自備拍攝設備（小型相機即可，如 Pocket 3 或同類設備均可，無需大型器材）；
(ii) 具備攝影或錄影經驗或興趣；
(iii) 良好的溝通技巧及責任感；
(iv) 細心、準時、可靠；
(v) 能獨立工作，亦具團隊合作精神。
拍攝時間表：
2026年10月7日（星期三） | 18:30 – 20:30 | 李兆基建築學大樓 G01（ARC G01）
2026年10月9日（星期五） | 12:00 – 1:00 pm | 伍宜孫圖書館（研討室）
2026年10月30日（星期五） | 18:30 – 20:30 | 李兆基建築學大樓 G01（ARC G01）
時薪：港幣 $65
有意申請者，請將 1–2 頁 CV 電郵至
chingtungli@cuhk.edu.hk
Ms. Fiona Li，標題請註明 「Application for student helpers」，並列明可協助的日期。
如有任何查詢，歡迎隨時與我聯絡。
謝謝，期待你的參與！
The project "Contemplative Pedagogy Across Disciplines: Enhancing Deep Learning and Wellbeing in Holistic Education with GenAI and Technologies" (2026–2028) is looking for student helper(s) to assist with filming during lessons.
Job Duties:
- Take videos and photo inside the classroom during the lesson
- Assist with basic on-site filming as directed
Applicants of student helper should have:
(i) their own filming device (a small camera is sufficient – a Pocket 3 or similar is perfectly fine; no large equipment is needed);
(ii) some experience or interest in photography or video recording;
(iii) good communication skills and a sense of responsibility;
(iv) attention to detail, punctuality, and reliability;
(v) the ability to work independently as well as in a team.
Filming Schedule:
7 October 2026 (Wed) | 18:30 – 20:30 | ARC G01 (Lee Shau Kee Architecture Building)
9 October 2026 (Fri) | 12:00 – 1:00 pm | Wu Chung Library (Seminar Room)
30 October 2026 (Fri) | 18:30 – 20:30 | ARC G01 (Lee Shau Kee Architecture Building)
Rate: HK$65 per hour
Applicants who are interested in the recruitment, please send an email with a 1–2 page CV titled "Application for student helpers" to
chingtungli@cuhk.edu.hk
Ms Fiona Li, indicating which date(s) you are available.
If you have any questions, please feel free to reach out.
Thank you, and we look forward to hearing from you!
View Count

https://cumassmail.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk
For enquiries, please write to:
http://servicedesk.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk

/weekly/

Appreciating Hong Kong Theatre Through a Critic's Lens 香港劇場專題講座：評論家眼中的香港劇場 - The Office of the Arts Administrator
From: Dorothy Yuen
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
cuoaa@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -

香港劇場專題講座：評論家眼中的香港劇場

由本地資深藝評人陳瑋鑫帶領大家在本地的創意迷霧中疏理分析，認識當代重要創作人及其代表作品，分享戲劇欣賞技巧，幫助你從不同角度了解表演藝術，開啟屬於自己的劇場之旅。
日期：2026.10.07 (三）
⏰ 時間：晚上7時30分
地點：邵逸夫堂大堂
主/合辦單位：中大藝術行政主任辦公室
講者：陳瑋鑫
陳瑋鑫先生現為香港演藝學院表演藝術研究系講師, 他擁有逾十年的高等教育經驗。
陳氏持有香港城市大學創意媒體學院媒體設計及科技藝術碩士學位，以及英國華威大學與塞爾維亞貝爾格萊德藝術大學聯合頒授的國際表演研究雙碩士學位。
他的教學及研究興趣包括表演藝術領域的實踐研究、反思實踐、文獻紀錄、檔案整存和評論寫作。他亦專注於紀錄劇場創作和香港戲劇發展的史學研究。
對象：中大學生、教職員及校友 (FTA成員優先)
費用：免費
查詢：
3943 7528
,
cuoaa@cuhk.edu.hk

https://www.srrsh.cuhk.edu.hk/zh/node/717/

他的教學及研究興趣包括表演藝術領域的實踐研究、反思實踐、文獻紀錄、檔案整存和評論寫作。他亦專注於紀錄劇場創作和香港戲劇發展的史學研究。

2027 年 1 月 10 日（星期日） 0815 – 1230

1. 全日制中大學生
2. 操流利粵語
3. 富責任感
4. 主動性強

6. 樂意團隊合作

Dear students and staff,
Community Inclusion Service Programme: Calling for Team Members
Are you eager to step beyond the campus and connect with the community but unsure where to start? The Community Inclusion Service Programme invites you to embark on a meaningful community engagement journey. Through a variety of themed activities, you will have the chance to interact with persons with intellectual and physical disabilities, fostering mutual understanding and respect while building trust and friendships. Apart from participating in these activities, you will collaborate with fellow students to coordinate extended services and activities to enrich your experience in planning social services and honing valuable skills.
Programme Schedule
1. Briefing session and activity preparation
23 October 2026 (Friday)       1830 – 2030
2. Visit to hostel of persons with intellectual / physical disabilities
7 November 2026 (Saturday)  1000 – 1230
3. Training for special marathon (3KM)
11 November 2026 (Wednesday)       1830 – 2015
18 November 2026 (Wednesday)  1830 – 2015
25 November 2026 (Wednesday)  1830 – 2015
6 January 2027 (Wednesday) 1830 – 2015
4. iRun Special marathon (3KM)
10 January 2027 (Sunday) 0815 – 1230
Target and Requirements
1. Full-time CUHK students
2. Fluent in Cantonese
3. Be responsible
4. Be self-motivated
5. Be passionate in social service
6. Good team player
Quota
10 (selected by interview)
Certificate
A certificate will be awarded upon attendance of 80% of all activities and services

bodyText:
Mass Mail System

2026/10/02
»
Events / Activities
Watoto Children’s Choir Concert | Music & Stories from Uganda  Watoto 兒童合唱團音樂會｜來自烏干達的音樂與故事 - S.H. Ho College
From: S.H. Ho College
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
shhosa@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
Watoto 兒童合唱團音樂會
適逢善衡書院成立20周年，我們非常榮幸邀請到來自烏干達的 Watoto 兒童合唱團，與大家分享一個結合音樂、故事及文化交流的晚上。
一眾年輕表演者將透過歌唱、舞蹈及親身故事，與大家分享他們的經歷，以及對未來的盼望。以 「Better Days – There is Hope」 為主題，是晚除了合唱團演出及分享，亦設有攤位及互動活動，讓大家與表演者交流，感受不同文化。
活動詳情
日期
2026年11月2日（星期一）
時間
6:30–6:45PM – 接待及登記
7:00–8:15PM – Watoto 兒童合唱團演出及分享
8:15–9:00PM – 攤位及交流*
地點
香港中文大學 善衡書院陳震夏館（多用途禮堂）
主題
Better Days – There is Hope
語言
英語
*音樂會結束後，攤位及交流活動將於晚上8:15至9:00進行。參加者可自由參觀攤位、與參與者交流，並可按個人安排於此時段內隨時離開。
報名
歡迎所有中大教職員及學生參加。請於**2026年10月15日（星期四）**或以前透過以下連結報名。
立即報名
（名額有限，先到先得；座位不設劃位。）
* 所有參加者請
攜帶中大教職員／學生證（
CU Link Card）
，以安排進場。
如欲了解更多詳情，請參閱
[
活動網頁
]
。
Watoto Children’s Choir Concert
As part of the 20th Anniversary celebrations of S.H. Ho College, we are delighted to present an evening of music, stories and cultural exchange with a special performance by the Watoto Children’s Choir from Uganda.
The internationally renowned group of young performers will share messages of hope and resilience through music, dance and personal stories. The concert, themed “Better Days – There is Hope”, will offer an inspiring evening of music and stories.
Event Details
Date
2 November 2026 (Monday)
Time
6:30-6:45 PM  –  Reception
7:00-8:15 PM  –  Watoto Children’s Choir Concert & Sharing
8:15-9:00 PM  –  Booths and Engagement Activities*
Venue
Chan Chun Ha Hall (Dining Hall), S.H. Ho College, CUHK
Theme
Better Days - There is Hope
Language
English
* Following the concert, booths and engagement activities will be available from 8:15 PM to 9:00 PM. Guests are welcome to explore the booths and interact with the participants at their leisure and may depart at any time during this period according to their own arrangements.
Registration
All CUHK staff and students are welcome to join. Please register via the link below by 15 October 2026 (Thu).
[Register Now]
(Limited seats; first come, first served.) (Free seating.)
*All attendees are kindly reminded to
bring their CU Link card
for entry to the event.
For more details, please visit the
[event webpage]
.

bodyText:

2026/10/02

Announcements
聽講座送紀念品 醫護行社區藥房分享會：認識社區藥房服務 Sharing by HIA Community Pharmacy: Understanding Community Pharmacy Services   - The Jockey Club School of Public Health and Primary Care
From: The Jockey Club S.A.T.H. Project for Healthy Families (JCSATH)
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
jcsath@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -

醫護行社區藥房分享會：認識社區藥房服務

您有沒有想過，藥劑師除了配藥之外，還可以如何支援您和家人的健康？
誠邀您參加由
醫護行者（
Health In Action, HIA
）社區藥房
藥劑師主講的分享會，了解社區藥房如何透過不同服務協助您及家人管理健康，成為您值得信賴的社區健康夥伴。

日期：
2026年10月16日（星期五）

時間：
下午2時至3時

地點：
鰂魚涌海濱活動空間 Quarryside 活動室 1 至 3（鰂魚涌海新里20號）

語言：
英語

講者：
醫護行社區藥房藥劑師

名額：
20人
您將會了解：
藥劑師在基層醫療中的角色
社區藥房提供的服務
藥物安全使用及藥物管理知識
輕微疾病及慢性疾病管理支援服務
藥劑師如何成為您可靠的社區健康夥伴
醫護行者相信，社區藥房可以成為大眾接觸醫療服務的重要第一站。透過健康教育、藥物管理及社區藥房服務，藥劑師能協助個人及家庭掌握健康資訊，促進身心健康。
本活動適合多元文化社群人士、社區工作者、照顧者，以及有興趣了解香港醫療服務的公眾人士參加。

報名連結：
https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_3QnJthMMwdTKD2K

名額有限，先到先得。成功報名者將收到
WhatsApp
確認訊息。

成功報名並出席活動者，將獲贈精美紀念品乙份
‼
⭐
期待與您見面，一同了解社區藥房服務如何協助建立更健康的社區！
JCSATH

Sharing by HIA Community Pharmacy: Understanding Community Pharmacy Services

Have you ever wondered how pharmacists can support your health beyond dispensing medicines?
Join us for an informative sharing session by a pharmacist from
Health In Action (HIA) Community Pharmacy
and learn how community pharmacy services can support you and your family in maintaining good health.

Date:
16 October 2026 (Friday)

Time:
2 p.m. - 3 p.m.

Venue:
Activity Room 1–3, Quarryside, 20 Hoi Shin Lane, Quarry Bay

Language:
English

Speaker:
Pharmacist from Health In Action Community Pharmacy

Quota:
20 participants
What will you learn?
The role of pharmacists in primary healthcare
Services provided by community pharmacies
Safe use of medications and medication management
Support available for minor ailments and chronic disease management
How pharmacists can become your trusted community health partners
Health In Action believes that community pharmacies can serve as an important first point of contact for healthcare services. Through health education, medication management, and community-based pharmacy services, pharmacists play an important role in helping individuals and families stay healthy and informed.
This session is suitable for members of multicultural communities, community workers, caregivers, and anyone interested in learning more about healthcare services in Hong Kong.

Register here:
https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_3QnJthMMwdTKD2K
Places are limited and will be allocated on a
first-come, first-served basis
. Successful registrants will receive a WhatsApp confirmation message.

Successfully registered participants who attend the event will receive a special souvenir!
‼⭐
We look forward to seeing you and exploring how pharmacists can support healthier communities together!
JCSATH

bodyText:

»
Announcements
Update on enhancement to VeriGuide Assignment Submission Service from Academic Year 2026-27  - The VeriGuide Team, Department of Computer Science and Engineering
From: Kevin Lam
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
veriguide@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
Following our previous announcements, we are pleased to inform you that the integration of Turnitin originality checking into VeriGuide was successfully launched on
1 October 2026
.
As you use this new academic integrity enhancement, please note the following key information:
Automatic originality checking:
All student course assignments submitted via VeriGuide, including those submitted through Blackboard integration, will automatically undergo Turnitin originality checking.
Submission workflow and EULA:
The submission process remains largely unchanged. Students are required to accept the Turnitin End-User License Agreement (EULA) during the upload process before their submissions can be processed.
Originality Report access for instructors:
Instructors can access Turnitin Originality Reports through the existing VeriGuide service to support academic integrity review and assessment.
For further information about the Turnitin-VeriGuide integration, including user guidance and frequently asked questions, please visit the information webpage:
https://academic2.veriguide.org/cuhk/documents/vg_turnitin_page/
Should you have any questions or encounter any issues, please contact Mr Patrick Lau (Email:
tplau@cuhk.edu.hk
; Tel:
3943 9457
).
Thank you for your continued support and cooperation.
繼我們先前的公告之後，我們很高興地通知您，VeriGuide已於
2026年10月1日
成功整合Turnitin原創性偵測功能。
在使用這項新的學術誠信強化功能時，請注意以下重要資訊：
自動原創性偵測：
所有學生透過VeriGuide提交的課程作業，包括透過Blackboard整合提交的作業，都將自動進行Turnitin原創性偵測。
提交流程和終端使用者授權合約 (EULA)：
提交流程大致維持不變。學生在上傳過程中必須接受Turnitin終端使用者授權合約 (EULA)，其提交的作業才能被處理。
教師查閱原創性報告：
教師可以透過現有的VeriGuide服務存取Turnitin原創性報告，以輔助學術誠信的審查和評估。
有關此項整合的進一步資訊，包括用戶指南和常見問題，請瀏覽資訊網頁：
https://academic2.veriguide.org/cuhk/documents/vg_turnitin_page/
如有任何疑問或遇到任何問題，請聯絡劉先生（電子郵件：
tplau@cuhk.edu.hk
；電話：
3943 9457
）。
感謝您的持續支持與合作。
继此前发布公告后，我们很高兴地通知您，VeriGuide系统已于
2026年10月1日
成功整合Turnitin原创性检测功能。
在使用这项旨在提升学术诚信的新功能时，请注意以下要点：
自动原创性检测：
所有通过VeriGuide提交的学生课程作业，包括经由Blackboard整合提交的作业，均会自动进行 Turnitin 原创性检测。
提交流程与最终用户许可协议 (EULA)：
提交流程基本保持不变。学生在上传作业时，须先接受Turnitin最终用户许可协议 (EULA)，方可完成提交。
教师查阅原创性报告：
教师可通过现有的VeriGuide服务查阅Turnitin原创性报告，以辅助学术诚信审查与评估工作。
如需了解关于此次整合的更多信息（包括用户指南及常见问题解答），请访问相关网页：
https://academic2.veriguide.org/cuhk/documents/vg_turnitin_page/
如有任何疑问或遇到问题，请联系刘先生（电邮：
tplau@cuhk.edu.hk
；电话：
3943 9457
）。
感谢您一贯的支持与配合。

For request submissions, please submit them at
https://cumassmail.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk
For enquiries, please write to:
http://servicedesk.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk

/weekly/

您知道嗎？腸道的功能不僅僅是消化食物！腸道微生物群（Gut Microbiome）對我們的身體健康、心理健康、免疫力、睡眠質素以及整體生活質素都擔當著重要角色。研究顯示，我們的飲食習慣、睡眠質素、運動量，甚至壓力水平，都會影響腸道健康。
誠邀您參加這個內容豐富且實用的健康講座，一同了解如何透過簡單的生活習慣，促進腸道健康，提升整體身心健康。

Trust Your Gut: From Early Life to Everyday Wellbeing
Did you know that your gut does much more than digest food? The gut microbiome plays an important role in our physical health, mental wellbeing, immunity, sleep, and overall quality of life. Research shows that what we eat, how we sleep, how active we are, and even our stress levels can influence our gut health.
Join us for an informative and practical health talk to learn how simple lifestyle choices can support a healthier gut and improve overall wellbeing.
Learn what the gut microbiome is and how it is established in early life

Announcements
Join Countryside Conservation! Come to Play YTT ARchive Web App  齊來響應鄉郊保育！YTT ARchive 網頁版，與 AR 動物互動拍照！ - Department of Geography and Resource Management
From: Cherry Lau
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
cherrylau123@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
齊來響應鄉郊保育！YTT ARchive 網頁版，與 AR 動物互動拍照！
YTT ARchive Web App has launched!!
On the occasion of the 2nd anniversary of the “Exploring YTT Nature ARchive” project, we are delighted to present a special gift to everyone on this special day.
YTT ARchive combines AR technology with interactive features to let you explore the natural ecology of Yim Tin Tsai anytime and anywhere. This web version makes it accessible to everyone, you can feel free to interact with AR animals, take photos, and enjoy a festive experience!
Key Features:
Fun Animal Facts: Discover unique habits and fascinating trivia about different species, to deepen your ecological knowledge.
Augmented Reality Photo Experience: In addition to standard photo-taking, the web also supports selfie mode, allowing you to capture memorable moments together with AR animals, making the experience even more fun!
Visit now:
https://yttarchive.ust.hk/
Explore the wonders of Yim Tin Tsai’s ecosystem and celebrate the festival with AR animals!
適逢「智遊自在鹽田梓」項目成立兩週年，我們誠意為大家送上一份特別禮物
YTT ARchive 網上版應用程式正式登場！！
https://yttarchive.ust.hk/
YTT ARchive 是由香港中文大學地理與資源管理學系及香港科技大學綜合系統與設計學部合作開發，結合AR技術與互動功能，讓您隨時隨地探索西貢鹽田梓的自然生態故事。
以往YTT ARchive手機應用程式需要特定手機型號才能下載。現在，網頁版讓所有人隨時隨地都能使用，與 AR 動物互動拍照，真正全民皆用，人月兩團圓！
核心特色：
動物趣事知多少：點擊即可了解不同動物的獨特習性與趣事，深入認識生態知識。
擴增實境拍照體驗：將 AR 動物放置於您的環境中，欣賞生動的動物模型，並隨光照變化呈現真實陰影效果。除了普通拍照，網頁還支援自拍模式，讓您與 AR 動物合照留念，更添趣味。
立即進入
https://yttarchive.ust.hk/
探索鹽田梓生態系統的奇妙世界，與 AR 動物共度佳節！
注意：
此網頁為手機App的精簡版，提供 AR 簡單拍照功能，讓無法下載手機應用程式的用家仍能體驗部分AR 內容。若想體驗完整功能（如 GPS 動物尋寶、互動問答等），請下載全功能版手機應用程式：
https://www.yttnaturearchive.org/ar/ar
══════════
關於我們 About the Project
本項目【智遊自在鹽田梓 Exploring YTT Nature ARchive】（全稱：「西貢鹽田梓生態保育應用研究：擴增模型與智能體驗式參與」）於2024年9月正式開始，為期三年，旨在運用擴增實境技術展示鹽田梓的生物多樣性，將智能科技融入島上自然保育與鄉郊復育工作。
"Exploring YTT Nature ARchive" is a three‑year project (2024–2027) that integrates Augmented Reality (AR) technology with nature conservation and rural revitalisation on Yim Tin Tsai Island. It aims to enhance public awareness and interest in the island's biodiversity through innovative technology and experiential learning.
資助單位 Funders: 鄉郊保育資助計劃、鄉郊保育辦公室 Countryside Conservation Funding Scheme (CCFS), Countryside Conservation Office (CCO)
主辦單位 Organiser: 香港中文大學地理與資源管理學系 Department of Geography and Resource Management
協辦/支持單位 Partners：香港科技大學綜合系統與設計學部、香港戶外生態教育協會、鹽田梓村委會、鹽光保育中心 HKUST Division of Integrative Systems and Design, Outdoor Wildlife Learning Hong Kong (OWLHK), Yim Tin Tsai Village Committee, Salt and Light Preservation Centre

http://www.yttnaturearchive.org

https://www.facebook.com/yttnaturearchive

資助單位 Funders: 鄉郊保育資助計劃、鄉郊保育辦公室 Countryside Conservation Funding Scheme (CCFS), Countryside Conservation Office (CCO) 主辦單位 Organiser: 香港中文大學地理與資源管理學系 Department of Geography and Resource Management 協辦/支持單位 Partners：香港科技大學綜合系統與設計學部、香港戶外生態教育協會、鹽田梓村委會、鹽光保育中心 HKUST Division of Integrative Systems and Design, Outdoor Wildlife Learning Hong Kong (OWLHK), Yim Tin Tsai Village Committee, Salt and Light Preservation Centre Website: http://www.yttnaturearchive.org Facebook: 智遊自在鹽田梓 Exploring YTT Nature ARchive https://www.facebook.com/yttnaturearchive Instagram: @yttnaturearchive https://www.instagram.com/yttnaturearchive https://cumassmail.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk http://servicedesk.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk

Stephen Kotkin Lecture: Winning the War, Losing the Peace? A Preview of Stalin Vol. III 《斯大林》作者Stephen Kotkin（科特金）講座預告 - CUP
From: Leung King Hung
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
khleung@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
We are pleased to invite you to our upcoming Lecture "Winning the War, Losing the Peace? A Preview of Stalin Vol. III" by Professor Stephen Kotkin at The Chinese University of Hong Kong on October 12, 2026 (Monday).
Professor Stephen Kotkin is a Senior Fellow at Freeman Spogli Institute for International Studies of Stanford University and the Birkelund Professor in History and International Affairs Emeritus at Princeton University. A renowned scholar of nineteenth- and twentieth-century Russian, Eastern European, and Eurasian history, he is the author of numerous influential works, including Stalin: Paradoxes of Power, 1878–1928, Magnetic Mountain: Stalinism as a Civilization, and Armageddon Averted: The Soviet Collapse, 1970–2000. The Chinese edition of Stalin was published by the Chinese University of Hong Kong Press in 2023, with the second volume to be released in 2027.
As an esteemed author with The Chinese University of Hong Kong Press, we hope that Professor Kotkin's lecture will provide a valuable opportunity for scholarly exchange in Hong Kong.
10月12日（星期一）下午，《斯大林》作者、斯坦福大學胡佛研究所克萊因海茲（Kleinheinz）高級研究員Stephen Kotkin（斯蒂芬・科特金） 將蒞臨香港中文大學，公開講座。
Kotkin教授是20世紀蘇聯歷史的重量級學者，致力研究斯大林時代，和蘇聯政治史。他將在本次講座中，分享正在撰寫的《斯大林》第三卷，從跨度更長的歷史脈絡出發，延續對這位歷史人物及蘇聯的學術研究。
同時，我們也很高興正式預告：《斯大林》第二卷即將由香港中文大學出版社出版。

2026/10/02

Announcements
Second round of recruitment!!Free Training・Paid Internship! Join Us as a Project Ambassador in Yim Tin Tsai, Sai Kung 【智遊自在鹽田梓】第二屆項目大使加推第二輪招募！把握機會報名 - Department of Geography and Resource Management
From: Cherry Lau
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
cherrylau123@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
【智遊自在鹽田梓】第二屆項目大使加推第二輪招募！把握機會報名
Call for YTT Countryside Conservation Project Ambassadors! The Second Round of Recruitment is now open!!
熱愛大自然？或是對客家文化與天主教深感興趣？機會來了！
為讓更多年青人有機會參與保育，「智遊自在鹽田梓」團隊決定加開第二輪申請，並專為不參與導賞工作的同學而設。
無論你擅長寫作、攝影、拍片、畫畫、設計、研究，還是想在幕後默默支持鄉郊保育，都歡迎你報名，成為項目大使的一分子！

成為項目大使
，你可以：
· 協助社交媒體推廣、內容創作及設計
· 支援活動籌備及現場協助
· 參與學術研究、數據整理及生態紀錄
·
優先報名參加項目活動，活動船費全免！
Love nature? Curious about Hakka culture and Catholicism? This is your opportunity!
"Exploring YTT Nature ARchive" is now recruiting for its second cohort (2026/2027) of Project Ambassadors. The programme is free to join, and you will receive free training and a certificate upon completion. Be part of our ecological conservation and community guiding efforts.
The first round of our ambassador recruitment received an overwhelming response, and we are delighted to see so many students eager to support our cause. To give more students the opportunity to participate in conservation, we have decided to open a second round of applications, specifically designed for students who do not wish to take part in guided tours.
Whether you excel in writing, photography, video production, drawing, design, or research, or simply wish to support countryside conservation behind the scenes. We welcome you to apply and become part of our team of Project Ambassadors!

As a Project Ambassador, you can:
Assist with social media promotion, content creation, and design
Support event preparation and on-site assistance
Participate in academic research, data collection, and ecological recording
Enjoy priority registration for project activities, with ferry fares fully covered!
參與資格 Eligibility：
• 必須為香港中文大學在讀學生（本科生及碩士生均可）Current CUHK student (both undergraduate and postgraduate students are welcome)
• 對生態、客家文化、導賞或保育有興趣 Interest in ecology, Hakka culture, guided tours, or conservation
• 粵語流利，具英語能力更佳 Fluent in Cantonese (English proficiency is an advantage)
• 不怕坐船，熱愛戶外活動 Comfortable with outdoor activities
計劃日程 Programme Schedule：
• 面試 Interview： October 2026 (via Zoom)
• 網上理論課 Online Training： October – November 2026
• 實地考察 Field Visit：Early – Mid of November 2026 (Yim Tin Tsai Island)
截止報名 Application Deadline: 10 October 2026 (Saturday) 23:59
報名表格 Join Us Now
：
https://forms.gle/Wxug16m9pCyBRdXZ6
Enquiries：Cherry Lau (Project Manager)
cherrylau123@cuhk.edu.hk
══════════
關於我們 About the Project
本項目【智遊自在鹽田梓 Exploring YTT Nature ARchive】（全稱：「西貢鹽田梓生態保育應用研究：擴增模型與智能體驗式參與」）於2024年9月正式開始，為期三年，旨在運用擴增實境技術展示鹽田梓的生物多樣性，將智能科技融入島上自然保育與鄉郊復育工作。
"Exploring YTT Nature ARchive" is a three‑year project (2024–2027) that integrates Augmented Reality (AR) technology with nature conservation and rural revitalisation on Yim Tin Tsai Island. It aims to enhance public awareness and interest in the island's biodiversity through innovative technology and experiential learning.
資助單位 Funders: 鄉郊保育資助計劃、鄉郊保育辦公室 Countryside Conservation Funding Scheme (CCFS), Countryside Conservation Office (CCO)
主辦單位 Organiser: 香港中文大學地理與資源管理學系 Department of Geography and Resource Management
協辦/支持單位 Partners：香港科技大學綜合系統與設計學部、香港戶外生態教育協會、鹽田梓村委會、鹽光保育中心 HKUST Division of Integrative Systems and Design, Outdoor Wildlife Learning Hong Kong (OWLHK), Yim Tin Tsai Village Committee, Salt and Light Preservation Centre
Website:
http://www.yttnaturearchive.org
Facebook: 智遊自在鹽田梓 Exploring YTT Nature ARchive
Instagram: @yttnaturearchive
View Count
For request submissions, please submit them at
https://cumassmail.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk
For enquiries, please write to:
http://servicedesk.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk
Copyright © 2013. All Rights Reserved. The Chinese University of Hong Kong.
/weekly/

title: Contemplative Workshop Series | Free of charge 靜觀工作坊系列 | 費用全免
bodyText:
Mass Mail System
Mass Mail System
Digest of CUHK Mass Mails for Undergraduate Students
»
2026/10/02
»
Announcements
Contemplative Workshop Series | Free of charge 靜觀工作坊系列 | 費用全免 - Department of Educational Administration and Policy
From: Ng Tsz Ying
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
1155258073@link.cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
靜觀工作坊系列
對象：歡迎所有職員及學生（職員及學生名額各設上限）
主要語言：廣東話
地點：何添樓G6室

費用全免
芳香療法工作坊
透過靜觀嗅聞與觀察，探索精油的舒緩力量。本工作坊將帶您運用感官，認識芳香療法的基礎知識，並體驗香氣如何促進放鬆與身心健康。
日期及時間：2026年11月13日（星期五）12：30–14：00
名額：15位

建議穿著輕便服裝

請自備潔手工具
探索內在之旅：明陣靜觀步行工作坊
在明陣步道上緩緩行走，讓身心回歸當下。本工作坊邀請您靜下心來，專注於每一步，向內反思。無需任何經驗，只需帶著開放的心前來。
日期及時間：2026年11月20日（星期五）14：00–15：30
名額：15位
活動安排： 將先於室內進行簡短講解，然後移師戶外進行靜觀步行。

建議穿著輕便服裝

請自備飲用水
園藝治療工作坊
通過插乾花與大自然連結。本工作坊將帶您靜心創作屬於自己的乾花作品，體驗植物帶來的療癒與平靜。完成後可將作品帶回家，延續這份靜觀體驗。
日期及時間：2026年11月19日（星期四）12：30–14：00
名額：15位

建議穿著輕便服裝
本活動由香港中文大學教學發展及語言培訓基金 (TDLEG) 贊助
如有查詢，請聯絡李小姐（
chingtungli@cuhk.edu.hk
）
Contemplative Workshop Series
Target audience: Welcome to all staff and students(a quota is set for staff and students respectively)
Language: Cantonese
Venue: Ho Tim Building, Room G6

Free of charge
Aromatherapy Workshop
Explore the calming power of essential oils through mindful smelling and observation. In this hands-on workshop, you will engage your senses, learn about aromatherapy basics, and experience how scents can support ax.
Date & Time: 13 November 2026 (Friday), 12:30 – 14:00
Quota: 15 participants

Suggested to wear casual/comfortable clothing

Please bring personal hand-sanitizing materials
Journey Within: A Labyrinth and Mindful Walking Workshop
Take a slow, mindful walk along the labyrinth path. This workshop invites you to quiet your mind, focus on your steps, and reflect inwardly. No prior experience is needed, just come with an open heart.
Date & Time: 20 November 2026 (Friday), 14:00 – 15:30
Quota: 15 participants
Activity Arrangement: The workshop will begin with a short indoor briefing, followed by the mindfulness walking practice outdoors.

Suggested to wear casual/comfortable clothing

Please bring your own drinking water
Horticultural Therapy Workshop
Connect with nature through the art of dried flower arrangement. In this workshop, you will mindfully create your own dried flower piece while experiencing the calming and therapeutic benefits of working with plants. Take your handmade creation home as a reminder of your practice.
Date & Time: 19 November 2026 (Thursday), 12:30 – 14:00
Quota: 15 participants

Suggested to wear casual/comfortable clothing
This activity is sponsored by the Teaching Development and Language Enhancement Grant (TDLEG) of The Chinese University of Hong Kong.
For enquiries, please contact Miss Fiona Li (
chingtungli@cuhk.edu.hk
)
View Count
For request submissions, please submit them at
https://cumassmail.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk
For enquiries, please write to:
http://servicedesk.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk
Copyright © 2013. All Rights Reserved. The Chinese University of Hong Kong.
/weekly/

will be held at

The Student Seminar will feature presentations of the awardees’ papers and visual representations, followed by an Award Presentation Ceremony to recognize their achievements. We are honored to have Professor Irwin KING Kuo-chin, Pro-Vice-Chancellor / Vice-President (Education), to be the guest of honor officiating at the Award Presentation Ceremony.
Event Name:

Student Seminar – Papers presented in Cantonese, Putonghua or English

|

About the Awards
In previous years, the General Education Best Essay Award provided students enrolled in the two foundation courses— “In Dialogue with Humanity” and “In Dialogue with Nature”— with a platform to submit their term papers and compete for Gold, Silver, and Bronze Awards. Starting from 2023-24, the new General Education Award for Best Expository Writing has extended to writings from all General Education courses, including GE Foundation courses, Four-Area courses as well as College GE courses. Additionally, a new General Education Award for Best Visual Representation, sponsored by a fund in memory of the late Professor T-C Chen, an advocate of general education who served for some years as Head of United College, Professor of Computer Science and Electronics, and Chairman of the Department of Computer Science, has been established, inviting submissions of visual representations with connections to General Education courses. Both Awards are open to all writings and visual representations related to General Education courses offered in the academic years 2023-24 and 2024-25. There are three categories of top awards: Gold (HK$ 5,000 each), Silver (HK$ 3,000 each) and Bronze Awards (HK$1000 each).
For more information, please visit:

Announcements
Leadership Psychology Study Participants Recruitment 【Finish Online Studies and Get 100 HKD!】 【完成線上研究，可獲HKD100報酬！】誠意邀請香港小學生及家長參與領導力相關心理學研究 - Gender Studies Programme
From: HE Chuting
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
conniehe@link.cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
你想了解孩子對於學校或日常生活裡的“領導”的看法嗎？想知道孩子對於“當領導”的意願嗎？不要錯過這次有趣又有意義的研究機會。簡單進行線上研究，還有報酬可領喔~~
招募對象
：
在香港男女共校的小學就讀小1到小6的小學生以及其父親或母親
目前各個組別依舊在積極招募，各個組別依舊席位多多！誠摯邀請合乎要求的小朋友同家長參與~~如果你們身邊有合乎要求的小朋友和家長，也懇請幫我們多多宣傳~~
研究項目：
小學生、家長及老師的領導認知與刻板印象
研究內容（全程以中文進行）：
1.孩子：1對1線上訪談（需錄音），約需1小時。
2.家長：填寫1份網上問卷，約需1小時。
報酬：
家長和孩子完成各自的研究項目後，可獲得共100港幣報酬。
參與條件：
1.兒童參加者為在香港就讀男女共校的小學的小1到小6的小學生，家長參加者為該兒童的父親或母親。
2.兒童能講流利廣東話或普通話，家長能閱讀和書寫中文。
3.兒童可使用有互聯網、視頻和音頻功能的電腦或平板參與研究。
4.兒童沒有主要的身體障礙（如：視障、四肢不健全）和未被診斷有任何有關精神健康或主要的發展障礙的狀況（如：自閉症、過度活躍、讀寫障礙）。
5.請留意參加者需在此前沒有參與過本研究的“預實驗”或“教師部分”（如不清楚是否參與過也可先留下聯繫方式，稍後我們的研究人員將與您聯繫進行確認）。
如對本實驗感興趣，請通過以下鏈接報名
，我們的研究人員將盡快聯繫您：https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_6KzWB6HhTtOhwou
參與純屬自願性質，所收集的資料只作研究用途及保密處理。如有任何疑問，請聯繫何小姐（conniehe@link.cuhk.edu.hk)。
We are inviting Hong Kong primary school students and parents to participate in a leadership cognition study.
Child:
One-on-one online interview (will be recorded), approximately 1 hour.
Parent:
Online questionnaire, approximately 1 hour.
Compensation:
Participants will receive HKD 100 in total.
View Count
For request submissions, please submit them at
https://cumassmail.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk
For enquiries, please write to:
http://servicedesk.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk
