題目：
《人間福報》與星雲大師人間佛教的實踐
時間：10月6日 | 週二 10：00 - 12：00
講者：楊錦郁博士 | 美國花藝設計學院（AFAS）教授
主持：陳劍鍠教授 | 香港中文大學人間佛教研究中心主任
形式：現場講座 & ZOOM網絡會議
地點：香港中文大學馮景禧樓 & 會議ID: 964 5779 7423，密碼: 999999
報名：https://cloud.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk/webform/view.php?id=13741295
演講簡介：
星雲大師一生以文字和語言弘揚佛法，從平面媒體用到電子媒體，跨域跨國，法水長流五大洲。2000年，他創辦《人間福報》，我那時任職聯合報副刊，奉報社之命專訪星雲大師談辦報緣起，文刊創刊當日聯副。其後兼《人間福報》藝文組主任，應聘擔任《人間福報》總監，於大師人間佛教的思想理念及其實踐，多所體會。此其間並長期為副刊撰寫專欄，結集5本散文專書。
Throughout his life, Venerable Master Hsing Yun propagated the Dharma through both the written and spoken word, utilizing mediums ranging from print to electronic media. His efforts crossed boundaries and transnational lines, spreading the water of the Dharma across five continents. In 2000, the Master founded The Merit Times. At that time, while working for the literary supplement of the United Daily News, I was commissioned by the newspaper to interview Venerable Master Hsing Yun regarding his vision for establishing the paper. The interview was published in the United Daily News literary supplement on the very day of The Merit Times’ inaugural issue. Later, I concurrently served as the Director of the Arts and Literature Section and was invited to become the Managing Director of The Merit Times, which granted me profound insights into the conceptual framework and practical application of the Master's Humanistic Buddhism. During this period, I also contributed long-running columns to the literary supplement, which were eventually compiled into five distinct prose volumes.
嘉賓簡介：
楊錦郁博士，散文家、媒體人，淡江大學中文系博士，美國花藝設計學院（AFAS）教授，曾任職聯合報副刊組、人間福報總監。著有多部人物報導集及散文集《遠方有光》、《穿過一樹的夜光》、《好時光》、《小西巷》、《霧中恆河》、《花希望成為自己的樣子》，論著《呂碧城文學與思想》等。曾獲中興文藝獎章、中山文藝創作獎，磺溪文學獎特別貢獻獎。

時間：10月5日 | 週一 14:30 - 16:30
講者：李瑞騰教授 | 中央大學中文系榮譽教授
主持：陳劍鍠教授 | 香港中文大學人間佛教研究中心主任

演講簡介：
星雲大師於1949年春率僧侶救護隊來臺，先到臺南，然後北上臺中、臺北，流離奔波，無處掛單，後落腳於中壢圓光寺，展開他在臺灣最初的艱困歲月，期間曾被逮捕拘禁，蒙難23天；曾赴苗栗法雲寺看守山林、到新竹靈隱寺協助臺灣青年佛教講習會，並開始執筆為文，參與佛教刊物的編輯工作，積累下一個階段在宜蘭弘法的文化資本。處境艱難，青年星雲法師如何肆應？
In the spring of 1949, Venerable Master Hsing Yun arrived in Taiwan leading the Buddhist Sangha Rescue Team. He initially traveled to Tainan, and later ventured north to Taichung and Taipei. Displaced, wandering, and finding no monastic shelter to lodge, he eventually settled at Yuanuang Temple in Zhongli, marking the beginning of his initial grueling years in Taiwan. 題目：
編者的凝視：從《星雲大師全集》看大師的寫作身影與文學世界
時間：10月5日 | 週一 10:00 - 12:00
講者：蔡孟樺院長 | 佛光山人間佛教研究院副院長
主持：陳劍鍠教授 | 香港中文大學人間佛教研究中心主任
形式：現場講座 & ZOOM網絡會議
地點：香港中文大學馮景禧樓 & 會議ID: 964 5779 7423，密碼: 999999
報名：https://cloud.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk/webform/view.php?id=13741074
演講簡介：
《星雲大師全集》高達395冊、逾四千萬字，不僅是當代人間佛教的百科全書，更是研究星雲大師文學世界最核心的文獻寶庫。本講座由《全集》主編的視角開啟，跳脫傳統學術理論的論述，從最微觀、最前線的編纂實務出發，希望與聽者一起重返大師創作的歷史現場，進入大師創作的初衷。在搜集與校勘過程中，編者得以穿梭時空，「近距離」凝視大師從青年詩歌小說到晚年口述隨筆的寫作身影。講座將分享親侍大師的微觀體感，透過筆觸細節讀出文字背後的呼吸與慈悲神情，為人間佛教文學研究開闢溫暖而深邃的新視野。
Spanning 395 volumes and over 40 million words, The Complete Works of Venerable Master Hsing Yun serves not only as a contemporary encyclopedia of Humanistic Buddhism but also as the most critical archival treasure trove for studying the Master's literary world. Opening from the unique perspective of the Editor-in-Chief of The Complete Works, this lecture moves beyond traditional academic theories. Instead, it begins with the most micro-level and frontline practices of compilation, inviting the audience to return to the historical scenes of the Master’s creations and enter his original intent. Through the processes of collection and collation, the editor was able to traverse time and space, observing the Master’s writing style "at close range"—from his youthful poetry and novels to his oral dictations and essays in his later years. This lecture will share the speaker's personal experience of closely serving the Master. By examining subtle details in his writing, the lecture reads the breath and compassionate expressions behind the words, opening up a warm and profound new horizon for the study of Humanistic Buddhism literature.
嘉賓簡介：
蔡孟樺，資深佛教出版人，現任佛光山人間佛教研究院副院長、《人間佛教學報．藝文》主編。13歲皈依星雲大師，佛光山叢林學院畢業並於佛光大學文學研究所進修。歷任佛光山法堂書記、《人間福報》副刊主編與香海文化執行長，編輯出版大師著作百餘本，並主編《百年佛緣》、《獻給旅行者365日》、《人間佛教佛陀本懷》等。2016年銜師命擔綱《星雲大師全集》主編。長期致力於人間佛教思想的傳播與出版。

bodyText:

Announcements
【$200 Coupon】Recruiting Children (aged under 33 months) for the Gut Microbiome and At-risk Children's Brain Development Study 誠意邀請33個月或以下兒童參加腸道微生態與兒童大腦發展及風險研究 - Department of Psychiatry
From: Dr. WONG Wing Ho, Oscar
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
hatch@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
家長您好，我們是香港中文大學醫學院精神科學系的研究團隊。本研究由香港中文大學醫學院精神科學系、內科及藥物治療學系統籌。
本研究團隊誠邀3歲以下兒童參與一項有關腸道微生態與兒童大腦發展及風險研究。此研究希望透過收集小朋友之大便及口腔樣本，幫助了解腸道微生態與大腦發展的關係。
研究對象:
1) 確診/懷疑小朋友有自閉症傾向或其他發展問題
2) 33個月或以下的小朋友 (交齊問卷和樣本的日子未滿3歲即可)
3) 父母皆為華裔或亞裔人士
4) 小朋友18歲以下的兄弟姊妹
以下為是次研究需要完成的事項：
1) 簽署參加同意書
2) 網上問卷調查：網上問卷主要詢問小朋友的行為及腸道情況，填寫時間約45分鐘
3) 收集大便和口腔樣本：我們會給家長一個樣本收集包，請家長使用收集包內的物在家中資協助收集樣本
4) 飲食習慣的問卷：記錄小朋友的飲食習慣
完成研究後，參加者可以獲得$200的超市現金券、 G-NiiB益生菌試用裝和腸道健康報告作為答謝 另外，家長有機會被邀請進行面談並隨訪2年,如有需要我們會提供轉介信。是次研究是自願參與性質參與，這個研究期間所取得的資料都會被嚴格保密。
如家長有意願參與此項研究，請填寫以下網上篩選問卷(https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_81kdBVoLu4f6l3o)。收到問卷回覆後，我們會再與合適參加是次研究的小朋友之家長連絡。
如果家長對研究細節有任何疑問，歡迎透過WhatsApp 6099-3064或致電 2607-6057與我們聯絡。
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Dear Parents,
We are a team of researchers from the Department of Psychiatry at the Chinese University of Hong Kong. We are conducting a research project jointly organised by the Department of Psychiatry, the Department of Medicine and Therapeutics of the Chinese University of Hong Kong.
Our team sincerely invites your children to participate in research on the gut microbiome and children's brain development. Through collecting stool and buccal samples, we aim to investigate the relationship between the gut microbiome and brain development.
A gut health report will be provided, A G-Niib probiotics trial pack and a $200 supermarket voucher will be awarded to participants.
Target participants:
1) The child is diagnosed/suspected to have autism or other developmental problems
2) The child is under 33 months old (all questionnaires and samples are submitted before 3 years old)
3) Both parents are Chinese or Asian
4) Children’s brothers and sisters under 18 years old are also welcome to join
Procedures and details of this Study:
1) Research Consent
2) Online Questionnaire : A 45-minute questionnaire on children’s behaviors and their physical health condition
3) Stool and Buccal Sample Collection: Samples collection kit will be provided for sample collection at home
4) Dietary Questionnaire: Recording children's eating habits
You will receive a $200 supermarket voucher after completing all the research procedures. Participation is voluntary, and your responses will be kept confidential. The information you provide will be used solely for research purposes.
If you are interested in participating in our research study, please fill out the following online questionnaire (https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_81kdBVoLu4f6l3o). We will contact you afterwards if your children are suitable to join this study.
For inquiries, please contact 2607-6057 or WhatsApp 6099-3064.

香港中文大學體育運動科學系誠邀中央肥胖人士參與健康管理研究！
研究目的：
中央肥胖與血糖異常、心血管疾病及其他代謝健康問題的風險增加有關。為應對這一公共健康挑戰，香港中文大學體育運動科學系正開展健康生活方式計劃，提供個人化健康支援。
參加條件：
年齡：40-64歲
平時少做運動/無規律運動習慣
中央肥胖：男性腰圍 ≥ 90 cm; 女性腰圍 ≥ 80 cm
過去三個月體重變動≤5%
現時沒有服用長期藥物
參加方法：
掃描海報二維碼或通過鏈接作網上登記【https://forms.gle/aBCMAHiFKdDK6z5L6】
研究團隊會進行初步篩選，以了解您是否符合基本參加資格
成功通過初步篩選後，預約檢查時間
前往香港中文大學汾陽體育館參加檢查
如果符合參加條件，將會被隨機分組，正式開展後續正式的健康生活方式計劃
參與地點：
香港中文大學汾陽體育館G02室
如您有任何疑問，可通過以下渠道聯絡這項研究的相關人員：
何小姐

Study Purpose:
Central obesity is associated with an increased risk of abnormal glucose regulation, cardiovascular disease, and other metabolic health problems. To help address this growing public health concern, the Department of Sports Science and Physical Education at The Chinese University of Hong Kong is launching a Healthy Lifestyle Program that offers personalized health support for individuals with central obesity.
Recruitment criteria:
Aged between 40 and 64 years
No regular exercise habits
Central obesity: waist circumference ≥ 90 cm for men and ≥ 80 cm for women
Body weight fluctuation ≤5% in the past three months
Not taking any chronic medication
Study arrangement:
Scan the QR code to register (https://forms.gle/aBCMAHiFKdDK6z5L6)
The study team will select participants based on the registration information
Arrange a screening time
Arrive at CUHK Kwok Sports Building for the test
If you are eligible, you will be randomly assigned to start the formal Healthy Lifestyle Intervention Program
Study Location:
Room G02, Kwok Sports Building, Department of Sports Science and Physical Education, The Chinese University of Hong Kong, Shatin

If you are interested and have any inquiries, please feel free to contact us:
Ms. He
WhatsApp: 94463265

Communication Seminar Series - From AI Adoption to AI Agency: How Artificial Intelligence Is Reshaping Communication Work
Date: 15 October 2026 (Thursday)
Time: 2:30 pm-4:00 pm
Venue: C-Centre (NAH313, Humanities Building, CUHK)
Speaker:
Prof. Sung-Un Yang
Professor
Department of Mass Communication, Advertising, and Public Relations
Boston University, USA
Bio:
Sung-Un Yang (PhD, University of Maryland, 2005) is the Harold Burson Endowed Chair in Public Relations and Department Chair of Mass Communication, Advertising, and Public Relations at Boston University. His recent research focuses on strategic communication management, with particular emphasis on how emerging technologies, especially artificial intelligence, reshape public-organization relationships, employee communication, and organizational change. His recent work examines how communication professionals adopt AI and how leadership, internal communication, and organizational readiness drive successful integration.
Abstract:
Artificial intelligence is reshaping communication management at technological, organizational, and professional levels. This seminar presents three interconnected studies examining that transformation. The first investigates how perceived innovation attributes and AI-related threats influence communication professionals’ adoption attitudes and workplace AI use. The second examines how transformational leadership, dialogic communication, commitment to change, and organizational AI readiness shape employee responses to AI-driven change. The third introduces ongoing research on agentic AI, focusing on how increasingly autonomous systems may affect role ambiguity, professional authorship, job meaningfulness, and AI-related stress. Together, the studies trace the evolution from adopting AI tools to managing organizational change and confronting the consequences of delegating professional agency to AI systems.

  [Online experiment] Looking for native English speakers
Prof. Haerim Hwang (Department of English, CUHK) is looking for participants for a study on language production.
Which participants are we looking for?
- English is your first/native and dominant language
- Your graduate degree is not in the field of linguistics
- Can use your laptop/computer and have access to stable internet (no smartphones, laptops, or hotspot)
- Can participate in an experiment on Zoom in a quiet environment
- Have Chrome on your laptop/computer
How do I participate?
1. Fill out this questionnaire
-- English speakers: https://forms.gle/ttuhGGCwRx2n95kBA
2. Our research team will reach out to you, confirming your availability.
3. It will take approximately 2 hours to complete these tasks.
What do I get out of the study?
You will get HK$250 in cash upon the completion of the task.
Your participation will enhance our understanding of how people process English sentences.
Questions?
Contact Prof. Haerim Hwang at haerimhwang@cuhk.edu.hk
Ethics Approval
The Chinese University of Hong Kong Survey and Behavioural Research Ethics Committee SBREC (fssc02@cuhk.edu.hk) has vetted the study (Approval ID: SBRE-22-0026D). If you have any concerns regarding ethics, please contact them.

From: Hong Kong Institute of Asia-Pacific Studies
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
hkiaps@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
(The application below is conducted in Chinese only.)
日期：2026年10月16日（星期五）
時間：下午12時半至2時
地點：香港中文大學利黃瑤璧樓4樓401室
語言：廣東話
講者：丁新豹教授（香港中文大學歷史系客席教授(禮任)）
免費登記：
https://cloud.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk/webform/view.php?id=13740761
講座簡介：
丁新豹教授，香港歷史學者，香港大學中文系哲學博士，現任香港中文大學歷史系客席教授（禮任）、比較及公眾歷史研究中心名譽高級研究員、香港大學中文學院名譽教授、廣東省文史館館員，以及香港與內地多間博物館的名譽顧問或理事。曾任香港歷史博物館總館長。
講者簡介：
回顧丁新豹教授半個世紀的習史過程可區分為：修讀碩士、博士時期；任職藝術館／博物館時期及退休後通過實地考察學習歷史共三個階段。第一個階段主要從文獻入手，從拓跋族遷徙漢化到香港開埠初期華人社會的形成並落地生根，兩者看似風馬牛不相及，而實有某些共通點。第二個階段利用文物研究歷史：在藝術館九年以歷史畫探研珠三角的昔日風貌，而在香港歷史博物館近二十年，因策劃香港故事常設展、海防博物館及孫中山紀念館，開啟了嶄新的研究範疇，擴闊視野；另方面，通過舉辦多個主題不一的專題展覽，有機會涉獵到國史以外的歷史，甚或可以和國史相互參證。退休後，除初期從事東華三院歷史研究外，主要圍繞：東南亞華僑史、絲綢之路及東亞文化圈（日本、韓國、越南）三個主題通過實地考察探究歷史，獲益良多。從求學、工作、消閒，丁教授在人生旅途的不同階段以不同方式習史，不變的是無比的興趣和一顆好奇心。

From: Rina To
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
rinato@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
香港中文大學耳鼻咽喉 頭頸外科學系現正招募十八歲或以上沒有聲線障礙的人士參與一項聲學分析的研究，旨在探究平滑化倒頻譜突出峰值 (CPPS) 的臨界值和其診斷準確性。
CPPS是一種可應用於日常對話的聲線聲學分析參數。CPPS相對於其他常用的聲學參數具有更高的診斷準確性。但是，根據文獻的報告顯示，使用不同的語言，聲線樣本類型，和軟件，都會影響到CPPS的結果。我們希望這項研究的結果能夠為臨床醫生和研究人員對聲線障礙患者進行客觀測量並為聲線評估的量化結果提供明確的參考。
招募對象：
年滿十八歲或以上
沒有聲線問題的人士
以廣東話為母語
費用：全免
評估與檢查地點：威爾斯親王醫院
研究程序及内容：
1）參加者將填寫聲線問卷， 並親臨威爾斯親王醫院接受喉纖維內視鏡檢查和聲線錄製。

CPPS is a parameter for acoustic analysis of voice that can be used in everyday conversation to provide a more comprehensive and realistic picture of an individual's vocal characteristics in natural communication situations. CPPS has a higher diagnostic accuracy than other commonly used acoustic parameters. However, reports in the literature indicate that the use of different languages, different types of voice samples, and different software can affect the results of the CPPS. We hope that the results of this study will provide clinicians and researchers with a clear reference for the quantitative results of objective measurement and voice assessment in patients with voice disorders.

Age 18 or above

Participants will undergo a laryngeal videostroboscopy examination and a comprehensive voice assessment at Prince of Wales Hospital.
A videostroboscopy examination can clearly observe the throat to detect whether it has structural or functional problem for speaking. Each examination takes approximately thirty minutes. It is a low-risk procedure, and participants typically only experience mild discomfort.

香港中文大學精神科學系正進行一項研究，旨在評估手機應用程式網上自助心理健康療程對改善青年睡眠及情緒健康的成效。現招募年齡介乎15歲至24歲青年研究。詳情如下:
我們誠邀符合以下條件的人士參與本次研究：
1. 15歲至24歲青年
2. 有失眠及情緒症狀
3. 過去三個月沒有接受失眠及情緒心理治療或藥物治療
您需要做什麼？
參與為期6週的手機App自助療程
每週觀看20分鐘左右的網上療程
完成四次網上問卷及七天睡眠日記，包括治療前、治療後、三個月跟進及六個月跟進
全部評估及治療皆在電話或網上進行，無需面見！

The Department of Psychiatry at The Chinese University of Hong Kong is conducting a research study to evaluate the effectiveness of an online self-help mobile app program for improving sleep and emotional well-being among youths. We would like to invite participants aged between 15 and 24 to join the study. Details are as follows:
Inclusion criteria:
1. Youths aged between 15-24 years
2. Experience symptoms of insomnia and emotional distress
3. Have not received psychological or medication treatment for these issues in the past 3 months
What will you do?
Join a 6-week self-help treatment via mobile app
Attend 20 minutes of online therapy weekly
Complete four online surveys and seven-day sleep diary: before treatment, after treatment, at 3-month follow-up, and at 6-month follow-up during the study
All assessments and treatments are conducted via phone or online — no in-person visits required!
If you are interested, please register and complete a short screening questionnaire here:
https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_domAhEzzCmdV2sK
The research team will contact eligible participants and further explain the details of the study. Information collected will be only used for research purpose and will be kept strictly confidential. If you have any enquiries, please contact us via email
winifredtywong@cuhk.edu.hk
or WhatsApp: (+852- 47544464 Miss Wong).

2

細胞功能和胰島素抵抗的影響】
香港中文大學內科及藥物治療學系與香港中文大學香港中西醫結合醫學研究所現正聯合進行一項為期36週，以內服中藥(沖劑)治療 2 型糖尿病人
 研究對象：18至80歲華人
沒有重大疾病，沒有服用中藥， 身體質量指數 (BMI) ≥18 kg/m²  (公斤 ÷ 米 ÷ 米)
不吸煙或已戒煙至少 12 個月，如女性目前未懷孕
患糖尿病未滿 6 年，且在過去 3 個月內未使用任何降血糖藥物（包括胰島素）治療
至少具備以下其中一項風險因素:
糖尿病家族史 (尤其父母或兄弟姐妹在40歲前診斷 )
代謝綜合症 (3高：高血糖，高血壓，高膽固醇)
超重或肥胖
脂肪肝
多囊卵巢綜合症
妊娠糖尿病病史
如不確定自己是否患有糖尿病，會安排你服用葡萄糖飲料（75 克口服葡萄糖耐量試驗）
研究內容：中西醫評估、心電圖、肝纖維化掃描、抽血檢查、填寫問卷、服用研究中藥或安慰劑等
地點：新界沙田威爾斯醫院，舊座，3 樓，3M 病房 - 糖尿及內分泌研究中心
參與研究費用全免，成功參與者可獲得高達港幣 $1,000 的津貼，名額有限，先到先得！

如果初步合適參與研究，負責同事將稍後聯絡你，謝謝
如對研究內容有任何疑問，歡迎致電  3505 3897 / 6937 3365 或 WhatsApp 6937 3365與負責研究人員聯絡、查詢詳情。
[Clinical safety, efficacy and multiomic evaluation of a novel Chinese Medicine formula in Type 2 diabetes: Effects on beta-cell function and insulin resistance
.]
Department of Medicine and Therapeutics and Hong Kong Institute of Integrative Medicine, CUHK are jointly conducting a 36-week clinical study on the use of oral traditional Chinese medicine (granule form) for treating type 2 diabetes.
Eligibility Criteria: Ethnic Chinese individuals aged 18 to 80 years
No major illnesses, not currently taking any traditional Chinese medicine, and with a Body Mass Index (BMI) ≥ 18 kg/m² (kg ÷ metre ÷ metre)
Non-smokers or those who have quit smoking for at least 12 months; females must not be currently pregnant
Diagnosed with type 2 diabetes for less than 6 years and have not used any glucose-lowering medications (including insulin) in the past 3 months
Must have at least one of the following risk factors:
Family history of diabetes (especially if parents or siblings were diagnosed before age of 40)
Metabolic syndrome (three highs: high blood sugar, high blood pressure, high blood cholesterol)
Overweight or obesity
Fatty liver

title: Call for Applications: NTU AI-for-X Postdoctoral Fellowship 2026 (Deadline: 30 October)
bodyText:

Call for Applications: NTU AI-for-X Postdoctoral Fellowship 2026 (Deadline: 30 October)  - Office of Academic Links
From: Office of Academic Links
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
oal_schemes@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
Nanyang Technological University (NTU), Singapore, is now inviting applications for the
NTU AI-for-X Postdoctoral Fellowship 2026
. The application period is open until
30 October 2026
.
About the Fellowship
Launched in partnership with Singapore's National Research Foundation (NRF), this prestigious fellowship supports outstanding early-career researchers who seek to apply Artificial Intelligence (AI) to accelerate scientific discovery across science, technology, engineering, mathematics, and medicine (STEM). The programme aims to nurture the next generation of interdisciplinary research leaders working at the intersection of AI and scientific research. More information is available
here
.
Fellowship Highlights
Up to 4 years of funding
Competitive remuneration and benefits
SGD 250,000 research grant with continued funding even after transition to a tenure-track role
Access to NTU's AI platforms, research facilities, and computing resources
Structured AI training and mentorship from NTU faculty across AI and STEM disciplines
Eligibility
Applicants should:
Hold a PhD (or equivalent) awarded in 2023 or later in a STEM discipline
Have a strong academic and research track record
Propose a research project that integrates AI to address a scientific challenge
Identify an NTU faculty member as a Project Mentor
Available to commence the fellowship by 31 March 2027
Each selected Fellow will be paired with:
A
Project Mentor
in their research field
An
AI Mentor
(assigned or selected post-award) to support AI integration
Application Information
Application Deadline
: 30 October 2026, 2359 hrs (Singapore Time, UTC/GMT+8)
Application Portal
: Applications must be submitted in electronic format via NTU Online Application
Portal
.

:
NTU AI-for-X Postdoctoral Fellowship

Registration

Register

Register

.

Unlock Your Potential: Join the CUHK eLearning Student Ambassadors 2026/2027! Registration is NOW open for all CUHK (UG & PG) students  - Information Technology Services Centre (ITSC)
From: Rudi C. (ITSC)

rudichow@cuhk.edu.hk

Are you someone who has a strong interest in communication, digital media, publication, information technology, AI trends, and online learning?
Would you like to develop your own multimedia and online portfolio while assisting other fellow students to have a better online learning experience?
If the answer is YES, we would like to invite you to apply and join us to become a
CUHK eLearning Student Ambassador (eLSA)
.
We are seeking applicants (Year 1 - 4 UG students, and all PG students) who are:
Driven to perform a
creative
and
dynamic
role to help fellow students in utilising various eLearning resources (including AI trends and its application in education).
Committed
and
motivated
to learn and improve IT, AI tools, online media, and digital skills to support their studies and future careers.
eLSA programme offers you:
An opportunity to develop digital, media production, IT, communication, organisation and teamwork skills.
Regular trainings that cover the fundamental IT and digital production skills you would need to support the work.
An opportunity to create and showcase your digital and online portfolio. (including CUHK SDP - Student Development Portfolio programme)
A space to contribute innovative ideas and exercise creative thinking to improve the CUHK eLearning environment.
eLSA ambassadors will receive subsidies under the
University’s Campus Work Scheme
.
Please complete the webform at:
https://cloud.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk/webform/view.php?id=13741495
Application deadline
(extended)
: October 3, 2026 - 11.59 PM.

https://www.cuhk.edu.hk/eLearning
.

Registration for the “Founders' Day Round Campus Run” of The 75th Chung Chi College Founders' Day Student Festival 報名崇基學院第七十五屆校慶學生節「崇慶環校跑」 - Chaplain's Office, Chung Chi College
From: Lam Sui Chi
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
chaplaincy@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
報名崇基學院第七十五屆校慶學生節「崇慶環校跑」
Registration for the “Founders' Day Round Campus Run” of The 75th Chung Chi College Founders' Day Student Festival
(Please scroll down for English version)
各位同學、教職員及校友：
為慶祝崇基學院七十五週年校慶，崇基學院將舉辦一年一度的「崇慶環校跑」，這項盛事不僅是體能與毅力的挑戰，更是凝聚校園精神、促進交流的絕佳機會。歡迎崇基學院以及香港中文大學其它書院的本科生、教職員及校友參加。不論您是運動健將還是跑步愛好者，都歡迎一同揮灑青春汗水，共慶崇基生辰！
活動詳情
日期：
2026年10月30日（星期五）
時間：
登記：下午2時00分 至 2時40分
儀式及比賽：下午2時45分 至4時
地點：
崇基學院嶺南運動場（起點與終點）
組別：
個人賽
男子組
女子組
參賽者：
崇基學院以及香港中文大學其它書院的本科生、教職員及校友均可參加，惟獎項只頒發給崇基學院學生、教職員及校友。
獎項：
冠、亞、季軍各一名（男、女子組分開計算）
初擬路線：
嶺南運動場 > 崇基學院行政樓 > 何添樓 > 崇基教堂 > 何善衡工程大樓 > 蒙民偉工程大樓 > 善衡書院 > 夏鼎基運動場 > 方潤華堂 > 嶺南運動場
備註：
參賽者必須於下午2時40分前到報到處登記並取號碼布，否則將被取消參賽資格；
學生參賽者必須於賽事登記時以學生證拍卡登記，並在完成賽事後重新拍卡以登記完成賽事，否則將不獲4分體育課程活動分；
參賽者必須於限時四十五分鐘內完成賽事；
參賽者必須以個人名義參賽；
參賽者（包括教職員和校友）將分為男子組及女子組進行比賽；
參賽者必須戴上號碼布及按照大會指定路線進行比賽；
參賽者在比賽期間不可阻礙其他參賽者前進及使用輔助工具；
如有投訴，參賽者必須在終點站關閉後十分鐘內向司令台負責人提出，逾時將不獲受理；
參賽者必須遵守以上規則，違規者將有機會被取消參賽資格；
參賽者必須注意個人安全及看管個人財物；
賽事將以名次決定勝出者，男、女子組分別最快完成賽事的參賽者為第一名，即個人賽的冠軍，如此類推（男、女子組分開計算，即男、女子組各有名次）。
雨程：
若活動當天中午12時正仍下雨，比賽將會取消。活動消息將在週會末段的宣傳時間公布，同時在眾志堂和嶺南場門外貼出通告，並透過電郵通知參賽者相關消息，敬請留意電郵；
若在報到或比賽期間下雨，大會將視乎雨勢及賽道情況而終止賽事。惟參賽者必須於下午2時40分前報到，並於本學期內把號碼布交還給體育部老師，方可獲4分體育課程活動分。
期待在跑道上見到你的身影，一起為校慶增添喜慶！請於
2026
年
10
月
16
日（星期五）或之前
於
CC75RoundCampusRun
報名。成功報名之參賽者將於10月23日（星期五）或之前收到確認電郵。
如有查詢，請與崇基學院校牧室Walter聯絡（電話：3943 4301或電郵至
walterlam@cuhk.edu.hk
）。
“Founders' Day Round Campus Run” of The 75th Chung Chi College Founders' Day Student Festival
Dear Students, Staff Members and Alumni,
In celebration of the Chung Chi College 75th Anniversary, the annual “Founders' Day Round Campus Run” will be held on October 30, 2026. This event is not only a challenge of physical strength and perseverance but also a wonderful opportunity to strengthen campus spirit and foster connections among students, faculty, and alumni. Students, staff members, and alumni from Chung Chi College and other colleges of The Chinese University of Hong Kong are all warmly welcome to join. Whether you are an athlete or a running enthusiast, come along to sweat it out and celebrate Chung Chi’s birthday together!
Details
Date:
October 30, 2026（Friday）
Time:
Registration: 2:00 p.m. to 2:40 p.m.
Ceremony & Competition: 2:45 p.m. to 4:00 p.m.
Venue:
Lingnan Stadium of Chung Chi College (Start and Finish points)
Division:
Individuals
Men
Women
Participant:
Students, staff members, and alumni from Chung Chi College and other colleges of The Chinese University of Hong Kong are welcome to join, but only those from Chung Chi College are eligible to receive prizes.
Award:
Champion, first runner-up, and second runner-up will be awarded in both the Men’s and Women’s divisions.
Initial Route:
Lingnan Stadium > CCC Admin Building > Ho Tim Building > CC Chapel > Ho Sin-Hang Engineering Building > William MW Mong Engineering Building > S.H. Ho College > Sir Philip Haddon-Cave Sports Field > Fong Yun Wah Hall > Lingnan Stadium
Remarks:
Runners must check in at the registration counter and collect race bib no later than 2:40 p.m. Late registration will lead to disqualification.
Student runners must tap their student ID card at registration and tap again upon completion of the race. Failure to do so will result in forfeiture of the 4 participation marks in P.E. course.
Runners must complete the race within the 45-minute time limit.
All runners must compete as individuals.
Runners (including staff and alumni) will be divided into Men’s and Women’s divisions.
Runners must wear their assigned bib number and follow the designated route throughout the race.
Runners must not obstruct other runners or use any form of assistance during the race.
Any complaints must be lodged with the officials at the command desk within 10 minutes after the closing of the finish line. Late complaints will not be entertained.
Runners must adhere to all rules above. Violations may lead to disqualification.
Runners are responsible for their personal safety and belongings.
Winners will be determined by finishing order. The fastest finisher in the Men’s and Women’s divisions respectively will be awarded 1st place, followed by 2nd and 3rd places. Rankings are calculated separately for each division.

CALL FOR PROPOSALS | Participation in the 17th Chinese National Arctic Research Expedition 2027 | HKPSIC  - Hong Kong Polar Science Innovation Centre
From: Yolanda YIM
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
yolandayim@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
An Opportunity to Conduct Research in Arctic
Regions
__________________________________________________________________________________
The Hong Kong Polar Science Innovation Centre (HKPSIC) is pleased to invite proposals from scientists and researchers interested in participating in the
17th
Chinese National Arctic
Research Expedition 2027
.
Research opportunities are available at
Arctic Ocean Expedition with Xuelong or Xuelong 2, Yellow River Station
and
China-Iceland Arctic Science Observatory (CIAO)
in Arctic Regions. All proposals and personnel nominations will be reviewed and selected by the Polar Research Institute of China (PRIC).
This opportunity is primarily open to researchers from universities in Hong Kong.
Expedition Purpose
The expedition will be conducted for
scientific research purposes
.
Research Opportunities
Arctic Ocean Expedition with Xuelong or Xuelong 2
Quota:
Tentatively 1-2 participants
(Subject to adjustment based on the approved research proposals.)
Eligibility:
PhD candidates
Postdoctoral fellows
Academic staff and researchers
Duration:
Approximately 2–4 months at the station
Tentative departure from Shanghai aboard the icebreaker
Xuelong
or
Xuelong 2
in June or July 2027
Return to Shanghai in Sep or Oct 2027
Additional travel time should be allowed for flights to Shanghai
Yellow River Station
Quota:
1–2 participant(s)
Eligibility:
PhD candidates
Postdoctoral fellows
Academic staff and researchers
Duration:
Approximately 1- 2 week(s) at the station
Tentative departure from Longyearbyen to the station in Aug or Sep
Additional travel time should be allowed for flights to Longyearbyen and from Hong Kong
China-Iceland Arctic Science Observatory (CIAO)
Quota:
1–2 participant(s)
Eligibility:
PhD candidates
Postdoctoral fellows
Academic staff and researchers
Duration:
Approximately 1- 2 week(s) at the station
Tentative departure from Akureyri and drive to the station in Aug or Sep
Additional travel time should be allowed for flights from Hong Kong to Reykjavík, onward travel to Akureyri, and ground transportation to the station.
Priority consideration:
Applicants with existing research collaborations or academic connections in Iceland
Research Instruments
As the icebreakers
Xuelong
and
Xuelong 2
will depart from Shanghai, PRIC recommends that any required research instruments be shipped to Shanghai no later than
Mar-April
for loading and transportation to the Antarctic research stations.
Health and Visa Requirements
Selected participants will be required to:
Complete a medical examination specified by PRIC
Submit a medical report for review
Obtain a Schengen visa for Yellow River Station or CIAO
Participants should allow sufficient time for medical examinations and visa applications.
Clothing and Equipment
PRIC will provide basic expedition clothing and equipment, including:
Expedition jackets
Trousers
Thermal wear
Sunglasses
Other essential gear
These items will be provided to selected participants before departure.
Expenses to Be Covered by Participants
Participants are responsible for all associated expenses, including:
International airfares
Accommodation on the stations before and after station entry/exit or during the expedition in the stations
(Accommodation on Xuelong or Xuelong 2 is provided free of charge)
Travel insurance
Visa application fees (if applicable)
Medical examination fees
Shipment and transportation costs for research instruments and equipment
Any other incidental expenses
Proposal Submission
Researchers who are able to meet the above requirements and schedule are invited to submit an email request to obtain the proposal template.
Submission Deadline
10 November 2026 (Tuesday)
All proposals will be forwarded to PRIC for evaluation and selection. HKPSIC will provide support to participating researchers and facilitate communications with PRIC throughout the application and preparation process.
Enquiries
Secretariat
Hong Kong Polar Science Innovation Centre (HKPSIC)
Email: hkpsic@cuhk.edu.hk
Tel: 3943 0345
We sincerely encourage interested researchers to take advantage of this unique opportunity to conduct scientific research in Arctic Regions and contribute to polar research collaboration.
We look forward to receiving your proposals.
View Count
For request submissions, please submit them at
https://cumassmail.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk
For enquiries, please write to:
http://servicedesk.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk

[External activity] L.I.O.N. 2027
To encourage young people to assist peers in overcoming the difficulties they face in their development and to resist temptation of drugs, the Narcotics Bureau of the Hong Kong Police Force founded the “Leadership Institute on Narcotics” (L.I.O.N.) in 2021 with the support of various sectors of the community and recruited 100 secondary and university students over the territory as mentees each year. Through providing systematic training by expertise from different professions and offering guidance on design and implementation of anti-drug activities by mentors, L.I.O.N. aims to foster mentees’ sense of social responsibility and nurture them into outstanding young anti-drug leaders.
L.I.O.N. 2027 is now open for applications! The institute offers a range of practical training, covering topics like drug prevention knowledge – its effects on mind and body and legal applications, leadership skills development and project management, multimedia creation and hands-on promotion techniques, and courses on generative AI applications. Mentees will receive systematic training on drug knowledge and leadership skills throughout the year, and university mentees will lead secondary school mentees to implement anti-drug campaigns under the guidance of their mentors.
On top of the originally planned series of local training sessions, the upcoming 2025/26 L.I.O.N. will be continued to organize a field trip to the Mainland which aims to deepen mentees’ understanding on the national anti-drug strategies and latest developments in the Mainland. An overseas trip will also be offered to outstanding mentees. Mentees will also receive leadership training from professional instructors, apply their learning by leading teams of secondary school students, gain first-hand exposure to the work of officers from the Narcotics Bureau, participate in large-scale events, and have opportunities to be featured in media interviews.

[External activity] L.I.O.N. 2027
To encourage young people to assist peers in overcoming the difficulties they face in their development and to resist temptation of drugs, the Narcotics Bureau of the Hong Kong Police Force founded the “Leadership Institute on Narcotics” (L.I.O.N.) in 2021 with the support of various sectors of the community and recruited 100 secondary and university students over the territory as mentees each year. Through providing systematic training by expertise from different professions and offering guidance on design and implementation of anti-drug activities by mentors, L.I.O.N. aims to foster mentees’ sense of social responsibility and nurture them into outstanding young anti-drug leaders.
L.I.O.N. 2027 is now open for applications! The institute offers a range of practical training, covering topics like drug prevention knowledge – its effects on mind and body and legal applications, leadership skills development and project management, multimedia creation and hands-on promotion techniques, and courses on generative AI applications. Mentees will receive systematic training on drug knowledge and leadership skills throughout the year, and university mentees will lead secondary school mentees to implement anti-drug campaigns under the guidance of their mentors.
On top of the originally planned series of local training sessions, the upcoming 2025/26 L.I.O.N. will be continued to organize a field trip to the Mainland which aims to deepen mentees’ understanding on the national anti-drug strategies and latest developments in the Mainland. An overseas trip will also be offered to outstanding mentees. Mentees will also receive leadership training from professional instructors, apply their learning by leading teams of secondary school students, gain first-hand exposure to the work of officers from the Narcotics Bureau, participate in large-scale events, and have opportunities to be featured in media interviews.

From: The Graduate School Office

[Invitation] Graduate School Seminar 202
6
: “
AI in Education
”
As
CUHK Graduate School
celebrates its
60th Anniversary
, we are not only reflecting on six decades of excellence, innovation, and impact, but also looking ahead to the future of education in an increasingly AI-driven world.
To mark this milestone, we are pleased to invite you to join us on 6 November 2026 (Fri) for a series of celebration activities
,
including our annual signature event, the
Graduate School Seminar 202
6:
“
AI in Education
”
, a
networking session
bringing together speakers, students, and alumni from diverse backgrounds and disciplines, as well as a
mini exhibition
showcasing the Graduate School’s history and achievements.
Jointly organised by the CUHK Graduate School and the Federation of Graduate School Alumni Associations (FGSAA), the
Graduate School Seminar 2026: "AI in Education"
presents a forward-looking dialogue on how artificial intelligence is transforming teaching and learning, research, and graduate education.
We are honoured to welcome three distinguished speakers who will share their insights on the evolving role of AI in education in keynote speeches and panel discussion:

"From Knowledge to Discovery: AI and the Future of Graduate Education"
Professor Irwin KING
- Pro-Vice-Chancellor / Vice-President (Education)
- Professor, Department of Computer Science and Engineering
Keynote Speaker & Panelist

"How Hong Kong Education City can Assist in the Implementation of the
Blueprint for Digital Education Development in Primary and Secondary Schools
"
Mr. Armstrong LEE
- Chairman, Hong Kong Education City
- Graduate of
@CUHK MBA
Keynote Speaker

"Standardised AI Literacy and Certification: Lessons from Southeast Asia"
Dr. Winson WONG
- Certified AI Trainer of United Nations University
- Graduate of
@CUHK EMBA
Keynote Speaker & Panelist
Dr. Tenny LAM
- Executive Director, Hong Kong Education City
- Graduate of
@CUHK EMBA
Panelist
Moderator:
Prof. Anthony SO, Dean of the Graduate School
Drawing on their diverse expertise across academia, education, and industry, our speakers will share insights on the opportunities and challenges presented by AI technologies, and discuss their implications for the future of higher education.
The Seminar will conclude with a
networking session with refreshments
, providing an opportunity for alumni, students, academics, and professionals to connect, exchange ideas, and explore new collaborations.

Date:
6 November 2026 (Friday)

Time:
3:00 pm – 5:30 pm

Venue:
VR Zone, Learning Garden, LG/F, University Library, CUHK
Shuttle bus service will be provided between University MTR Station and the CUHK University Library according to the designated schedule
Online Registration:
Please click
here
to register online via CUHK Registration and Attendance System on or before 23 October 2026 (Friday).
All CUHK, CUHK(SZ) and CUSCS students, alumni and staff are welcome to sign up for the event.
Join us as we celebrate 60 years of excellence and reimagine the future of graduate education at CUHK and beyond.

自2012年始，大學通識教育基礎課程已在中大全面推行。UGFH和UGFN不知不覺已成為中大人的共同學習經驗。在2026-27學年，大學通識教育基礎課程將繼續推出

【TSSSU】Technology Start-up Support Scheme for Universities (TSSSU) 2027-28: Call for Applications [Deadline: 1 Nov 2026] 「大學科技初創企業資助計劃 2027-28」[截止日期: 11月1日 (星期日)] - Knowledge Transfer Office (KTO)
From: Knowledge Transfer Office (KTO)
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
vateam@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
Wish to transform your R&D results to a real business and become an entrepreneur?
If you wish to turn your research output into a real business, please consider applying for the
Technology Startup Support Scheme for Universities (TSSSU)
. Or, if your students wish to commercialize their R&D results, please also encourage them to apply for TSSSU.
Successful applicants may receive
Up to HK$600,000 funding per year for potentially up to three years
Potential to join HKSTP’s Incubation Programme
Access to potential investors & industry partners
Mentorship from experienced entrepreneurship consultant
Apply Now IF
Your idea is innovative, your team is capable, your innovation and technology are unique and your business plan is sound
Your team wants to make a societal impact and is passionate about entrepreneurship
Eligibility of a PIC
The Person-in-Charge (PIC) of a CUHK TSSSU company must be a full-time CUHK student, a full-time CUHK professor, or alumni graduated within the last three years.
Compulsory Requirements:
The technology involved in the application must be CUHK-related
and with Intellectual Property (IP) owned by CUHK*.
The technology involved in the application must reach the required Technology Readiness Level (TRL).
Physical Science and Engineering technology must reach TRL 4 or above
and
HealthCare technology must reach TRL 3 or above
.
The number of members of the Company must be
at least two
including the eligible PIC. Active members of CUHK should be the effective majority of shareholders of the Company.
Fulfill all the eligibility requirements in CUHK TSSSU Guideline 202
7
-2
8
.
(TSSSU+ only) The assessment panel shall review the investment arrangement during the assessment process per the request of ITC.  Please submit the
agreement
issued by the private investor together with the applications.  If the agreement has not yet been signed, please submit the latest available draft agreement.
* If a patent application has not been filed at the time of submission of a TSSSU-O or TSSSU+ application, the applicant should consider submitting an Invention Disclosure Form or a Copyright Disclosure Form and Assignment to the KTO IP and Technology Licensing Team.

Unlock Your Potential: Join the CUHK eLearning Student Ambassadors 2026/2027! - Registration is NOW open for all CUHK (UG & PG) students  - Information Technology Services Centre (ITSC)
From: Rudi C. (ITSC)
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
rudichow@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
Are you someone who has a strong interest in communication, digital media, publication, information technology, AI trends, and online learning?
Would you like to develop your own multimedia and online portfolio while assisting other fellow students to have a better online learning experience?
If the answer is YES, we would like to invite you to apply and join us to become a
CUHK eLearning Student Ambassador (eLSA)
.
We are seeking applicants (Year 1 - 4 UG students, and PG students) who are:
Driven to perform a
creative
and
dynamic
role to help fellow students in utilising various eLearning resources (including AI trends and its application in education).
Committed
and
motivated
to learn and improve IT, AI tools, online media, and digital skills to support their studies and future careers.
eLSA programme offers you:
An opportunity to develop digital, media production, IT, communication, organisation and teamwork skills.
Regular trainings that cover the fundamental IT and digital production skills you would need to support the work.
An opportunity to create and showcase your digital and online portfolio. (including CUHK SDP - Student Development Portfolio programme)
A space to contribute innovative ideas and exercise creative thinking to improve the CUHK eLearning environment.
eLSA ambassadors will receive subsidies under the
University’s Campus Work Scheme
.
Please complete the webform at:
https://cloud.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk/webform/view.php?id=13741495
Application deadline
: September 27, 2026 - 11.59 PM.
To learn more about eLearning@CUHK, please visit
https://www.cuhk.edu.hk/eLearning
.
For more information, please contact ITSC-EDT via email at:
rudichow@cuhk.edu.hk

Call for Papers 11th Conference of the International Society for Gesture Studies - ISGS 2027  - Department of Educational Psychology
From: Catherine So
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
wingchee@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
Call for Papers
11th Conference of the International Society for Gesture Studies - ISGS 2027
Conference Dates: 14-16 December 2027, Hong Kong
Abstract Submission Dates: July 2, 2026 - November 30, 2026
Conference website:
https://events.polyu.edu.hk/isgs2027/home
Abstract Submission Link:
https://cems.polyu.edu.hk/abstract-submission?id=68&eventId=2DC9D9A1-D4F9-4BD9-9B8C-D5E229D92760
We cordially invite abstracts on topics related to Futures for Gestures within the following thematic areas: “Theory, Practice, Technology, Ecology” and their subthemes.
Theory
Mind, embodiment, and cognition
Perception and social understanding
Psychology and philosophy
Meaning and multimodality
Gesture studies theory
Practice
Knowledge, competence, and skill
Habitualisation, routine, and culture
Learning, pedagogy, and performance
Interaction, conduct, and communication
Intervention, impact, and profession
Technology
Artificial Intelligence, computer vision, and big data
New, digital, and social media
Screen, film, and cinema
Kinematics and capture
Human-Computer Interaction
Ecology
Organism, environment, and nature
Vitality, life, and living
Growth, movement, and process
Relationality and materiality
Dynamic and complex systems
We welcome all submissions that explore these themes and sub-themes.
Presentation Formats:
Paper presentation   20 minutes & 5 minutes Q & A
Poster presentation   Print: Size: A0 (Width: 841mm x Height: 1189mm)
Thematic Panels   90 min slot. Maximum 5 presentations + minimum 15 minutes discussion/ Q & A
Abstract Submission Guidelines for papers and posters:
Abstracts should be anonymous. Please delete all references to the authors.
Each abstract should include the following:
a. Title (max: 15 words)
b. Abstract (max: 350 words excluding references)
c. Citation style: APA (7th edition)
Please submit your abstract online following this format.
For Thematic Panels:
Add the details of the panel chair as the submitting author and of all the authors using the "Add Co-author" function. (Please indicate which contributing authors are also panel co-chairs, if any).
Add a title line with the title of the panel under "Abstract Title".
Upload one document with all the abstracts including a 250-word rationale for the panel + 150 words per paper (max. 5 papers).
Remember to delete all references to the authors.
Each presenter can appear on a maximum of three abstracts (whether paper / poster presentation, panel) and only once as the first author (excluding thematic panels).
Authors should ensure that the same abstract has not been presented at another conference.
Deadline for submission: 30 November 2026, 11:59PM (Hong Kong Time) (UTC+8)
Selection Process
All submissions will undergo a double (or triple) blind review and the first author of accepted submissions will be informed by the beginning of April 2027.
The ISGS will offer a restricted number of bursaries to student presenters, including PhD candidates, at the conference as a waiver of the registration price. Information regarding the application process will be provided following review of conference abstracts.
International Sign interpreting will be provided by Overseas Interpreting. We will inquire about your requirements during registration.
Pre-conference Workshops
Pre-conference workshops are being organised and will take place the day before the conference (December 13th 2027). More information will be shared once available.
Abstract Submission Link
https://cems.polyu.edu.hk/abstract-submission?id=68&eventId=2DC9D9A1-D4F9-4BD9-9B8C-D5E229D92760
Please contact us at
isgs2027.hk@polyu.edu.hk
if you have any enquiries.

Abstract Submission Dates: July 2, 2026 - November 30, 2026
Conference website:
https://events.polyu.edu.hk/isgs2027/home
Abstract Submission Link:
https://cems.polyu.edu.hk/abstract-submission?id=68&eventId=2DC9D9A1-D4F9-4BD9-9B8C-D5E229D92760
We cordially invite abstracts on topics related to Futures for Gestures within the following thematic areas: “Theory, Practice, Technology, Ecology” and their subthemes.
Theory
Mind, embodiment, and cognition
Perception and social understanding
Psychology and philosophy
Meaning and multimodality
Gesture studies theory
Practice
Knowledge, competence, and skill
Habitualisation, routine, and culture
Learning, pedagogy, and performance
Interaction, conduct, and communication
Intervention, impact, and profession
Technology
Artificial Intelligence, computer vision, and big data
New, digital, and social media
Screen, film, and cinema
Kinematics and capture
Human-Computer Interaction
Ecology
Organism, environment, and nature
Vitality, life, and living
Growth, movement, and process
Relationality and materiality
Dynamic and complex systems
We welcome all submissions that explore these themes and sub-themes.
Presentation Formats:
Paper presentation   20 minutes & 5 minutes Q & A
Poster presentation   Print: Size: A0 (Width: 841mm x Height: 1189mm)
Thematic Panels   90 min slot. Maximum 5 presentations + minimum 15 minutes discussion/ Q & A
Abstract Submission Guidelines for papers and posters:
Abstracts should be anonymous. Please delete all references to the authors.
Each abstract should include the following:
a. Title (max: 15 words)
b. Abstract (max: 350 words excluding references)
c. Citation style: APA (7th edition)
Please submit your abstract online following this format.
For Thematic Panels:
Add the details of the panel chair as the submitting author and of all the authors using the "Add Co-author" function. (Please indicate which contributing authors are also panel co-chairs, if any).
Add a title line with the title of the panel under "Abstract Title".
Upload one document with all the abstracts including a 250-word rationale for the panel + 150 words per paper (max. 5 papers).
Remember to delete all references to the authors.
Each presenter can appear on a maximum of three abstracts (whether paper / poster presentation, panel) and only once as the first author (excluding thematic panels).
Authors should ensure that the same abstract has not been presented at another conference.
Deadline for submission: 30 November 2026, 11:59PM (Hong Kong Time) (UTC+8)
Selection Process
All submissions will undergo a double (or triple) blind review and the first author of accepted submissions will be informed by the beginning of April 2027.
The ISGS will offer a restricted number of bursaries to student presenters, including PhD candidates, at the conference as a waiver of the registration price. Information regarding the application process will be provided following review of conference abstracts.
International Sign interpreting will be provided by Overseas Interpreting. We will inquire about your requirements during registration.
Pre-conference Workshops
Pre-conference workshops are being organised and will take place the day before the conference (December 13th 2027). More information will be shared once available.

isgs2027.hk@polyu.edu.hk
if you have any enquiries.

CUHK eLearning Student Ambassador (eLSA)
.

Driven to perform a
creative
and
dynamic
role to help fellow students in utilising various eLearning resources (including AI trends and its application in education).
Committed
and
motivated
to learn and improve IT, AI tools, online media, and digital skills to support their studies and future careers.

A space to contribute innovative ideas and exercise creative thinking to improve the CUHK eLearning environment.

26-27 The Friends of the Arts開始接受報名啦！
「Friends of the Arts」（FTA）由藝術行政主任辦公室主辦，旨在為中大全日制學生提供更多接觸藝術、體驗藝術的機會，拉近大家與藝術之間的距離，探索藝術文化的多元面貌。本計劃將持續舉辦不同類型的藝術活動，讓各位透過參與體驗，發掘興趣、拓闊視野，並從不同藝術形式中獲得啟發，豐富校園生活。
無論你是資深藝術迷，還是想踏出接觸藝術的第一步，都歡迎加入，一同成為 Friends of the Arts！
計劃為期一年：2026年9月1日 至 2027年4月30日。
截止日期: 2026年10月30日（五）
對象：
香港中文大學全日制學生
會員費用：
$250
基本禮遇：
．2張本地演出門票
．1張展覽門票
．1次文化工作坊/本地文化遊（任選其一）
額外福利：
．會員專屬藝術資訊平台，接收最新藝文訊息
．與藝術文化導賞員或資深藝術家交流
．與不同科系背景的藝文同好交流
．優先參與OAA藝術活動

Our MAJS Programme offers comprehensive training in Japanese society, culture, history, and language. Designed for those seeking deeper academic engagement or professional opportunities related to Japan, the programme equips students with the knowledge and skills essential for careers in Japan-related fields or further academic pursuits.
Whether you're passionate about Japanese studies or planning a career with a Japan focus, this programme is your gateway to meaningful growth and development.

From: Office of Student Affairs

香港中文大

傑出學生獎
2026－現正接受報名！
你是否曾在藝術、創新、體育或社會服務方面發揮所長，創造影響力？
歡迎申請
2026 傑出學生獎，與大家分享你的成就和故事！
除了追求學術成就外，香港中文大學(中大)學生亦積極在非學術範疇發揮所長。為表揚在不同領域有傑出表現，並持續為大學社群及社會作出積極貢獻的學生，中大設立「傑出學生獎」，以肯定其成就與貢獻，並鼓勵同學追求卓越、勇於突破自我。
【獎項類別】
藝術
創新與發明
社會服務
體育
特別表現
【申請資格】
在2025–26學年就讀於香港中文大學的全日制本科生或研究生，如於有關學年在上述其中一個範疇取得卓越成就或作出重大貢獻，均符合申請資格。
【截止日期】
2026年9月18日（星期五）中午12時正。
歡迎以個人或團隊形式申請。
【詳情及報名】
https://www.osa.cuhk.edu.hk/programmes/osa-application-guideline/

潘小姐(電話：3943 7210；電郵：
gladys@cuhk.edu.hk
)或
陳小姐(電話：3943 1843；電郵：
kimichan@cuhk.edu.hk
)。
誠邀你把握機會展示卓越成就，分享成長歷程，並以自身經驗啟發同儕。
我們期待收到你的報名！
Are you the next CUHK Outstanding Student?
Apply now for 2026!
Have you made a mark in the arts, innovation, sports, or social service this year? It’s time to be recognized for your passion and achievements!
The CUHK Outstanding Students Awards 2026 aim to celebrate students who have demonstrated outstanding achievements and made a positive impact on the University community and society through their dedication, talent, and perseverance.
【
Award Categories
】
Arts
Innovation and Invention
Social Service
Sports
Special Achievement
【Eligibility】
Full-time undergraduate and postgraduate students enrolled at CUHK during the 2025–26 academic year who have demonstrated outstanding achievements or made significant contributions in one of the above categories within the same academic year are eligible to apply.
【
Application Deadline
】
18 September 2026 (Friday), 12:00 noon
.
(Applications are welcome from both individuals and teams.)
【
Details & Application
】
https://www.osa.cuhk.edu.hk/programmes/osa-application-guideline/

)

)

We look forward to receiving your application!

****
中小學學生活動管理專業證書課程
2026–2027****
香港中文大學教育學院、香港教育研究所與香港課外活動主任協會於2026–2027學年舉辦兼讀制 「中小學學生活動管理專業證書課程」，以回應中、小學學生活動的發展情勢，並配合學員的專業需要。
課程對象
負責或協助籌辦及帶領學生活動的現職中、小學教師，尤以現任及新任課外活動主任、全方位學習統籌主任、新高中「其他學習經歷」統籌主任、「學生學習概覽」統籌主任及課程發展主任為合。需持有教師資歷及認可大學之學士學位。
課程內容
課程包括四個必修單元和一個選修單元，共126小時。
必修單元
選修單元
DSA0001學生活動的基礎知識與理論
DSA0002學生活動的管理
DSA0003學生活動的實踐
DSA0004學生活動專題探究
DSA0101小學學生活動的組織與運作
DSA0102中學學生活動的組織與運作
修讀日期
2026年11月至2027年6月（除實習單元外，上課時間暫定為星期二及四晚上）
截止報名日期
2026年9月21日（星期一）
請於網上填寫及提交申請表格：
https://hkier.cuhk.edu.hk/programmes/csa
課程查詢
香港中文大學香港教育研究所
地址：香港新界沙田香港中文大學何添樓204室
電話：3943 6999
傳真：2603 6850
電郵：
hkier-training@cuhk.edu.hk
****Professional Certificate Programme in Management of Student Activities in Primary and Secondary Schools 2026-2027****
The Faculty of Education and the Hong Kong Institute of Educational Research (HKIER) of the Chinese University of Hong Kong, and the Hong Kong Extra-curricular Activities Masters’ Association collaborate in offering the one-year Professional Certificate Programme in Management of Student Activities in Primary and Secondary Schools in the 2026–2027 academic year. This programme is designed to respond to the development of student activities and to accommodate the needs of professional training of educators.
Target Participants
Serving teachers in primary or secondary schools who are responsible for or involved in organizing and managing student activities, and holders of teacher qualification and a Bachelor's degree from a recognized university.
Curriculum
The curriculum consists of four compulsory modules and one elective module, a total of 126 hours.
Study Period
November 2026 to June 2027 (mainly on Tuesday and Thursday)
Application Deadline
21 September 2026
Please submit your application online:
https://hkier.cuhk.edu.hk/programmes/csa
Enquiries
Hong Kong Institute of Educational Research, CUHK
Address: Room 204, Ho Tim Building, The Chinese University of Hong Kong, Shatin, N.T., Hong Kong
Tel: 3943 6999
Fax: 2603 6850
Email:

2. be passionate about arts and culture, curious about museums, and eager to explore the connections between artifacts and everyday life.
3. attend the interview-cum-briefing session (details in the application form).

【Public Health and Health Service Research】 Student Helper Recruitment | Literature Review, Data Extraction and Fieldwork  - JC School of Public Health and Primary Care
From: Ng Sammi
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
samming001@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
The
JC School of Public Health and Primary Care, CUHK
is recruiting student helpers to support several research projects about health promotion, evidence-based medicine, and Chinese medicine, led by Prof. Martin Chi-sang WONG, Prof. Jason Junjie HUANG, Prof. Claire Chenwen ZHONG.
The main responsibilities may include, but are not limited to:
Data extraction and data entry
Literature review and article screening
Fieldwork and survey data collection
Interview transcription and data management
Other research-related and administrative duties as assigned
This position provides an excellent opportunity for students who are interested in gaining hands-on experience in public health and health services research.
Requirements:
Training will be provided. Students should be responsible, detail-oriented, and committed to completing assigned tasks reliably and on time.
Good communication and organizational skills
Proficiency in English and Chinese
Prefer BSc Public Health, Community Health, & Chinese Medicine, and students from the Faculty of Medicine.
Working arrangements:
Flexible working schedule (We do not have a specific reporting schedule for students. We will reach out personally to coordinate the working schedule)
On-site work (work from home can be arranged depending on project needs)
Training will be provided
Expected Working Period: August 2026 to 2027
Salary (in hourly rate): 64
Application deadline
: Recruit on an ongoing basis
If you are interested, please send your
CV
,
academic programme/year of study
, and
weekly availability
to
samming001@cuhk.edu.hk
. Should you have any questions regarding the position, please feel free to contact us at the same email address.

The
JC School of Public Health and Primary Care, CUHK
is recruiting student helpers to support several research projects about health promotion, evidence-based medicine, and Chinese medicine, led by Prof. Martin Chi-sang WONG, Prof. Jason Junjie HUANG, Prof. Claire Chenwen ZHONG.
The main responsibilities may include, but are not limited to:
Data extraction and data entry
Literature review and article screening
Fieldwork and survey data collection
Interview transcription and data management
Other research-related and administrative duties as assigned
This position provides an excellent opportunity for students who are interested in gaining hands-on experience in public health and health services research.
Requirements:
Training will be provided. Students should be responsible, detail-oriented, and committed to completing assigned tasks reliably and on time.
Good communication and organizational skills
Proficiency in English and Chinese
Prefer BSc Public Health, Community Health, & Chinese Medicine, and students from the Faculty of Medicine.
Working arrangements:
Flexible working schedule (We do not have a specific reporting schedule for students. We will reach out personally to coordinate the working schedule)
On-site work (work from home can be arranged depending on project needs)
Training will be provided
Expected Working Period: August 2026 to 2027
Salary (in hourly rate): 64
Application deadline
: Recruit on an ongoing basis
